headline: Centre to launch fifth edition of Nayi Chetna gender campaign on Nov 25
content: New Delhi, The Centre will launch the fifth edition of its national gender campaign, 'Nayi Chetna, Pahal Badlav Ki', on November 25, with a focus on strengthening women's economic empowerment, access to assets, safe mobility and equal opportunities, an official statement said.The month-long campaign, spearheaded by the Ministry of Rural Development under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission , will run from November 25 to December 23 across the country.Union Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will inaugurate the campaign in the presence of Women and Child Development Minister Annpurna Devi and Minister of State for Rural Development Kamlesh Paswan.The fifth edition, themed "From Access to Agency: Empowering Women through Livelihoods and Equal Opportunities for a Viksit Bharat", seeks to move beyond awareness generation towards coordinated action to improve women's economic participation, independence and decision-making, the Rural Development Ministry said.It will focus on recognising women as economic contributors, strengthening their access to and control over assets, promoting safe mobility and ensuring a more equitable distribution of unpaid care work.The campaign will also seek to address barriers restricting women's access to livelihood opportunities, markets, financial services, public spaces and essential services.A key highlight of the launch will be the release of a joint inter-ministerial advisory involving 15 ministries and departments to promote coordinated action on the campaign's objectives.The advisory will provide a framework for aligning government schemes, programmes and institutional mechanisms to improve women's access to livelihoods, assets, financial services, safe mobility and support systems at the national, state, district and community levels.A quadripartite memorandum of understanding among the Ministries of Rural Development and Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the National Legal Services Authority will also be released.The agreement seeks to strengthen institutional coordination for preventing and responding to gender-based violence at the community level, including through greater awareness of legal rights, access to justice and support mechanisms.Community institutions set up under DAY-NRLM, including Self-Help Groups , Village Organisations, Cluster Level Federations and Gender Resource Centres, will play a central role in implementing the campaign.New Gender Resource Centres will be inaugurated as community-level platforms to facilitate women's access to services, entitlements, support systems and grievance redressal mechanisms.The Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report, documenting the findings and learnings from the previous edition, will also be released. State-level videos showcasing good practices and community-led initiatives, along with campaign video resources, will be unveiled.Launched in 2022, Nayi Chetna has evolved into a nationwide campaign to address gender-based violence, challenge discriminatory social norms and promote gender equality.The fifth edition will also seek to involve men, boys and young people in challenging discriminatory practices and promoting equality and shared responsibility.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Delhi Police considered reporter jackets, press IDs to distinguish journalists from ‘reel-makers’ during anti-SIR protests
content: NEW DELHI The Delhi Police had considered issuing high-visibility reporter vests carrying its name and separate identification cards to journalists covering the anti-SIR protests in the Capital in October, in an attempt to distinguish genuine mediapersons from those it described as ‘reel-makers’, senior police officers told The Hindu. The proposals, however, did not materialise, with officers concerned that the vests and identification cards could be easily replicated, potentially creating another layer of confusion during an already tense law-and-order situation. Why dismiss ‘reel-makers’ when police rely on reels: women media professionals ask in Supreme Court Why dismiss ‘reel-makers’ when police rely on reels: women media professionals ask in Supreme Court Network of Women in Media, India says journalists’ entitlement to undertake lawful newsgathering from public places cannot be made contingent upon State accreditation; Article 19(1)(a) is not confined to material which the police chooses to recognise as ‘news’, it says Why dismiss ‘reel-makers’ when police rely on reels: women media professionals ask in Supreme Court storyline 1 In conversations with The Hindu, at least four senior Delhi Police officers, who spoke on condition of anonymity, acknowledged that distinguishing journalists from social media content creators and protesters posing as mediapersons had been a challenge during the demonstrations. They cited the circulation of fake press identification cards, the absence of a clear mechanism to authenticate journalists and instances of protesters claiming to be independent journalists to avoid detention. “We are not against journalists covering the protests. But the lack of clarity over who qualified as a journalist, and the large number of people carrying cameras and microphones, complicated the task of managing crowds and ensuring the safety of mediapersons,” an officer said. The confusion on the ground subsequently found its way into the police’s November 16 affidavit before the Supreme Court, in which it argued that social media content creators, ‘reel-makers’ and people carrying cameras or microphones could not automatically be considered bona fide journalists or claim the protections available to accredited mediapersons. It maintained that the Supreme Court’s directions against hindering journalists covering the anti-CEC protests did not extend to social media influencers, reel-makers or unruly elements violating the law. The argument drew criticism from independent journalists, several of whom said they had been reporting from the ground without institutional backing or formal accreditation. On November 21, the Network of Women in Media, India (NWMI), told the Supreme Court that lawful newsgathering could not be made conditional on State accreditation or formal employment with a media organisation. ‘We are journalists, not reel makers’: independent reporters hit back at Delhi Police’s affidavit to Supreme Court ‘We are journalists, not reel makers’: independent reporters hit back at Delhi Police’s affidavit to Supreme Court As Delhi Police tells Supreme Court that social media content creators and reel-makers cannot be equated with bona fide journalists, independent reporters who covered the anti-SIR protests say the argument dismisses ground reportage, undermines digital journalism and overlooks the work of those who documented police action. ‘We are journalists, not reel makers’: independent reporters hit back at Delhi Police’s affidavit to Supreme Court storyline 1 However, police officers who spoke to The Hindu said they initially relied on press ID cards to verify journalists. But the circulation of cards with unverifiable credentials soon made the process difficult. “Some individuals were carrying press cards issued by a website called Indian Press Union. We did not know whether it was a statutory body authorised to issue such identification cards. We asked journalists about it, and even they were unable to give us a clear answer. So, how were we supposed to establish which card was genuine?” an officer said. The officer said that even attempts to find a definitive answer through official sources had yielded little clarity. “ We want to understand from the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting what parameters could be used to distinguish journalists from those who were not engaged in journalism, the officer said. The possibility of introducing more secure identification cards, with features such as holograms or security threads similar to those on currency notes, was also discussed. Such features, officers said, could help personnel verify whether an individual belonged to an authenticated category of journalists. Youth Congress workers detained over protest against Meta for blocking social media accounts Youth Congress workers detained over protest against Meta for blocking social media accounts The IYC workers staged a demonstration against Meta in Hyderabad over alleged blocking of social media accounts. Over 21 protesters were released following a three-hour detention by police Youth Congress workers detained over protest against Meta for blocking social media accounts storyline 1 Drawing a comparison, an officer said the police issued signed slips to people from outside the force who were required to work alongside personnel, asking them to display the authorisation on their shirts. In the absence of a common verification mechanism, the guidelines issued during the protests had, in effect, become the immediate reference point for personnel on the ground, another senior officer said. “The distinction was often made on the basis of the conduct of a person at the spot. Were they part of the crowd, were they raising slogans, or were they maintaining a distance and reporting? These were among the things personnel had to look at,” the officer said. “While several journalists were standing on the pavements and reporting from a safe distance, some individuals would breach the police cordons to get close-up footage. They would come in between personnel and those being detained. This made an already difficult situation more complicated, and in many cases genuine journalists were also detained due to misjudgment,” the officer added. Police officers also cited instances in which protesters allegedly claimed to be independent journalists to avoid detention, but were subsequently seen raising slogans and joining the demonstrations. The officers also called for some form of regulation, whether through self-regulation or otherwise, to bring greater clarity to who could claim to be a journalist and establish a mechanism for the future.

headline: Karnataka makes free sanitary napkins mandatory in schools, warns of action for lapses
content: Girls in Classes 6 to 12 across Karnataka will get free sanitary napkins in government, aided and private schools, with the state government making it mandatory for institutions to ensure their availability and warning of disciplinary action against those that fail to comply.A circular issued by the School Education Department directs all schools and pre-university colleges to provide biodegradable sanitary napkins meeting prescribed standards, free of cost. Schools must make the products easily accessible, preferably by installing vending machines in girls’ toilets. Where machines cannot be installed immediately, institutions must arrange distribution through a designated location or an assigned official.“All government, aided and private schools and pre-university colleges in the state are hereby instructed to implement the directions contained in the aforementioned Supreme Court judgment compulsorily, promptly and without any lapses,” the circular says.“Failure to comply will invite disciplinary action, as per the rules, against the head teachers of the concerned government schools and the managements of private schools,” it added.Schools have three months to establish menstrual hygiene management corners, stocked with spare undergarments, uniforms and disposable bags. These facilities are intended to help students manage unexpected menstruation and other hygiene requirements during school hours.The circular also mentions separate toilets for boys and girls, functional water connections and handwashing facilities. Every toilet unit must have a covered bin for collecting sanitary waste, which schools must ensure is disposed of safely.District education officers must inspect schools annually to assess infrastructure, toilet facilities, the availability of sanitary napkins, general hygiene, waste disposal arrangements and menstrual health awareness programmes, the circular said, adding that the officers must also obtain anonymous feedback from students.Responsibility for implementation has been assigned according to the type of institution. In government schools, head teachers must ensure the availability of toilets, washing facilities and sanitary napkins. For aided and unaided schools, the circular links compliance to Section 18 of the Right to Education Act and Rule 16 of the RTE Rules. Inspection findings and consolidated student feedback must be attached to notices issued under the relevant provisions.The department has also called for male and female teachers to be sensitised about menstrual health. The State Council of Educational Research and Training and the National Council of Educational Research and Training have been asked to develop learning materials covering menstruation, adolescence and associated health conditions, including polycystic ovary syndrome and polycystic ovarian disease.

headline: ‘Stop acting like Baahubali,’ says Supreme Court to Bihar judicial officer for FIR against Superintendent of Police
content: New Delhi "Stop acting like a Baahubali", the Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) remarked while slamming a Bihar judicial officer who convicted a Superintendent of Police (SP) for disobeying directions to register an FIR and fined him. A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana questioned Bihar Judge Anil Kumar's conduct and said his understanding of law is appalling. "We are really surprised at your understanding of law. You must first understand the scope and ambit of Section 384 BNSS and Section 345 CrPC. If someone slaps someone or abuses the court, or refuses to leave the courtroom when directed, that is an offence committed in the face of the court. But if we direct someone to register an FIR and they do not, it does not amount to a crime committed in the face of the court. "Your understanding of law is appalling. You also took such an aggressive stance, called the superintendent and convicted him on the same day," Justice Bagchi remarked orally. Questioning the Judge's objection to an inspecting Judge's intervention, Justice Bagchi said, "Were you within your domain and jurisdiction when you called the District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police, treated their non-appearance as an offence committed in the face of the court and convicted and sentenced him? You also stay your hands. Enough of adventure." The SC said the judicial officer should be sent to the National Judicial Academy for training. "Ask your client to stop acting like a 'Bahubali' while exercising judicial powers," the CJI said orally while hearing a plea filed by the judicial officer against the Patna HC order staying his order. The District and Additional Sessions Judge-IV, Rohtas at Sasaram convicted IPS officer Raushan Kumar—then SP Rohtas—on September 29, 2026, for wilfully disobeying court orders and imposed a symbolic fine of ₹1. He directed the Director General of Police (DGP), Bihar, to enter the court's observations into the officer's service records and called on the Union Ministry of Personnel and Training to overhaul training for IAS and IPS officers to align better with a democratic setup. The Patna High Court had earlier stayed an order imposing a ₹1 fine on the SP for contempt of court while he was posted in Rohtas. On September 29, an additional sessions judge in Sasaram held the officer guilty of disobeying an order to register an FIR against a person who had given false evidence in a criminal case decided in 2023.

headline: FSSAI suspends licences of 5 more nutraceutical makers over hygiene, infrastructure violations
content: NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) on Monday announced the suspension of licences of five nutraceutical and health product manufacturers for serious violations.In a social media post, the food regulator said it had suspended the licences of Vedant Remedies, Lucid Healthcare Pvt Ltd, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare, Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals and Adorreal Healthcare over various violations, including poor hygiene and damaged infrastructure."FSSAI has suspended the license of several nutraceutical and health product manufacturers for serious food safety and regulatory violations," the regulator said.FSSAI said it remained committed to protecting public health through strict vigilance and enforcement of food safety standards.Earlier this month, the regulator had taken action against six nutraceutical manufacturers over various violations."Regulatory action initiated, including suspension of FSSAI licenses for serious food safety violations," it had said.The six companies facing action were Airen Herbals, Aquabliss Lifesciences, Raskam Healthcare, Supercure Biotech, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare and Vedant Remedies.During the current calendar year, FSSAI has stepped up enforcement action against food business operators (FBOs) and e-commerce companies as part of its efforts to ensure safe food for consumers. headline: ASEAN-India Maritime Conclave in Visakhapatnam calls for deeper cooperation to secure Indo-Pacific trade routes
content: VISAKHAPATNAM Policymakers, diplomats and naval officials called for deeper regional cooperation to safeguard Indo-Pacific trade routes, address geopolitical uncertainties and build a resilient blue economy as the two-day ASEAN-India Maritime Conclave commenced on Monday (November 23, 2026) in Visakhapatnam. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Visakhapatnam/ Organised by the India Foundation in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the conclave brought together Union Minister of State for External Affairs Pabitra Margherita, Andhra Pradesh Minister for Human Resources Development, IT and Electronics Nara Lokesh, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, former Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Dinesh Kumar Tripathi, India Foundation President Ram Madhav and ambassadors and strategic thinkers from ASEAN member states. Addressing the inaugural session, Mr. Margherita said that ASEAN-India synergy was central to India’s Indo-Pacific vision and Act East Policy, adding that stronger maritime connectivity, disaster management and sustainable blue economy partnerships were vital as both sides marked the Year of ASEAN-India Maritime Cooperation. Admiral Swaminathan cautioned that geopolitical shifts, climate change, and extreme weather events were creating uncertainty across the Indo-Pacific’s 12 million square kilometres of exclusive economic zones, where security is tested daily by maritime terrorism, cyber threats, theft, and trespassing—challenges that require shared regional responsibility to ensure secure sea lanes. Mr. Lokesh pitched Andhra Pradesh’s 1,053-km coastline—backed by four upcoming ports, a proposed ₹30,000-crore shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam, subsea cable landing infrastructure, and green ammonia exports—as an industrial and digital gateway for ASEAN supply chains. Meanwhile, Mr. Madhav said that Visakhapatnam was among the country’s foremost maritime stations, adding that the conclave would deliberate on recent shipping disruptions and channel closures to revitalise Indo-Pacific commerce. Over two days, delegates and maritime experts will discuss port modernisation, maritime domain awareness, coastal resilience and institutional frameworks to turn diplomatic convergence into regional partnerships. Port and digital push Mr. Lokesh said Andhra Pradesh was committed to forging lasting maritime partnerships with Southeast Asian nations in connectivity, digital technology, clean energy and skill development. He pointed to Visakhapatnam Port’s record handling of 91.17 million tonnes of cargo in the previous financial year, and to port-led MoUs worth ₹7,500 crore signed in the city for port expansion, logistics, specialised terminals and ship repair. Visakhapatnam was evolving into a hub for international subsea cables, data centres and artificial intelligence, he said, urging ASEAN delegates to turn their shared maritime heritage into economic collaboration and make the Bay of Bengal a corridor of regional growth.

headline: Hyderabad bomb threat email sender used Europe-based VPN, temporary email account
content: HYDERABAD The sender of the bomb threat email, received by Hyderabad Police, reportedly used a Europe-based Virtual Private Network (VPN) and a temporary email account to conceal their identity, making it difficult for investigators to trace the origin of the message. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/hyderabad-police-issue-alert-over-terror-threat-email-security-checks-conducted-at-key-locations/article71731583.ece The cybercrime teams are working to identify the sender by analysing the digital trail left behind by the email, which threatened 26/11-style attacks in the city and named Kacheguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza as potential targets. The email, received on Saturday (November 21, 2026), reportedly claimed that the attacks would be carried out in retaliation for the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba operative Lateef Bhat in Jammu and Kashmir. It threatened to kill at least 300 people. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/jammu-and-kashmir/let-lateef-bhat-killed-in-kulgam-encounter/article71715240.ece The police have intensified security at the locations mentioned in the email and other crowded public places, including railway stations, hotels, bus terminals and religious places. Bomb detection squads and sniffer dog teams conducted anti-sabotage checks, but no explosives were found. The investigators are examining the email and associated digital information to establish the sender’s identity and verify the authenticity of the threat. The use of a VPN and a temporary email account has complicated the tracing process, with teams working to establish the origin of the message. Dial 112 to report suspicious persons or unattended objects The police have appealed to citizens not to panic or circulate unverified information and asked them to report suspicious persons or unattended objects by dialling 112.

headline: Government’s anti-cybercrime wing has ‘WhatsApp Web’ warning for you
content: The government’s anti-cybercrime wing has issued a warning for those who use WhatsApp Web. In a new security advisory issued on Monday (November 23), the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) cautioned that active, authenticated WhatsApp Web sessions can be exploited for unauthorised access by hackers by leaving an open door to hijack your account, read private chats and impersonate you to carry out fraud,Once inside, bad actors can read personal messages, view contact lists and group chats, and send messages pretending to be the account owner, leveraging the victim's trusted identity to launch fraud, phishing, and social-engineering scams, the warning explained as per PTI.‘Closing the browser tab is not enough’The I4C specifically stressed that simply closing a browser window or tab does not end a WhatsApp Web session. Users must manually log out every time they finish using the platform on a computer.“Users are therefore advised to exercise caution while using WhatsApp Web, particularly on office computers, shared systems, public computers or devices that may be accessible to other persons," the advisory stated, further warning, “Avoid official or sensitive work on WhatsApp Web. Government, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information should preferably not be exchanged through WhatsApp Web sessions on computers.”Key safety tips from advisoryTo protect accounts from unauthorised takeovers, the I4C recommended the following precautions:Avoid logging into WhatsApp Web on cyber cafe computers, public kiosks, hotel business centers, borrowed laptops or other unknown and public devices.If logging in on a shared system is unavoidable, use the browser’s incognito or private browsing mode but remember to log out manually afterward.Pay close attention to unusual account behaviour, such as unexpected messages sent from your number, strange replies from contacts or any unexplained activity.Keep your devices, operating systems, browsers and security software updated, and steer clear of suspicious downloads, unknown files and cracked software.Fearless legend or grounded realist? headline: Karnataka Congress MLAs oppose elephant relocation; Motamma submits resignation
content: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma on Monday resigned from the Karnataka assembly in protest against the Forest Department’s operation to drive wild elephants from Belur in Hassan district towards Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary in Chikkamagaluru. Her resignation came a day after she, along with two other Congress MLAs, threatened to quit if the operation was not stopped.Motamma, who represents Mudigere, submitted her resignation at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru and left without speaking to reporters.Her resignation escalates the opposition by three Congress MLAs from Chikkamagaluru to the operation. Motamma, Sringeri MLA TD Rajegowda and Chikkamagaluru MLA HD Thammaiah have argued that bringing elephants from Hassan would worsen human-elephant conflict in their constituencies.At a joint press conference on Sunday, Motamma showed her resignation letter and said she would submit it on Monday if the elephants were not sent back. She also alleged that forest officials had proceeded with the operation without consulting legislators from the affected constituencies, despite their objections.Rajegowda said people in his constituency had died in elephant attacks over the past 18 months and that bringing more animals into the region would increase the threat. He said more than 450 elephants were already present in the Muthodi forest range.“We will never allow these elephants into Bhadra. If the government goes ahead forcibly, we are ready to make any sacrifice,” he said, suggesting that the animals be moved to other reserves, including Bandipur, Nagarahole, Sathyamangalam and Biligiriranganabetta.Thammaiah said Chikkamagaluru district had faced severe human-elephant conflict for five years. He questioned why forest officials had begun driving the animals towards Bhadra without consulting elected representatives.“At a Karnataka Development Programme meeting chaired by the district in-charge minister, we had demanded that elephants in the district be shifted to the Bhadra project, but officials rejected the demand, saying it would violate a Supreme Court order. Now, the officials are preparing to drive these elephants into the tiger reserve,” he said.Responding to the legislators’ opposition on Monday, forest, environment and ecology minister Ramalinga Reddy said the government would consider their recommendations on where the elephants should be relocated.“Let the MLAs suggest where the elephants should be moved. We will take action accordingly,” he said in Kolar.Reddy said Belur had about 55 elephants but only 13,917 acres of forest, much of it fragmented by coffee plantations and villages. The elephant population had increased from seven in 2019 to about 55, resulting in crop damage and attacks on people, he said.In comparison, Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary has about 141,000 acres of forest, with its buffer zone taking the total area to approximately 262,000 acres, he said. However, the government would have to ensure that relocation did not create problems for people in the receiving district.The controversy follows two fatal elephant attacks in Belur on November 14 and 16. The Forest Department subsequently launched Operation Gaja to capture and relocate elephants considered responsible for the attacks. An order issued by the principal chief conservator of forests (Wildlife) authorised the capture of a maximum of 10 elephants.Two tuskers have already been relocated. A 35-year-old elephant was taken to the Mathigodu elephant camp in Nagarahole Tiger Reserve, while a 15-year-old was released in Bandipur Tiger Reserve after being fitted with a radio collar.Separately, forest personnel began driving herds towards Bhadra as part of a larger proposal involving 56 elephants. By Sunday, a herd of more than 38 animals, including four tuskers and several calves, had crossed into Chikkamagaluru district and reached Karabailu village in Mudigere taluk.Hassan district in-charge minister KM Shivalingegowda defended the operation, saying Belur did not have sufficient forest cover to sustain its elephant population.“There is hardly any forest area in Belur, not even 100 acres. How can elephants survive there? I request everyone to cooperate and not obstruct the operation. We are sending the elephants back to the forest, not targeting any particular district,” he said.

headline: Ecostani: No climate deal at Antalya will not derail renewable transition
content: It is not the first time that the Conference of the Parties (COP) has failed to reach an agreement over a climate change action plan. In 2009, the COP at Copenhagen failed to reach an agreement. Yet six years later, the historic Paris Agreement was approved, having something for every nation.COP31, held in Antalya and jointly hosted by Türkiye and Australia, both major fossil fuel consumers, failed to reach an agreement even after three drafts were circulated on Sunday afternoon. The issues of contention were the timeframe for phasing out fossil fuels and the provision of adequate climate finance for developing and emerging economies to deal with the impact of the transition — issues that are not new in climate negotiations.Unlike in the past, the island nations, backed by the European Union and the UK, were not willing to accept any nuance on phasing out of fossil fuels, whereas a small group of oil-producing countries led by Saudi Arabia did not agree to a specific timeframe. Hence, the stalemate. India and China, the world’s two largest fossil fuel consumers, were also not willing to accept the European proposal and were seeking a firm commitment on climate finance, which developed countries were hesitant to provide. India, on behalf of the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), spoke about the need to continue using fossil fuels, citing its social security and development needs. COP agreements are reached by consensus, not by majority vote. Although Antalya was a repeat of 2009, there are many differences between the two.In 2009, the renewable energy journey was just starting to have an impact on economies, with a major push from the European Union and then US president Barack Obama. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), renewable energy accounted for just 18.29% of the total global energy mix in 2009, with Europe dominating the space.By 2025, the contribution of renewables had reached almost 34% and is projected to touch 45% by 2031. While around 130 countries had invested in renewables in 2009, nearly 200 countries now have renewable energy capacity.In 2009, the penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) in the global vehicle market was just 0.1%, with around 6,000 EVs sold that year. In 2025, around 26-28% of the vehicles sold across the world were EVs, a huge leap for the technology, which was considered nascent in 2009.According to the IEA, the growth of EVs has slowed the growth in demand for fossil fuels by eight percentage points. Similarly, the installation of solar power capacity has significantly displaced demand for natural gas, another fossil fuel.The IEA has projected that global renewable capacity will grow by almost 4,800 gigawatts (GW) between 2026 and 2031, 57% more than in the previous six years. During this period, India would become the world’s second-largest growth market after China, the IEA said in its outlook released in November.The IEA also pointed out that higher oil prices and energy security concerns amid the Middle East crisis have led to a higher forecast for growth in liquid biofuel production, up by 40% compared with last year’s report. Many countries — especially in Southeast Asia and Latin America — are accelerating the implementation of new and previously announced liquid biofuel mandates to reduce their reliance on imported fossil fuels.The data clearly shows that the world, pushed by the 2015 Paris climate agreement, has been steadily moving towards a green economy, even though China’s slowdown in solar capacity additions has impacted the transition in the last two years.From the beginning, it appeared that Antalya would not deliver a major climate statement. Not a single head of state from a major economy participated. Environment ministers of the host countries, Türkiye and Australia, were not seen making efforts to build global consensus on an agreement at the conference, and there was no media brouhaha over the conference. To me, it was the dullest COP since the 2015 Paris summit.Not having a deal in Antalya, Türkiye, will not derail the transition but will send a political message about the deepening global divide. In the past, COPs have delivered weak agreements or statements aimed at conveying a message of face-saving global unity in the effort to tackle climate change.To me, global climate negotiators are waiting for the United States elections in November 2028, a few days before that year’s COP, to push the climate agenda. No climate deal can succeed without the world’s biggest polluter, the United States, being on board.

headline: AASU marks 60th Constitution anniversary, raises education, identity concerns
content: Guwahati, Nov 23: The All Assam Students’ Union (AASU) on Monday used its Constitution Day programme to underline concerns over Assam’s education system, declining use of Assamese, protection of indigenous identity and the organisation’s future course, while reaffirming its regionalist and progressive outlook.More than 1,000 AASU representatives from different parts of Assam attended the Central Representatives’ Convention at Arjun Bhogeswar Baruah Stadium in Guwahati’s Sarusajai. The convention, held for the first time in an open public setting, marked the 60th anniversary of the organisation’s Constitution.AASU chief adviser Samujjal Bhattacharya said the programme was originally been planned for August but was postponed because of floods in Upper Assam. “Celebrations would be held throughout the year from the grassroots to the state level. The organisation would seek the people’s blessings as it worked for students’ future and the protection of indigenous people,” he said, addressing the gathering.AASU president Utpal Sarma paid tribute to the organisation’s martyrs and former members, saying their contributions have earned AASU the people’s affection. “The convention would discuss the organisation’s future course and challenges,” he said, pointing to what he described as a rise in “conspiracies” against AASU.Sarma said AASU remains committed to a regionalist and progressive ideology and owes allegiance to no political party. On the Citizenship Amendment Act, Sarma said AASU’s legal battle is continuing in the Supreme Court. He also called for re-verification of the National Register of Citizens and a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls to remove illegal immigrants from Bangladesh from voter lists, while maintaining that constitutional safeguards for Assam remained under discussion.The event also saw the unveiling of AASU’s new logo by Dibrugarh University vice-chancellor Dr Jiten Hazarika and Nagaon University vice-chancellor Dr Hitesh Deka. The logo will feature on AASU banners and programmes over the next year.Deka raised concerns over the state of educational institutions, saying institutions built by people had, over the past decade, begun their journey towards becoming “cremation grounds”. He questioned the government’s commitment to improving such institutions and urged AASU and regional student bodies to protect them. He also called for libraries to be established in villages and expressed concern over the declining desire among people to study in rural areas.Deka also flagged the declining use of Assamese and warned that merely “declaring Assamese as a classical language would not protect it”. Hazarika, a former AASU leader, called for a study into the weaknesses of students and greater efforts to preserve Assam’s heritage. While describing the National Education Policy as good, he said changes might be required to suit Assam’s needs. He also advocated workshops to help Assamese-medium students speak English and Hindi while preserving their mother tongue.

headline: ‘Appropriate reply at right time’: Naveen Patnaik on foreign visits probe
content: Biju Janata Dal (BJD) leader Naveen Patnaik on Monday rejected allegations of irregularities in his foreign visits, saying he travelled abroad as the chief minister in Odisha’s interest. Patnaik described the allegations as false two days after the state government ordered a probe into his overseas trips,“I had very limited travel abroad and only to deal with Odisha’s subjects and very important subjects. I understand some false allegations have been made about my travels and that of my officers. An appropriate reply will be given,” he said.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi ordered the inquiry into the foreign visits of Patnaik, former bureaucrat VK Pandian and Indian Police Service officer Ravi Kant in 2022-23 and 2023-24.SK Vashishth, principal secretary in the general administration department, will conduct the inquiry following allegations that records relating to the trips were incomplete and prescribed procedures may have been violated. Officials said the probe would seek to determine whether any illegality was committed and whether legal action was warranted.In June 2022, Patnaik visited Italy and Dubai, where he attended a World Food Programme event, met Pope Francis at the Vatican and participated in an investors’ meet. Patnaik’s first ever trip abroad after becoming chief minister was in 2012 when he visited the UK. He met with the UK’s international development secretary Andrew Mitchel to discuss welfare and anti-poverty schemes in Odisha.In April 2023, he led a business delegation to Japan and Singapore to attract investments. Pandian, then his private secretary, and IPS officer Ravi Kant accompanied him.Activists, citing information obtained under the Right to Information Act, questioned the expenditure details of the visits, particularly those to Italy and Japan. The BJD has dismissed the allegations as politically motivated. It cited deputy chief minister Pravati Parida’s seven-day visit to London from November 2 to 9 in 2024 to promote tourism and attract investment.The BJD demanded that the government disclose what tangible benefits Odisha’s tourism sector derived from the trip. It alleged that her entourage included non-official members. “The deputy chief minister is now on a visit to Indonesia and Bali with a large entourage while the winter session of the assembly is on. The BJD will raise this in the House, along with the foreign visits of other ministers and officials,” said BJD spokesperson Lenin Mohanty.

headline: Oppn mount pressure on TVK govt over Cauvery delta crop loss
content: Chennai, Opposition parties in Tamil Nadu on Monday mounted pressure on the ruling TVK over agrarian distress in the Cauvery delta districts, with DMK president M K Stalin announcing a party consultation panel to hear farmers' grievances and AMMK general secretary T T V Dhinakaran demanding that the region be declared drought-hit.In separate social media statements, both the leaders accused Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's administration of "ignoring the plight" of delta cultivators facing severe water scarcity.Announcing that the DMK will deploy a "Cauvery Farmers' Consultation Committee" across the delta districts starting November 25, Stalin alleged that the government had turned a "blind eye to farmers in tears"."The DMK will not remain silent even if the government chooses to abandon them," the former CM said, urging farmers to come forward with confidence so the party could take their demands to the administration and fight for justice.Dhinakaran called upon the chief minister to officially declare the delta districts drought-affected and disburse immediate compensation to affected growers.Pointing out that Samba paddy cultivated across nearly seven lakh acres was withering, he said farmers had been reduced to carrying stagnant pond water in pots to save parched crops, while dried fields had turned into grazing grounds for cattle.The AMMK chief accused the state government of being a "mute spectator" to the plight of farmers, alleging that it had neither secured Tamil Nadu's rightful share of Cauvery water from Karnataka nor stepped in to alleviate agrarian distress.Also, he flagged unannounced power cuts, fertiliser shortages, and unfulfilled crop loan waiver promises.Dhinakaran further criticised officials for allegedly advising distressed farmers to use sprays and tonics on water-starved crops, saying it was tantamount to asking them to quit farming.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 'Implement SC verdict': Annamalai slams TVK's review plea over lighting of Karthigai Deepam
content: Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai on Monday urged the Tamil Nadu government to implement the Supreme Court's order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at Thiruparankundram Hill, questioning the state's decision to file a review petition against the verdict.Reacting to the state government's review petition, Annamalai said the government should follow the Supreme Court's November 20 order and ensure that the lamp is lit at the designated spot on November 24."Tomorrow, if TVK does not let the lamp be lit in Thiruparankundram, then it will be against the Supreme Court verdict. We, the leaders, ask the TVK government to implement the Supreme Court verdict. State officials should go and light the lamp tomorrow in Thiruparankundram," he said. Annamalai also questioned the state government's decision to approach the Supreme Court again, saying the November 20 order had addressed the law-and-order concerns."We all have doubts that the TVK government, without clarity on the Supreme Court verdict, has approached the court again. The Supreme Court has given a verdict that states and cites law and order too," he said.Also read: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay's London trip faces fresh attack as Annamalai takes 'dead economy' jibeHe further alleged that the previous DMK government had prevented the lighting of the lamp at Thiruparankundram and recalled that the party had earlier taken steps against the judge who ruled in favour of the ritual."The DMK government didn't let the lamp be lit in Thiruparankundram. On November 20, an SC verdict came in which the judges allowed lighting the lamp in Thiruparankundram temporarily on Karthigai Deepam day, ordered the Madurai Collector to do it and asked to deploy CISF if needed. Today, the TVK government has filed a review petition in the Supreme Court," Annamalai added.The dispute concerns the annual lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill near the Sikandar Badhusha Dargah in Madurai.Also read: 'No need to display religion': Ex-BJP leader Annamalai on being a 'true Hindu' in fiery speechThe controversy began in November 2025, when local authorities withheld permission for the hilltop ritual, citing law-and-order concerns and the site's proximity to the dargah.In December 2025, a single judge of the Madras High Court directed the temple authorities to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, observing that the pillar was situated more than 50 metres from the dargah.A division bench upheld the direction on January 6, 2026, while requiring the temple administration to coordinate the ritual with the police and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), considering the site's heritage status.The Tamil Nadu government subsequently challenged the High Court's decisions before the Supreme Court, which issued notice on the state's plea in August 2026.On November 20, a Supreme Court bench led by Justice Aravind Kumar permitted a strictly conditional, one-time lighting of the lamp on November 24. The order did not establish a legal precedent or settle the broader claims relating to ownership and customary rights.The Tamil Nadu government has since filed a review petition seeking an immediate stay on the Supreme Court's order.

headline: New GDP, CPI and IIP series to help make better-calibrated policy decisions, says RBI's Poonam Gupta
content: MUMBAI: Revised measures of India’s economic growth, inflation and industrial output will give the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) a clearer picture of the economy, helping it make better-calibrated monetary policy decisions, RBI deputy governor Poonam Gupta said on Monday.The methodological improvements in the new GDP, Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) series are expected to make early estimates more stable and reduce subsequent revisions, allowing for more predictable policy decisions, Gupta said at a Data Users Conference on the revised series organized by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in Mumbai.“Monetary policy decisions are based on an assessment of current conditions as well as on projections. Early estimates, which draw on proxy indicators and provisional information, are therefore an important input into monetary policy,” she said.“The methodological improvements in the new series are expected to yield estimates that are more stable across successive vintages, with smaller revisions, which in turn supports better-calibrated and more stable policy.”The revised CPI series, with a base year of 2024-25, was introduced on 12 February 2026, followed by the new GDP series, with a base year of 2022-23, on 27 February. The new IIP series, also with a base year of 2022-23, was released on 1 June. It was subsequently updated to incorporate the Output Producer Price Index (PPI) as a deflator, replacing the Wholesale Price Index (WPI).According to the latest data under the revised series, India’s real GDP grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter of fiscal year 2027 (FY27), while retail inflation stood at 6.09% in October, and industrial production expanded 6.7% in September.The next set of quarterly GDP estimates, for Q2FY27, is scheduled for release on 30 November.A new measureOn the changes to GDP measurement, Gupta said the new national accounts series adopts a more recent base year of 2022-23, replacing 2011-12. It introduces double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture and draws on a wider range of surveys and administrative data to improve the measurement of the informal economy.The revised estimates also use more recent Household Consumption Expenditure Survey data to determine private consumption shares. Measurement of gross fixed capital formation has been improved to identify the sector undertaking investments, allowing policymakers to assess not just the quantum of investment but also who is investing and in what.The new series also adopts the supply and use table framework to bring estimates from the production and expenditure sides closer together, addressing discrepancies that were large and volatile in the earlier series.On inflation measurement, Gupta highlighted the shift to the revised CPI series, which uses consumption expenditure data from the 2023-24 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey, replacing the 2011-12 survey. As a result, the weight of food and beverages has declined to 36.8% from 45.9%, while the share of non-food items has increased.“This should make headline inflation less volatile, and the monetary policy process less uncertain and easier to explain,” she said.Other changes to the CPI include the adoption of the UN's COICOP 2018 classification, exclusion of social transfers such as free public distribution system (PDS) items, inclusion of rural house rents and collection of prices from 12 online markets. Employer-provided and government accommodation have also been excluded from the housing index.The revised IIP, meanwhile, assigns higher weights to technology- and consumption-oriented sectors such as motor vehicles, pharmaceuticals and electronics, while lowering the weights of refined petroleum products, basic metals and mining.Gupta said the revised series would help policymakers better understand structural changes and cyclical trends in the economy. “The revised GDP, CPI and IIP series give us a clearer view of an economy that has changed considerably,” she said.

headline: 'We stand ready': China signals push to ease business visa process for Indians amid reported curbs
content: NEW DELHI: China on Monday said it was ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries, amid reports of a slowdown in visa issuance to Indian nationals."China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said in a written response to questions from news agency PTI."We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson added.The remarks come amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business travellers.According to PTI, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly granted visas to attend this month's China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair provides a platform for businesses from around the world to showcase their products to Chinese consumers.Beijing has also stopped the China Visa Application Centre, a service provider, from accepting visa applications, with Chinese diplomatic missions now handling them directly amid rising demand for visas, particularly business visas.Visa arrangements between the two countries have improved since India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years. The move was part of efforts to repair bilateral ties, which came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.The resumption of tourist visas was seen as a significant step towards normalising relations after years of strained ties.As part of efforts to ease travel, the two countries also resumed direct air connectivity between several cities, including the Beijing-New Delhi route.According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has come down to around seven per cent in recent months to encourage business and tourism-related travel to India.China, meanwhile, launched the "China Online Visa Application System" for Indian applicants in December last year, allowing them to apply for visas online.Responding to a question on the status of bilateral relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi in September this year, the spokesperson said Beijing was ready to work with New Delhi to strengthen ties."The most important common understanding they (PM Modi and Xi) reached is that China and India need to be partners. Both sides are working to deliver on this important common understanding."China stands ready to work with India to improve and grow bilateral relations, support each other's development and revitalisation, and contribute to world peace and prosperity," the spokesperson said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Assam college teachers’ ‘Pen Down’ stir puts UGC norms, service issues in focus
content: Guwahati, Nov 23: College teachers across Assam staged a statewide “Pen Down” strike, total non-cooperation and dharnas on Monday, pressing the government to act on a raft of long-pending demands, with a major gathering held at Chachal in Guwahati.Carrying placards and raising demands including a shift from the New Pension Scheme (NPS) to the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), reopening of the OM 2013 Portal and resolution of service-related issues, teachers across districts voiced their frustration over what the Assam College Teachers’ Association (ACTA) described as prolonged government inaction.“The agitation is a necessary last resort to secure justice, uphold the dignity of the teaching fraternity and safeguard Assam’s provincial higher education sector from systemic collapse,” the association said in a statement.At the Guwahati protest, teachers said they had waited for the government to address their concerns through dialogue, stressing that their demands were based on existing University Grants Commission (UGC) guidelines rather than any additional benefits.“We're not asking for any added perks, but what we deserve under the UGC guidelines. Since such protests hamper the educational curriculum of colleges, we waited and wanted to resolve the issues through dialogue with the government. But it's disheartening that we had to resort to protest to make our voices heard,” a protesting teacher said.ACTA said administrative delays, unresolved policy gaps and the non-implementation of mandatory UGC standards have hindered career progression and affected teacher morale in provincialised colleges across the state.A key demand is the reopening of the OM 2013 Portal to resolve pending service-condition issues in accordance with UGC regulations. The association has also sought the transition of faculty from NPS to OPS to ensure post-retirement financial security.The teachers’ body has demanded that past service be counted towards seniority and promotions and that Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) promotions be granted from the date of eligibility in line with UGC guidelines and timelines.ACTA has also sought immediate regularisation and upgradation of fixed-pay teachers, citing a decision taken at a meeting with the Assam Chief Minister on June 1, 2025.Other demands include the release of financial benefits to eligible CAS promotees, comprehensive leave rules for college teachers, payment of pending arrears and withheld MPhil/PhD advance increments, and resolution of promotional anomalies and administrative bottlenecks.The association has further demanded that the superannuation age of college teachers be raised to 65 years, mutual transfers be facilitated for teachers facing genuine difficulties and adequate teaching staff be recruited to fill departmental vacancies and maintain the UGC-mandated student-teacher ratio.ACTA leaders said they regretted the disruption to academic activities but maintained that the statewide agitation had become necessary to press for resolution of the long-pending issues.

headline: 'Disappearing Faces': Tamannaah Bhatia, Vishal Bhardwaj discuss Sadhguru's photo book on Himalayan communities
content: Actor Tamannaah Bhatia and filmmaker Vishal Bhardwaj joined spiritual leader Sadhguru for a discussion on his photo book Disappearing Faces at the Fairmont Hotel in Mumbai on November 22.The conversation covered ageing, individuality, education, devotion and the changing lifestyles of people living in remote Himalayan regions.The book brings together photographs taken by Sadhguru over five decades of journeys through the Himalayas, particularly Nepal and Tibet. The portraits document people and communities whose lives have been shaped by their relationship with the natural environment.During the discussion, Tamannaah spoke about the photographs' portrayal of ageing and contrasted the acceptance of visible signs of ageing among the people captured in the book with attitudes in urban society.“Why are we not accepting of something that's the most inevitable, which is the passage of time?” she asked, observing that the people in the photographs appeared more accepting of ageing than those living in cities.Responding to her remarks, Sadhguru said attitudes towards ageing in India had changed in recent times. “This is, I think, a recent happening in India. Otherwise, women and men grew old gracefully in this country. But we have taken Western ideas where the whole civilizations are ruled by hormones,” he said.He added that society had come to place excessive importance on youth and the age associated with peak hormonal activity. “But if you make one aspect of life everything, then you will be a very skewed life,” he said.Discussion on individuality and educationThe conversation also examined the individuality of the people featured in the photographs. Tamannaah noted that despite having fewer resources, education and exposure than their urban counterparts, the people appeared to have distinct personalities and a greater sense of comfort in expressing themselves.Sadhguru linked this to the purpose of education, arguing that it was increasingly focused on preparing people for employment rather than encouraging them to explore their interests and capabilities.“Education should be about expanding our horizons,” he said, adding that many people remained occupied with securing jobs, leaving limited room to explore what they were capable of or inclined towards.Bhardwaj, meanwhile, drew attention to the stillness visible in the faces captured in the book. He referred to Sadhguru's observation that stillness represented the highest level of intensity and asked how this related to the devotional lives of saints such as Meera and Kabir.Sadhguru explained that Meera's devotion to Krishna shaped her emotional experiences, allowing her to approach everything with a sense of sweetness. Kabir, he said, sought to balance his inner experiences with the practical demands of everyday life.He also referred to Krishna as an example of being fully engaged with the world without allowing external circumstances to disturb one's inner experience.About 'Disappearing Faces'Launched in August, Disappearing Faces is a collection of photographs taken by Sadhguru during his journeys through remote Himalayan regions over five decades.The book focuses particularly on communities in Nepal and Tibet, documenting their faces, lifestyles and experiences.According to the book's description, the photographs capture ways of life that are changing with the spread of modern development and the influence of the information age.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Uttar Pradesh Aircraft MRO Policy, 2022: Incentives, eligibility and implementation
content: POLICY AT A GLANCEItemPositionOfficial titleUttar Pradesh Aircraft Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul Policy, 2022Administrative departmentCivil Aviation Department, Uttar PradeshPrincipal objectiveDevelop Uttar Pradesh as a major aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul hubMain beneficiariesEligible aircraft, helicopter, engine, component and associated maintenance, repair and overhaul unitsCapital subsidy5 per cent, 8 per cent or 12 per cent of eligible capital investment, depending on investment sizeCapital investment up to Rs 500 crore5 per cent subsidyCapital investment above Rs 500 crore and below Rs 1,000 crore8 per cent subsidyCapital investment above Rs 1,000 crore12 per cent subsidyLand treatmentCost of land excluded from eligible capital investmentSkill-development focusAviation-related courses, technical training and partnerships with institutionsApplication mechanismCivil Aviation Department; prescribed capital-investment subsidy application form issuedStrategic infrastructureMRO facilities planned around Uttar Pradesh’s growing airport network, including the Noida International Airport ecosystemCurrent statusPolicy continues to be listed among the state’s operative policies; MRO projects remain at different stages of planning and development Maintenance, repair and overhaul, or MRO, covers the inspection, servicing, repair and overhaul required to keep aircraft, helicopters, engines and components airworthy. The Uttar Pradesh policy is intended specifically to create MRO capacity rather than subsidise airlines simply for operating flights from the state. What is the Uttar Pradesh Aircraft MRO Policy?The policy is a sector-specific framework intended to attract aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul businesses to Uttar Pradesh through capital incentives, airport infrastructure, skilled-worker development and administrative facilitation. MRO activity can involve different levels of maintenance, including:Line maintenance performed during routine aircraft operations;Airframe inspection and heavy maintenance;Engine maintenance and overhaul;Aircraft-component repair;Avionics maintenance;Landing-gear maintenance;Helicopter maintenance;Modification and refurbishment;Testing and specialist engineering services.The policy’s stated vision is to position Uttar Pradesh as a prominent and preferred MRO destination and to support development of large-scale MRO capacity within the state. The scheme is distinct from the Uttar Pradesh Defence and Aerospace Unit and Employment Promotion Policy. A company engaged in manufacturing aircraft components and one principally providing aircraft maintenance services may therefore fall under different policy frameworks depending on its main activity and approved project structure. Why was the policy introduced?Aircraft require scheduled and unscheduled maintenance throughout their operating life. Much of the higher-value maintenance performed for Indian airlines has historically depended on specialised facilities outside the country. The Union government has also sought to develop domestic MRO capacity by changing airport land-allotment and regulatory arrangements. Official Union government material states that revised MRO guidelines issued in September 2021 provided for allotment of land at Airports Authority of India airports through open tenders without airport royalty or cess on MRO operators. Against this background, Uttar Pradesh sought to use its expanding airport network and industrial base to attract MRO investment. The state policy aims to:Develop domestic aircraft-maintenance capacity;Attract Indian and international MRO operators;Reduce the need to send aircraft and components outside the state or country for maintenance;Generate skilled technical employment;Develop aviation-related training;Encourage private investment around airports;Support the wider civil aviation and aerospace ecosystem;Build links between MRO operators, aircraft manufacturers, airlines and educational institutions. These are policy objectives. They should not be presented as evidence that Uttar Pradesh has already captured a particular share of India’s MRO market. Who can qualify?The official policy applies to eligible MRO units established in Uttar Pradesh. Depending on the project and regulatory approvals, activities may include maintenance of:Commercial aircraft;General aviation aircraft;Helicopters;Engines;Auxiliary power units;Aircraft components;Avionics;Landing gear and other systems. A project must involve an eligible MRO activity and capital investment accepted by the Civil Aviation Department. Ordinary aircraft ground handling, passenger services, cargo forwarding or aviation consultancy should not be assumed to qualify merely because they are connected with an airport. The applicant must also obtain the approvals required under civil aviation regulation. State incentive approval does not authorise an organisation to maintain aircraft independently of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation or other applicable aviation regulators. Depending on the maintenance activity, the operator may require approvals relating to:Maintenance organisation certification;Approved facilities and hangars;Qualified engineers and technicians;Approved maintenance procedures;Tool and equipment calibration;Technical records;Quality and safety systems;Aircraft or component ratings. Where international airline customers are targeted, additional approvals from foreign aviation regulators may also be commercially necessary. What capital subsidy is available?Capital investment subsidy is the principal financial incentive under the policy. All eligible MRO units may receive support according to their approved investment: Eligible capital investmentSubsidy rateUp to Rs 500 crore5 per centAbove Rs 500 crore but below Rs 1,000 crore8 per centAbove Rs 1,000 crore12 per cent The official Invest UP policy page confirms these investment-linked slabs. The rate is applied to eligible capital investment, not automatically to the entire amount mentioned in a project announcement. The official policy explicitly states that land cost is not included in capital investment for calculating the benefit. Eligible expenditure may therefore relate to approved project assets such as:Hangars;Workshops;Maintenance machinery;Testing equipment;Aircraft-docking systems;Specialised tools;Component-repair facilities;Engine-handling equipment;Electrical and technical infrastructure;Other approved fixed assets. Applicants must use the definitions and exclusions contained in the sanctioned project and claim procedure. Working capital, financing expenses, routine maintenance expenditure and unrelated commercial assets should not be included merely because they form part of the company's overall investment. How is the subsidy claimed?The Civil Aviation Department has issued a dedicated MRO Capital Investment Subsidy Request Form for units claiming assistance under the 2022 policy. The application form requires project and investment information and identifies the applicable subsidy slab of 5 per cent, 8 per cent or 12 per cent. The broad process involves:Establishing an eligible MRO project in Uttar Pradesh.Obtaining project and statutory approvals.Completing the approved investment.Beginning commercial operations.Preparing the prescribed subsidy application.Submitting evidence of eligible capital expenditure.Providing invoices, payment records and supporting documentation.Undergoing departmental scrutiny and physical verification.Receiving the approved instalment after sanction.The official claim form refers to the financial year immediately following commencement of commercial operation, indicating that the capital support operates as a post-investment incentive rather than an unconditional upfront grant. Investors must therefore arrange sufficient equity and debt to construct and commission the project before relying on subsidy receipts. What documents are required?The exact checklist depends on the claim, but the official application form requires documentary support relating to investment and asset ownership. The form specifically refers to documents such as:Registered purchase documents;Evidence of asset cost;Stamp-duty payment receipts;Registration-fee receipts;Bank-related information;Capital-investment details;Applicable subsidy rate;Commercial-operation information. A claimant should also maintain:Chartered accountant-certified investment statements;Machinery invoices;Bank-payment records;Import documents, where applicable;Installation and commissioning records;Statutory approvals;Aircraft-maintenance organisation approvals;Building and fire-safety clearances;Employment records;Proof that assets are used for the sanctioned MRO operation.The eligible amount should be confirmed by the department rather than calculated only from the company’s balance sheet. What skill-development support is proposed?Aircraft maintenance depends heavily on skilled technical workers. An MRO business may require:Aircraft maintenance engineers;Licensed technical personnel;Avionics specialists;Engine technicians;Non-destructive testing personnel;Mechanical and electrical technicians;Quality inspectors;Planning engineers;Stores and component-control specialists.The policy therefore contains a specific human-resource component. Official policy material provides for promotion of aviation-related courses in technical institutes and universities in Uttar Pradesh to develop the technical workforce. It also encourages private partnerships for aviation training. The state’s aerospace-sector material additionally refers to plans for a training institution to support MRO activity. These measures should be regarded as ecosystem-development provisions. They do not mean that every MRO company automatically receives a fixed training subsidy unless a specific government order or project sanction provides one. Why is airport location important?Unlike many industrial activities, heavy aircraft maintenance generally requires direct or convenient access to airport infrastructure. An airframe MRO may need:Taxiway access;Large hangars;Aprons;Aircraft parking;Security-controlled premises;Fire and emergency services;Customs facilities for imported aircraft parts;Reliable power;Warehousing;Specialist workshops. Uttar Pradesh’s expanding aviation network is therefore central to the policy’s investment case. The state’s Civil Aviation sector page continues to list the MRO Policy, 2022 among its principal policies. The Noida International Airport ecosystem has been identified by the state as a major location for MRO and cargo infrastructure. Invest UP’s infrastructure material refers to an expected Rs 1,800 crore MRO and cargo hub associated with the airport. The word “expected” is important. The Rs 1,800 crore figure should not be presented as investment already completed or operational MRO capacity unless later official information confirms commissioning. How does the policy relate to Noida International Airport?Noida International Airport at Jewar is expected to provide a major opportunity for aviation-support businesses because of its scale, passenger and cargo potential and proximity to the National Capital Region. The state has promoted development of MRO infrastructure around the airport as part of the broader aviation ecosystem. Official Invest UP material has referred to an MRO and cargo hub and to efforts to attract aircraft-maintenance operators. However, several stages must be distinguished:A proposal;Expression of interest;Selection of a developer;Land allotment;Financial closure;Construction;Regulatory certification;Commercial operations.An announcement that an airline, aircraft manufacturer or airport operator is considering an MRO facility is therefore not evidence that the facility is operational. Does the policy replace aviation regulation?No. The state government can provide incentives and infrastructure, but aircraft airworthiness and maintenance standards fall within the national civil aviation regulatory framework. An MRO organisation must comply with the relevant requirements of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. Depending on its intended customers, an operator may also pursue certification from international regulators. Airlines may prefer facilities holding approvals recognised by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency, the US Federal Aviation Administration or other authorities. The policy therefore improves the investment environment but cannot reduce mandatory aviation-safety standards. How does it fit with the wider aerospace strategy?The MRO policy complements several other Uttar Pradesh initiatives:Expansion of civil airports;Development of Noida International Airport;Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor;Defence and aerospace manufacturing incentives;Cargo and logistics development;Aviation-related skill development. The state's current defence and aerospace material continues to identify MRO facilities for aircraft, helicopters, engines and components as an area being actively promoted. However, businesses must select the correct incentive framework. An aerospace manufacturer cannot automatically claim MRO incentives for its manufacturing expenditure, and an MRO project should not assume that the same capital investment can simultaneously receive benefits under another sectoral policy. Implementation and current statusThe Uttar Pradesh Aircraft Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul Policy, 2022 remains listed on Invest UP and Nivesh Mitra among the state's policies. The state has also issued the prescribed capital-subsidy application form, showing that the incentive mechanism has moved beyond the policy-announcement stage. At the infrastructure level, the government continues to promote MRO development, especially around Noida International Airport. However, the official sources reviewed did not provide a consolidated public dashboard showing:MRO applications received;Units approved;Capital subsidy sanctioned;Subsidy actually disbursed;Private investment realised specifically under the policy;Hangar capacity commissioned;Aircraft serviced annually;Direct employment generated;International regulatory certifications obtained by policy-supported units. For that reason, proposed MRO hubs, investment discussions and announced projects should not be presented as operational achievements. Key challenges and practical considerationsHigh capital requirement: Heavy maintenance, engine and component facilities require expensive hangars, equipment and specialised tooling. Regulatory certification: Commercial operations cannot begin solely on the basis of state-policy approval. Aircraft access: Heavy MRO facilities need suitable airport land and taxiway connectivity. Skilled workforce: Licensed engineers and specialised technicians take time to train. Imported components: Aircraft parts and specialised equipment may remain dependent on international supply chains. Customer contracts: Airlines generally require strong technical credentials before awarding major maintenance work. Long gestation: Construction, equipment installation, certification and airline approvals can delay revenue generation. Back-ended incentive: Capital subsidy is claimed after investment and commencement of operations, increasing financing requirements. What investors should keep in mindBefore committing capital, an MRO investor should verify:Whether the proposed activity qualifies under the policy;The correct capital-investment slab;Which assets are eligible for subsidy;Exclusion of land cost;Airport land and taxiway availability;Civil Aviation Department approval;Directorate General of Civil Aviation certification requirements;Customs and bonded-warehouse arrangements;Fire and environmental approvals;Power and utility availability;Skilled-worker requirements;Commercial-operation deadlines;Claim documentation;Restrictions on overlapping incentives.A formal project-specific eligibility decision should be obtained before the subsidy is incorporated into the financing model. FAQsWhat is the main incentive under the policy?Eligible MRO units receive capital investment subsidy at rates of 5 per cent, 8 per cent or 12 per cent depending on the size of eligible investment. What subsidy applies to a project investing up to Rs 500 crore?The applicable rate is 5 per cent of eligible capital investment. What happens above Rs 500 crore?Projects investing more than Rs 500 crore but below Rs 1,000 crore may receive an 8 per cent subsidy. What is the rate above Rs 1,000 crore?Eligible investment above Rs 1,000 crore attracts a 12 per cent capital subsidy. Is land cost included?No. The official policy states that land cost is excluded from capital investment for subsidy calculation. Who administers the policy?The Civil Aviation Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, administers the framework. Does a subsidy approval allow an operator to service aircraft immediately?No. The MRO must separately satisfy all applicable Directorate General of Civil Aviation and aviation-safety requirements. ConclusionThe Uttar Pradesh Aircraft Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul Policy, 2022 is designed to use the state's expanding aviation infrastructure to attract a specialised, capital-intensive service industry. Its principal incentive is a graded capital subsidy of 5 per cent, 8 per cent or 12 per cent according to eligible investment, with land excluded from the calculation. The policy also emphasises aviation skills and institutional partnerships needed to create a sustainable MRO workforce. Its effectiveness should ultimately be judged through functioning maintenance facilities, aircraft and components actually serviced, skilled employment created and capital subsidies disbursed. Planned hubs and investment discussions are important indicators of interest, but they should remain clearly distinguished from commissioned MRO capacity. SourcesUttar Pradesh Aircraft Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul Policy, 2022, Civil Aviation Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh.MRO Capital Investment Subsidy Request Form, Civil Aviation Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh; 2023.Civil Aviation Sector, Invest UP, Government of Uttar Pradesh.Civil Aviation, Invest UP, Government of Uttar Pradesh.Directorate of Civil Aviation, Uttar Pradesh, Government of Uttar Pradesh.Policies, Nivesh Mitra, Government of Uttar Pradesh.

headline: 'Starlink to enter India very soon': ISpA says satellite internet rollout nearing next phase
content: NEW DELHI: Director general of Indian Space Association Lt Gen Anil Kumar Bhatt (Retd.) on Monday said India's satellite internet market was gearing up for expansion, with OneWeb ready to launch services and Starlink awaiting final spectrum allocation.Speaking on the sidelines of the India International Space Conclave 2026, Bhatt said Starlink's entry into India was expected soon, while Jio was planning to deploy a large satellite communication constellation by 2029."Starlink is also going to come into India very soon. They are waiting for the final spectrum allocation for them," he told news agency ANI.The developments come amid a controversy over Starlink's entry into India, after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk alleged that powerful business interests were attempting to block the company's entry to protect existing operators.The government had rejected the allegations, maintaining that the licensing process was transparent and uniform.According to a report by ANI, Jio, OneWeb and Starlink had all secured licences, but commercial services would begin only after the spectrum allocation and pricing framework was finalised and the operators met security requirements.According to ANI, Starlink was the last of the three to submit its compliance documents.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
