headline: US monetary policy: Why aggressive rate hikes are a bad idea in this economy
content: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Americans are justifiably losing patience after six years of elevated inflation rates. So, too, are some key central bankers. Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller, an influential voter on monetary policy, said this week that he was prepared to “shock people” by raising interest rates by half a percentage point when policymakers meet in three weeks to help contain inflation. Minutes from the Fed’s last meeting in October that were released last week suggest at least one other participant shared Waller’s willingness to boost rates in larger increments. Increasing rates is the right strategy, but a monetary policy broadside would be wrong at a time when wage growth is failing to keep pace with the rising cost of living, credit market conditions have tightened, the housing market continues to deteriorate and shares of artificial intelligence (AI) firms are wobbling and risk dragging the broader S&P 500 Index into a correction. In that context, you’d probably be shocked to discover that the Fed is raising rates at all, let alone considering moving in half-point increments. But the reality is that consumer prices are up 3.7% from a year earlier, well above the Fed’s 2% target. So although it’s appropriate for the Fed to be resolute in getting inflation under control, caution is warranted. In other words, raising rates in quarter-point increments should suffice.

headline: India, Vietnam to lead Asia-Pacific growth in 2027 as China slows: S&P
content: India's economy is expected to grow by 7 per cent in both the current and the next financial years, keeping the country among the fastest-growing economies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027, according to S&P Global Ratings.In its Economic Outlook for Asia-Pacific, released on Monday, the rating agency said India and Vietnam were likely to lead regional growth next year, with Vietnam's economy projected to expand by 7.5 per cent.China's growth, meanwhile, is expected to slow to 4.3 per cent in 2027 from 4.5 per cent in 2026.S&P said India's expansion during the June and September quarters was supported by strong goods exports, public-sector investment and household consumption, with the latter benefiting from buoyant credit growth."We expect Vietnam and India to be the region's fastest-growing economies in 2027," the agency said.India's export performance has benefited from higher commodity prices, trade diversification and its growing integration into global supply chains. S&P said the strength was particularly visible in electronic and engineering goods, as well as chemicals.El Nino, rising costs pose inflation risksDespite the strong growth outlook, S&P expects India's growth-inflation mix to become less favourable in the second half of the current financial year, as higher input costs are increasingly passed on to consumers.It flagged uneven monsoon conditions, deficient summer rainfall and lower reservoir levels as factors that could weigh on current agricultural output and the upcoming winter crop. Persistent El Nino conditions are also expected to put pressure on food prices across Asia-Pacific, particularly in India.The agency expects inflation in India to average 5.3 per cent in the financial year ending March 2027, with risks tilted to the upside.Retail inflation stood at 6.1 per cent in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's tolerance band of 2-6 per cent.S&P anticipates a further 25-basis-point policy rate hike by the RBI in December, followed by another increase in early 2027. It expects inflation to ease to 4.7 per cent in the financial year ending March 2028.India is scheduled to release its official GDP growth data for the July-September quarter on November 30.The RBI had projected 7.2 per cent growth for the quarter, while the Finance Ministry's Monthly Economic Review estimated it at 7.35 per cent.Asia-Pacific growth to moderate, China remains weak spotAt the regional level, S&P expects Asia-Pacific economic growth to ease to 4.4 per cent in 2027 from 4.8 per cent in 2026. It identified high energy prices as the biggest macroeconomic headwind and the global expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure as the largest growth tailwind, although both forces are expected to moderate somewhat next year.The agency expects exports to remain strong, largely driven by shipments of AI-related technology, while domestic demand is likely to stay broadly resilient outside China.However, it warned that technology export growth could peak in the coming quarters because of challenging base effects and a possible slowdown in AI infrastructure investment in the US and other markets.China is expected to remain a weak spot in the regional outlook, with S&P projecting its growth to slow to 4.3 per cent in 2027 from 4.5 per cent this year.The agency cited weak domestic demand, a prolonged downturn in the housing sector and subdued consumption and investment.It also said the likelihood of significant fresh policy stimulus in China was limited, given that the country's 2026 growth target of 4.5 per cent was within reach.S&P identified three major risks to the regional outlook: a significant slowdown in global AI-related spending, persistently high energy prices and a sharper increase in global interest rates.While consumer inflation across Asia-Pacific is expected to moderate in 2027 as the impact of higher energy prices eases, the agency cautioned that prolonged high energy costs could push inflation and interest rates higher.Stronger pressure from US interest rates could also trigger capital outflows and currency depreciation in some economies.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

headline: ‘Ties built on trust’: India announces Rs 15,000 crore package for Nepal
content: India on Monday announced a Rs 15,000 crore development assistance package for Nepal, alongside a series of cross-border connectivity and energy projects, after Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks with his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, in New Delhi. The two sides launched a new train service between Ayodhya and Janakpur, advanced a hydropower project and an oil pipeline, and took steps to strengthen road, rail, and border connectivity between Nepal and towns in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar. They also agreed to deepen cooperation in education, innovation, agriculture and youth development. Sharing my remarks during the joint press meet with PM Balendra Shah of Nepal. @ShahBalen @PM_nepal_ — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 23, 2026 'Shared history, faith, culture' After the bilateral meeting, PM Modi said the relationship between India and Nepal "is not merely one of neighbours, but one of kinship and unbreakable trust". "Our joys are shared, and so are our challenges. We are partners in each other’s progress and a source of support for each other in difficult times,” PM Modi said. Modi also expressed condolences over the loss of lives in the devastating floods that hit Nepal in August. The PM said India had continued to ensure supplies of fuel, fertilisers, and other essential commodities to Nepal despite disruptions and challenges to global oil supplies amid the West Asia conflict, reaffirming its commitment to the Neighbourhood First policy. As the two leaders launched the Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur, Modi said the ties between India and Nepal are “woven together by shared history, faith, culture and deep people-to-people ties”. “Lord Ram and Mother Sita are symbols of our shared civilisation and faith.” Modi said India would support youth development and innovation in Nepal by establishing a start-up incubator, an innovation hub, and an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT). “We will expand scholarship opportunities in Law and Technology in India for Nepali students.” He said India will also help develop an agro-industrial park in Nepal to promote food processing and value addition. ‘Ties stand as firm as the Himalayas’ Shah said the Nepal-India relationship is built on mutual respect, trust, and goodwill, with people-to-people connections forming its foundation. “The ties between Nepal and India stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the ocean. A closeness so profound that words alone can scarcely capture it. As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India has consistently stood as a first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult hours.” Shah thanked the Indian government and people for their support, saying the delegation-level talks had focused on strengthening and modernising the two countries' longstanding relationship through substantive discussions on a wide range of bilateral issues. “In this context, important understandings across diverse areas of Nepal-India cooperation have been reached, alongside the inauguration and groundbreaking of key infrastructure projects. We are clear that the outcomes of the understandings that we reach today and the projects we advance must translate into prosperity in the fields of our farmers, employment and opportunity in the hands of our youth, new horizons in the dreams of our students, and tangible avenues for new markets, investment and business expansion for our entrepreneurs. I am confident that these historic milestones will elevate Nepal-India relations to new heights,” the Nepali PM said. Shah said the two countries must build on their longstanding relationship to strengthen cooperation and lay a firm foundation for future ties. “Our Himalayas, as sources of clean water, sustain millions across this region. The pristine rivers that flow from the Himalayas into the Ganga remind us of our future and destiny, underscoring the imperative to address the challenges of climate change through collective action.” He also welcomed Indian investors to Nepal to partner in the economic prosperity of our two countries. “In the coming days, we should foster an environment where Indian students come to study at an IIT established in Nepal while expanding direct air connectivity between cities of both countries for the convenience of our citizens,” he added. Other projects The two leaders laid the foundation stone of a new Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Banbasa in Champawat district, Uttarakhand, along the India–Nepal border. They also reviewed progress in the construction of the ICPs at Bhairahawa in Nepal, Sunauli in UP, and Nepal’s Dodhara Chandani, and inaugurated a new cross-border motorable bridge between Dharchula (India) and Darchula (Nepal). They also laid the foundation stone for the Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project (669 MW) and dedicated Phase II of the Motihari–Amlekhgunj Pipeline (MAPL). The two leaders also laid the foundation stone for a petroleum terminal at Jhapa for the proposed Siliguri-Jhapa petroleum pipeline. Shah, popularly known as Balen Shah, is in India on his first bilateral visit abroad since taking office in March. Although this is Shah’s first bilateral visit abroad, the two PMs have spoken by phone before.

headline: Sikkim tops states in per capita government health spending
content: Gangtok: Sikkim has recorded the highest per capita government healthcare expenditure among Indian states, with spending of ₹16,026 per person in 2023–24, according to the latest National Health Accounts (NHA) estimates released by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The figure is more than five times the national average of ₹2,959 and over 14 times Bihar’s ₹1,126, the lowest among the 28 states. Health Minister GT Dhungel described the achievement as a “big leap” for the Himalayan state, crediting Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang’s sustained focus on public health and patient welfare. “The latest report from the Government of India confirms that Sikkim has the highest per capita health expenditure among states at around ₹16,025 per person, compared to some states spending around ₹2,000,” Dhungel said. He said the state was addressing key healthcare challenges, including tuberculosis (TB), diabetes and specialised procedures such as kidney transplants, through sustained financial support and accessible medical care. “While the prevalence of certain diseases remains a concern, comprehensive measures are being taken to control and contain them so that citizens receive maximum benefit,” the minister added.

headline: India, Nepal get new rail link connecting Ayodhya and Janakpur Dham; key details
content: NEW DELHI: A new rail link connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal has made the travel between the two major religious destinations easier, with the Saryu Kamala Express covering around 604 km in approximately 19 hours.The launch comes during Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah's first state visit to India, who is in New Delhi for bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The service will operate once a week in each direction from November 28, allowing pilgrims to travel directly between the two destinations without changing trains en route.The inaugural run on Monday, however, operated as a special train (No. 04295), departing from Ayodhya Dham at 12.30 pm.Saryu Kamala Express: Regular weekly scheduleThe regular service will run once a week in both directions. The train will cover the approximately 604-km route in around 19 hours.Ayodhya to Janakpur Dham — Train No. 15596Frequency: Every MondayDeparture from Ayodhya Cantt: 5.50 pmArrival at Janakpur Dham: 12.40 pm on Tuesday (Nepal time)Janakpur Dham to Ayodhya — Train No. 15595Frequency: Every SaturdayDeparture from Janakpur Dham: 1.10 pm (Nepal time)Arrival at Ayodhya Cantt: 8.10 am on SundayRoute and stoppagesThe train will stop at 10 stations along the route: Ayodhya Dham, Mankapur, Basti, Gorakhpur, Narkatiaganj, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Shisho, Madhubani and Jaynagar.The direct connection is expected to make the journey more convenient for pilgrims and tourists travelling between the two religious centres, eliminating the need to change trains along the way.Ayodhya and Janakpur hold a special place in the Ramayana tradition. Ayodhya is associated with Lord Ram, while Janakpur in Nepal is regarded as the birthplace of Goddess Sita.The state government expects the service to strengthen the Ramayana Circuit and promote religious tourism. It is also expected to boost trade, local businesses and employment opportunities in border areas of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Nepal.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 80 people from Hakki-Pikki community arrested in DR Congo receive no food, healthcare
content: Davanagere: Over 80 people belonging to Hakki-Pikki, arrested in Democratic Republic of Congo, for allegedly carrying out business activities without holding business visa are spending their days in jail without food and healthcare. Of them, 36 are in Beni city, 35 in Kisangani and the remaining are in Kinshasa. They are from Davangere, Shivamogga and Mysuru districts of Karnataka. Sharing an audio call involving Indian embassy official in DR Congo, Karnataka's Hakki-Pikki community President Puneeth Kumar told DH that officials are not responding to the grievances. Instead, they asked him to question the community for engaging in illegal business activities. .Six Hakki-Pikki tribals stuck in Fiji for carrying 10 dollars; seek help from Karnataka govt."A team of officials went to Kinshasa capital of DR Congo, and gathered information about arrested Indian nationals. Since then, they have not lent helping hand to them Hakki-Pikki community," he charged. He further stated it is the duty of Indian Embassy officials to provide food, shelter and healthcare on priority basis when their fellow citizens are in trouble in overseas. "There is an Indian community welfare Fund which has to be used for this. So this is high time the government of India comes forward and helps them to return to the mother land," Kumar said. On repeated arrests of people belonging to the community in African countries, he said they don't own land so they go there to earn their livelihood. "The government should give lands to them so that they can work here only. Besides, awareness camps must be conducted at taluk and village level for the community on measures to be taken when they go 10 people," Kumar said.

headline: Naveen Patnaik breaks silence over foreign trip probe: ‘Allegations false; appropriate reply will be given’
content: Biju Janata Dal (BJD) president Naveen Patnaik on Monday strongly refuted allegations surrounding his foreign trips while serving as the chief minister of Odisha, dismissing them as “false”. This comes two days after the Odisha government ordered an “administrative probe” into the foreign trips made by Patnaik, his close aide and retired bureaucrat VK Pandian, who was serving as his private secretary, and another IPS officer between 2022 and 2024. “I had very limited travel abroad only to deal with some important subjects about Odisha's interests. I understand that some false allegations have been made about my travels and those of my colleagues. An appropriate reply will be given,” Patnaik told reporters in the state Assembly. The probe, which is to be conducted by a senior civil servant, was ordered following allegations by rights activists that information relating to expenditure on the foreign visits to Italy and Japan between 2022 and 2024 was “suspicious, non-transparent and incomplete”. The inquiry has triggered a political slugfest in Odisha, with the BJD questioning the timing and motive of the move. The BJP maintained that the law is equal for all and said that whenever allegations are made, it is the duty of the state government to investigate and uncover the facts. During his 24-year tenure as chief minister, Patnaik undertook three foreign trips. In June 2022, he travelled to Italy and Dubai on an 11-day visit. In Italy, he attended an event organised by the World Food Programme and met Pope Francis at Vatican City. He also participated in an investors’ meet in Dubai. In April 2023, Patnaik led a business delegation to Japan and Singapore to attract investments to Odisha. Pandian, who was then serving as Patnaik’s private secretary, accompanied him on the visits, as did IPS officer Ravi Kant. Kant, a 1998-batch IPS officer, was posted at the Odisha Resident Commissioner’s Office in New Delhi during both trips. He is currently serving as an Inspector-General with the Border Security Force (BSF). Patnaik, who spent much of his early life abroad before entering politics at the age of 51, made his first foreign visit as chief minister to the United Kingdom in 2012, more than 12 years after assuming office.

headline: Wider access to finance, digital economy key to eradicate poverty: FM
content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said wider access to finance, markets and the digital economy would be key to eradicating poverty and ensuring those lifted out of it do not slip back.Quoting the World Bank report which showed that nearly 500 million Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, Sitharaman said the Narendra Modi government has focused on targeted interventions, measurable outcomes and tailored schemes to remove deprivations."Garibi is not merely a shortage of income or wages. A household without a secure roof, safe water, sanitation or healthcare remains vulnerable even when its income rises. One illness can wipe out savings and push a family back into poverty," the minister said in a LinkedIn post titled 'The Decade India Turned the Tide on Poverty'.She said welfare schemes like Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, and Swachh Bharat are together acting as "insurance against the shocks" that once pushed families back into poverty, while lowering household expenditure and freeing time for work."The next phase builds on this progress to lift the few people still at the bottom of the ladder out of poverty, while ensuring those who have already risen keep advancing and never slip back. The protection offered via various measures must now be complemented by even wider access to finance, markets and the digital economy," Sitharaman said.The government is building closer links between academia and industry through employment-linked incentives, internships and apprenticeships, while the government's investment in infrastructure is connecting the country. Opportunity cannot remain the preserve of a few, she said while outlining the challenges to Viksit Bharat.Observing that while protection keeps families from slipping back into poverty, to rise further, they need opportunities to earn."The government has created financial opportunities through schemes like MUDRA (60 crore loan accounts have been sanctioned, about two-thirds to women), while PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma support street vendors and traditional artisans," she said.Last month, the World Bank's Poverty & Equity Brief on India report showed that nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, while extreme poverty has been almost eradicated.Sitharaman said India has witnessed a fundamental shift from temporary relief to removing the barriers that perpetuate poverty. Guided by Antyodaya, the welfare of the last person in the line, the government chose the harder path of addressing deprivations, household by household, ensuring development reached those who needed it most, she wrote."There was no magic wand. Each scheme required careful identification of beneficiaries, effective delivery and follow-up until the last household was reached," Sitharaman said, adding, "Prime Minister Modi's sustained attention has helped translate policy into tangible improvements in people's lives.

headline: Sexual health stigma pushes men towards self-medication and delayed care, expert warn; Pacific OneHealth launches dedicated Men's Health Centre
content: PRNewswireNew Delhi [India], November 23: Sexual health concerns such as erectile dysfunction, premature ejaculation, infertility and low libido remain difficult conversations for many Indian men, often leading to delayed consultations, self-medication and reliance on unverified remedies or unqualified practitioners. Expert warn that stigma surrounding sexual health can affect relationships and quality of life while delaying the identification of underlying metabolic, hormonal and cardiovascular conditions.A recent Indian study involving 14,594 men diagnosed with erectile dysfunction found that 13.3% reported self-medication, highlighting the risks of managing sexual health concerns without professional supervision. Another recent study of patients attending a specialist sexual health clinic found that 72% had not sought formal care before presenting, while 46% had experienced symptoms for over a year."Men's health often remains overlooked, particularly when it comes to sensitive concerns that are difficult to discuss openly. Through our dedicated Men's Health Centres, we aim to create an environment where men feel comfortable seeking medical advice without hesitation or stigma. Our endeavour is to make specialised, confidential and preventive healthcare more accessible, while encouraging men to take a proactive approach to their overall well-being," said Dr Swadeep Srivastava, Co-founder & President, Pacific OneHealth.Addressing the growing need for accessible and confidential men's healthcare, Pacific OneHealth has introduced its dedicated Men's Health Centre services at Karol Bagh and Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi, led by Prof. (Dr.) Rajeev Sood is Principal Director - Urology at Pacific OneHealth. He has previously served as Vice Chancellor of Baba Farid University of Health Sciences, Faridkot, and Dean of Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi. He was also a Founder Member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi. The initiative aims to encourage men to seek timely medical advice, move beyond stigma and prioritise preventive screening and evidence-based treatment. Consultations are conducted in complete confidentiality, providing men a discreet and comfortable setting to discuss sensitive health concerns.Sexual health problems are not always isolated concerns. Erectile difficulties, reduced sexual desire, ejaculation-related problems and fertility issues may sometimes be associated with diabetes, cardiovascular risks, hormonal imbalances, stress or other underlying medical conditions. Doctors caution against relying on unverified sexual enhancement products, online remedies or medicines without medical supervision, as these may delay diagnosis and appropriate treatment."Men often hesitate to discuss sexual health concerns because of embarrassment, social stigma or misconceptions around masculinity. Problems related to erections, desire, ejaculation or fertility should not be ignored or treated through unverified remedies. A proper medical evaluation helps us understand the underlying cause and guide treatment accordingly," said Prof. (Dr.) Rajeev Sood.The Men's Health Centre offers structured diagnostic pathways covering urinary, reproductive, hormonal, metabolic and broader systemic health. To encourage preventive evaluation, Pacific OneHealth has introduced four assessment packages:- Basic Men's Health Package - ₹800 (listed value ₹4,999): Uroflowmetry, Serum Total Testosterone, Semen Analysis and Periscope Evaluation.- Fatigue Profile - ₹1,000 (listed value ₹5,999): Thyroid profile, Vitamin D, Vitamin B12, iron parameters, Fasting Insulin, HbA1c, Homocysteine, APO A1, hs-CRP and Lipid Profile.- Complete Men's Health Package - ₹1,100 (listed value ₹4,999): Liver and Kidney Panels, Lipid Profile, Thyroid, Vitamins D and B12, Iron Panel, ESR, CRP, RA Factor, HbA1c, Random Glucose, Urine R/M, PFT, Chest X-ray and Dental Evaluation.- Ultimate Men's Health Package - ₹2,500 (listed value ₹9,999): Expanded investigations including PSA and other listed tumour markers, ECG, Uroflowmetry, PFT, Chest X-ray, functional gait testing, skin and scalp analysis, and oral, eye and ear evaluations. ECHO and USG Abdomen are available as optional additions.With its specialist-led Men's Health Programme, Pacific OneHealth aims to make men's healthcare more approachable by addressing the hesitation around sexual health, promoting early evaluation and providing a structured pathway to preventive care across both centres.Confidential Consultation. headline: In 12 states, NGO Pratham’s Second Chance Programme is helping women school dropouts appear for their Class X Board exams
content: In a tranquil residential enclave at Vijaypura in Devanahalli, 40 kilometres from Bengaluru city, a modest abode has been converted into a classroom, the walls supporting a mixed population of subjects: on one patch of a wall, Kannada vowels and consonants and scientific diagrams enjoy joint tenancy. Women frantically take down notes as the blackboard gets busy. From time to time, someone would look up from the note-taking to clarify doubts. At this hour, the doubts pertain to monohybrid cross and dihybrid cross. Navyanthi D.N., the science teacher, offers patient answers. It is a motley class of learners, consisting of Asha workers, a tailor, a young mother with a toddler on her lap watching the phone, noon meal staff working in schools, and determined homemakers in good numbers. An employee with the Kempegowda International Airport makes a dash for the door around noon; she had sought permission to leave the class early to be present at work. This is one of the many learning clusters run as part of the Pratham-Jameel Second Chance programme, an initiative by the Pratham Education Foundation, to support girls and women who have dropped out of school before completing secondary education. At the Devanahalli Block, this programme is in its second year. Parliamentary panel flags nearly 73% students drop out before finishing higher secondary Parliamentary panel flags nearly 73% students drop out before finishing higher secondary "The Committee are of the view that there is an urgent need to increase the number of schools at secondary and higher secondary levels," it said. Parliamentary panel flags nearly 73% students drop out before finishing higher secondary storyline 1 Approximately 24 lakh students fail in Class X every year, and a vast number of them drop out of the formal education system, says a study from the Ministry of Education. Efforts to get them to progress to Class XI through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) meet with modest success. An analysis report by the Ministry of Education, published in The Hindu in May 2023, states the failure rates range between 47% and 55%. Given this, interventions by NGOs such as Pratham become significant and essential. Pratham has been bringing out the ASER (Annual Status of Education Report) since 2005. Started in 2011 as a pilot in Maharashtra, the Second Chance Programme was extended to seven states. Currently, it is being run in 12 states, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Karnataka has over one lakh school dropout students aged above 15 Karnataka has over one lakh school dropout students aged above 15 Samagra Shikshana-Karnataka has found that 38,469 students, who had registered for SSLC exams, and 64,573 students, who had registered for II PUC exams, did not take them; it plans to enrol them to take exams through Karnataka State Open Schools Karnataka has over one lakh school dropout students aged above 15 storyline 1 After many door-to-door mobilisation campaigns to enrol women candidates, the new academic year of the Second Chance Programme began in July 2026 in most cities. The foundation course, typically covering lessons taught in the upper middle classes, soaks up three to four months. Mothers’ groups in neighbourhoods help the ground staff get information about other women or older girls who might be interested in completing class X. Their ground staff’s tasks include persuading family members to support the women to pursue studies and have a secondary school leaving certificate no matter what the age of the person is. The persuasion sometimes has to be targeted at the women who have to take up the studies. The challenge of getting women to enrol is different in every state. “In Tamil Nadu, we come across men who would prefer that women stay at home; in Rajasthan, the confidence levels of women are low as they have failed in school, and in Gujarat, many are not allowed to enrol due to safety and security reasons,” says Renu Seth, co-lead, Girls and Women Programs, Pratham Education Foundation. Giving girls and women a second chance — whether in getting an education or earning a livelihood — creates a multiplier effect that transforms not just one life, but the family and, gradually, whole communities, says Renu. They use videos, organise community meetings and share success stories of alumnae to help them take the decision to return to the classroom. Many learners hesitate to disclose their enrolment in Class X due to fear of being judged or mocked by others. “Some will hide their books when they go to class and will tell family and friends only when they pass,” says Renu. Inspired by neighbours Many women who enrol to clear their Class X examinations are inspired by working neighbours, and some do so to set an example for their children. Twenty-nine-year-old Supritha Rani, a mother of two young girls, wanted to enrol as a lawyer only to be refused admission as she did not have an SSLC certificate. “My mother died young, and it was my grandmother who took care of me, but she did not have the means to send me to school after a certain age. Now, my husband is very supportive and shares responsibilities at home, so I get time to study at home,” says Supritha, adding that she spends at least an hour every day with textbooks. Likewise, 47-year-old Lakshmi, working as a tailor, is back in the classroom after three decades. Many of the topics taught in the class are completely new to her, but Lakshmi feels she can devote more time, as someone is there to help them, unlike in the times she grew up in. Then there is 51-year-old Rudramma M, a single mother who runs a hotel. By two marks, she failed in the English paper that she wrote this year but is determined not to give up. After the foundation classes, students move to the “main course”, which focuses on helping learners prepare for the board-mandated curriculum. The progress during this stage is tracked through internal assessments. In all these months, interactive methods such as activity-based learning, group work and self-learning are adopted. Pitching tent Pratham has managed to cover much ground with the help of its many foot soldiers. Many of these classes are conducted at rented spaces, and some spaces are given free by the community. Sometimes, spaces are also sought in schools successfully. “We have built that trust with the community, so there is some familiarity going to a certain geography. Very rarely do we attend to a completely new geography,” says Soumya Nair, Girls and Women – Strategic Partnerships & Operations, Pratham Education Foundation. Although classes are held from Monday to Saturday, it is unlike a regular school. There are no punishments and greater emphasis is placed on flexibility so that women do not drop out of the programme. At the centre in Devanahalli, for instance, young mothers with children have the option of putting them to sleep in the adjoining room while they attend the classes. Once students move to the main course and are unable to attend classes regularly for genuine reasons, the facilitator is sent to the house of the candidate for home classes. Ahead of the board examination, government school teachers are invited to motivate the students. In some clusters, the ground staff take permission from the neighbourhood school so that candidates take a mock exam by writing with regular students to remove any anxiety. Transportation is arranged during exam time. During this one year in preparation for the Board examination, life skills-focused activities are also conducted with the learners, concentrating on enhancement of communication, decision-making and critical thinking skills. Despite all these measures, getting women to dedicate one full year in preparation for the Board examination is not easy, as many drop out for various reasons. Rashmi R., cluster head of the Devanahalli Block, shares this data: last year, the cluster enrolled 120 candidates, of which 75 registered to take the Karnataka State Examination Board, but finally only 48 appeared for the examination, and 33 passed in all six subjects. “Although classes have begun, we continue with our mobilisation activity, some from the current batch give us leads. Our target is to enrol 100 students this year,” says Rashmi. Despite the dropout rate across states, Pratham believes the programme has made inroads. Till date, the programme has impacted over 50,000 girls and women, and the current national pass percentage is 78. The contents of the syllabus vary from state to state. At least five states follow the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) pattern; four states adopt the State Open Schooling Board; and Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka are under the State Board, with subjects such as maths and English being compulsory. The way ahead Since 2022-23, the Second Chance Programme has been expanding, with more learners appearing for board exams. Board results have improved from 72% in 2023-2024 to 78% in 2025-26. Maharashtra and Odisha have been registering consistent performance. In states where Pratham has been working for a long time, the team collaborates as knowledge partners. The district administration has a database of women who have dropped out of the schooling system, making it easy to identify gaps. In 2022, Pratham began with a district-level rural livelihood mission partnership in Nagpur, Maharashtra, where they provided content, training, support in mobilisation and handholding the entire programme cycle, and this helped 175 women complete Class X. “Later, we partnered with the state-rural livelihood mission in Bihar (Jeevika), where this year, 1,000 women have appeared for their Class X exam. In 2026, we are also embarking on a new chapter with the Telangana government’s rural livelihoods mission, SERP, to enrol SHG members for Class X, and we will support them end-to-end,” says Soumya. Soumya says that transitioning from “direct operations to government partnerships” will help increase the number of women enrolling for Class X in a year and help them move towards a more sustainable model. Earlier, the goal of the programme was to help women who have dropped out of the formal schooling system to complete their Class X; now, as they have cracked that code, it has expanded in other ways. Many of the alumnae have enrolled for higher education. Both Soumya and Renu say subjects such as maths, science, language and social science are given so much importance in the curriculum that they sparked an interest in some of the women. And Pratham is exploring ways to get such candidates into STEM-related courses.

headline: Assam govt halts 251 forest promotions, puts PCCF order in abeyance
content: Guwahati, Nov 23: In an unusual move that has exposed the apparent disconnect between the State forest department headquarters and the Assam government, the regime in Dispur has put on hold the promotion of 251 forest personnel, barely a day after an order was issued by the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) and Head of Forest Force (HoFF). The sudden intervention has triggered speculation within the department, with questions being raised over the circumstances that led to the government’s decision to suspend the promotion order. While officials have maintained silence on the reasons, sources point to growing differences between the forest department headquarters at Aranya Bhavan and Dispur over administrative control and decision-making. The promotion order, issued by PCCF & HoFF Sandeep Kumar on November 20, elevated 251 Forester-II personnel to officiate as Forester-I and also assigned them their respective places of posting. The Divisional Forest Officers (DFOs) concerned were directed to release the promoted personnel within seven days to enable them to join their new places of posting. However, the order was short-lived. On November 21, the Joint Secretary of the forest department issued a fresh directive, placing the PCCF’s promotion order in abeyance with immediate effect and until further orders. “The order issued by the PCCF & HoFF, Assam, is hereby kept in abeyance with immediate effect until further orders,” the communication stated, adding that the decision had the approval of the competent authority. In a parallel move, the department issued another order on the same day, making it mandatory for the PCCF & HoFF to obtain prior government approval before issuing any promotion, transfer or posting order involving forest officials. “In order to streamline and ensure transparency on transfer and posting of forest officials under the Environment, Forest & Climate Change Department, it is hereby ordered that no promotion and transfer of any forest official shall be issued or effected by office of the PCCF & HoFF, Assam, without obtaining prior approval of the government. This order shall come into force with immediate effect and until further orders,” the directive stated. The twin orders have brought into focus the apparent lack of coordination between Aranya Bhavan and Dispur, an issue that has reportedly been a point of contention within the department for some time. The timing of the development is also significant, as PCCF & HoFF Sandeep Kumar is due to retire later this month. The episode comes at a time when the BJP-led State government is accelerating the process of filling up vacant promotional posts across departments as part of its commitment to provide two lakh government jobs to youths.

headline: Video of excavator at Sheshnag lake sparks concern; crime against Hinduism, says PDP leader
content: A video shared on social media, apparently by an excavator operator, has sparked widespread concerns over the alleged large-scale damage to the ecologically fragile Himalayan landscape in the Kashmir Valley. The video also shows the excavator dumping the soil on the shores of the high-altitude glacial lake of Sheshnag that sits at an altitude of 3,590 metres above the sea level. The video, originally shared by an Instagram account by the name 'Neeraj_excavator-lover', shows heavy earth excavators being used to create a road near the Sheshnag lake that falls on the trekking route from Pahalgam to the Amarnath cave shrine. Other video posts on the account show the excavators being used in the snowy mountains. The Sheshnag and its surroundings fall in the glacial region and is covered by snow for most part of the year. While the Instagram user has since deleted the video, it has gone viral on social media sparking concern and anger in the Valley. “This is a disaster. How such heavy machines reach our glaciers of Kashmir,” asked climate activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat in a post on X. “What is all this? Can anyone update?” Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) leader and spokesperson Mohit Bhan called it a “crime against Hindu faith”. “Sheshnag is not just another lake in the mountains of Kashmir. In Hinduism, it is the sacred landscape where Lord Shiva is believed to have left behind the serpents before proceeding towards the Amarnath Cave to narrate the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati,” Bhan said. “For generations, Hinduism has revered rivers, springs, lakes and mountains as sacred manifestations of nature. There is a profound contradiction in invoking Hindu faith while allowing the very landscape associated with that faith to be disturbed through unnecessary construction, road cutting and surface levelling,” he added. ‘Both faith and ecology demand protection’ Bhan said development should not come at an environmental cost. “What is being projected as development must not come at the cost of a fragile alpine ecosystem and a landscape deeply embedded in Hindu religious belief. Faith and ecology are not competing interests. Both demand protection,” he said. “You cannot celebrate the sanctity of a pilgrimage while disregarding the sanctity of the landscape through which it passes. If we cannot respect Sacred Sheshnag, what exactly are we preserving in the name of the Amarnath Yatra?” he asked. Valley’s chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq called the visuals “very disturbing”. He said, “With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm.” He said, “Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem. Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such ‘developmental projects’.” He said, “Our precious mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection not plunder, for now and for the future generations. So, this must be immediately stopped.” The excavations in high-altitude Himalayas, official sources said, are part of widening and stabilisation of the existing track that connects Chandanwari in Pahalgam to Amarnath cave. However, there has been no official word from the government over the use of excavators in such an eco-fragile zone. Sheshnag is an oligotrophic lake that can be reached from Pahalagam by a 23-kilometer trek from Chandanwari. The alpine lake, which is fed by the glaciers, is one-kilometre long and 0.7-kilometre wide.

headline: India's new GDP series brings demand, supply estimates closer: RBI DG Gupta
content: The new gross domestic product (GDP) series has narrowed the gap between estimates derived from the demand and supply sides of the economy, addressing a key limitation of the earlier series, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said on Monday. Under the previous series, the two estimates did not always align, with the resulting discrepancy at times being large and volatile. The revised series brings them together through a supply-use table framework, resulting in a much closer alignment of nominal GDP estimates. “In the earlier series, GDP estimates from the demand and supply sides did not always align. The resulting gap was reported separately as a discrepancy, and it could at times be large and volatile,” Gupta said. “The new series brings the two sides together through the supply-use table framework. As a result, nominal GDP estimates from both sides align much more closely. A small gap may still persist in real terms because the two sides are deflated differently, but it is much narrower than before,” she said. The revised national accounts series, with 2022-23 as the base year, replacing 2011-12, incorporates a wider range of surveys and administrative data. It also uses double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture, in line with international best practices. Gupta said the revision reflected the changes in the Indian economy over the past decade. “The new series reflects an economy that has become larger, more diversified and more complex since the base was last revised in 2011-12,” she said. On the demand side, private final consumption expenditure estimates now use shares from the more recent Household Consumption Expenditure Survey. Gross fixed capital formation has also been mapped to the sector investing in each asset, whether public, private, corporate or household. “One can now assess not just how much is being invested, but also how much is being invested and in what,” Gupta said. The changes are expected to improve the assessment of growth drivers and make early estimates more stable, with smaller revisions across successive data releases. “This has improved our ability to analyse, forecast and explain the drivers of economic growth from both the demand and supply sides,” she said. Early GDP estimates, which rely on proxy indicators and provisional information, are an important input into monetary policy, Gupta said. “The improvements in the new series are expected to make estimates more stable across successive vintages, with smaller revisions. This, in turn, will support better-calibrated and more stable policy, particularly monetary policy,” she said. Gupta also highlighted the changes in the consumer price index (CPI), saying the revised series would better reflect evolving household consumption patterns and improve inflation measurement. The new CPI series uses the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey of 2023-24 instead of the 2011-12 survey. It follows the United Nations’ Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018, allowing for a more detailed classification of consumption. The revised methodology includes better handling of missing data, particularly for seasonal items, and changes in the way household indices are combined. Housing is now covered in rural areas, while prices from 12 online markets are being collected for the first time. “As the share of online consumption grows, this will matter for how we read price signals,” Gupta said. The expanded coverage also includes item-level indices for rural, urban and combined sectors, as well as all states and Union Territories. This would help policymakers assess whether price pressures were concentrated in particular regions or were more widespread. “These revisions should narrow the disconnect between measured and perceived inflation and add value to the conduct of monetary policy under our inflation-targeting framework,” she said. Gupta said a base revision was not merely a technical exercise but an important tool for understanding structural changes in the economy. “A base revision is not merely a routine technical update. It records important shifts in the structure of the economy, its evolving sectoral composition, changing household consumption behaviour, the segments that are growing rapidly, the organisation of economic activity and the sources of growth,” she said. “Better measurement of all these shifts is important for policymaking,” she added. The revisions to GDP and CPI are expected to strengthen the RBI's assessment of economic conditions and improve the calibration of monetary policy, particularly by making early estimates more stable and inflation readings less volatile. Gupta said monetary policy decisions depended on an assessment of both current conditions and projections. Early estimates, which rely on proxy indicators and provisional information, were therefore an important input into the policy process. The improved GDP series is expected to reduce the extent of revisions across successive estimates, allowing policymakers to work with a more stable assessment of growth. “The improvements in the new series are expected to make estimates more stable across successive vintages, with smaller revisions. This, in turn, will support better-calibrated and more stable policy, particularly monetary policy,” Gupta said. The revised CPI, meanwhile, is expected to make headline inflation less volatile and the policy process less uncertain. The RBI uses inflation data alongside growth indicators to assess the evolving macroeconomic outlook. Gupta said the changes in the CPI would help the central bank better understand price pressures across regions and consumption categories, while narrowing the gap between measured and perceived inflation. “These revisions should narrow the disconnect between measured and perceived inflation and add value to the conduct of monetary policy under our inflation-targeting framework,” she said.

headline: Skill-based education from class 6 aims to create cheap labour: AIDSO
content: KALABURAGI The Karnataka State Committee of the All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) has opposed the State Government’s decision to introduce skill-based education, including electrical work, plumbing, beauty and wellness, agriculture and horticulture, from class 6 in government schools. World needs skilled youth, not merely degree-holders, says PM Modi storyline 1 AIDSO alleged that the government’s move was anti-poor and based on an unscientific approach to education. It questioned the rationale that nearly 40% of students leave education at the SSLC and pre-university levels, and seek employment, but remain unemployed due to a lack of vocational skills. The organisation argued that instead of creating a supportive environment and providing opportunities to enable children from economically weaker sections to continue their education, the government was seeking to push them away from mainstream education at an early stage. It alleged that the initiative amounted to implementing the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, introduced by the previous BJP government, which, according to AIDSO, undermined public education and the broader purpose of education. The organisation claimed that while children from affluent families would continue to attend private schools and study core subjects, such as mathematics and science to prepare for higher education, children from poorer backgrounds would be diverted towards vocational training in the name of skill development. This, it alleged, would eventually create a supply of cheap labour for corporate companies. AIDSO further alleged that the government’s move was linked to the conditions attached to a ₹2,000-crore results-based loan obtained from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for implementing the Karnataka Public Schools (KPS) scheme. Questioning the need to introduce vocational skills at such an early stage, the organisation asked what specific vocational training had been imparted to eminent personalities such as engineer Sir M. Visvesvaraya and scientist C.V. Raman during their school education. AIDSO urged the government to abandon what it termed an attempt to sideline substantive education in the name of skill development. It also appealed to students, parents and educationists to oppose the move and strengthen its campaign, ‘Save Public Education’. The statement was issued by AIDSO district president Tuljaram N.K. and district secretary Venkatesh Devadurga.

headline: Bisleri water unsafe? What the company just said about FSSAI concerns
content: Bisleri International said Monday that its water continues to be “safe for consumption", after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against the packaged drinking water brand over an 'unsafe' sample. It also said it has not received any notice from the food regulator so far. This comes a day after FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd over "unsafe packaged drinking water". The prosecution followed a water sample that failed quality tests for bromate and, after the company's appeal, polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), both of which pose potential health risks. Initially, the sample failed to meet the prescribed bromate limits. After the company appealed, a food laboratory re-tested it and detected PAHs, again finding it unsafe. The sample was then declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The company, on the other hand, stated that the results pertained to only one batch of water produced at its manufacturing facility in Goa nearly 14 months ago, in September 2025. This plant is one of 143 facilities operated by the company. FSSAI drew six samples there on 30 September 2025. Five passed all checks, while the sixth showed bromate at 12 micrograms per litre, above the permitted 10, according to the company's statement. Bisleri said it appealed in November 2025, and FSSAI sent the sample to a referral laboratory. That lab found bromate within the limit but flagged polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). The mismatch, Bisleri said, "raised questions that Bisleri believed warranted clarification." The company then had the same sample tested at an FSSAI-approved lab, which also found bromate within the limit. Bisleri sent those results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office on 2 February 2026, the statement read. What followed, according to Bisleri, was silence. "We received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed," the company said. It added that it has received no notice by email or hard copy and has not been able to find the reported notice on FSSAI's website. Bisleri said it runs over 90 tests across a 10-step manufacturing process and will keep cooperating with the regulator. "Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri," the statement said, concluding that the brand "remains safe for consumption." While the findings concern only one sample and do not amount to a judicial conviction necessarily, they raise wider concerns about packaged drinking water quality in India, where 333 of 1,300 samples tested in 2023-24 were found non-conforming. FSSAI also sanctioned prosecution against Vasant Masala, Tit-Bit Foods India, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery, and suspended the licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance.

headline: JKSSB cheating case: 20 accused arrested, including six government employees, as investigation widens
content: As per reports, 20 people, including six government employees, have been arrested in connection with an alleged organised cheating racket during the Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board (JKSSB) Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination. The alleged malpractice took place on November 15, with investigators uncovering a network that reportedly attempted to help selected candidates clear the examination through unfair means.Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Jammu, Joginder Singh, disclosed the details during a press conference. He said the accused had allegedly used online platforms, including Google and Facebook, to learn techniques for cheating in the examination. The investigation also revealed the alleged involvement of an insider at an examination centre who facilitated the transfer of a question paper outside the venue.Six additional arrests after initial actionAccording to the SSP, police initially arrested 14 accused on November 15. Subsequently, a Special Investigation Team (SIT) continued the investigation and arrested six more individuals, taking the total number of arrests to 20.The alleged mastermind, who is also a government employee, reportedly devised the plan to secure the selection of a close relative and a friend through unfair means. Investigators are examining the involvement of other individuals in the alleged network.How the alleged cheating operation workedAccording to the investigation, another accused allegedly established a separate network and approached around 20 to 22 additional candidates. He reportedly collected their original documents and obtained blank cheques from four to five candidates, with an understanding that payments would be made after they cleared the examination.Investigators also found that an insider deployed at the examination centre allegedly obtained a question paper from the desk of an absentee candidate shortly after the examination began.The paper was reportedly handed over to an accomplice waiting outside the centre. The accomplice allegedly took it to his car, photographed the questions and returned the paper to the examination venue for deposit.The photographs were subsequently circulated through a Telegram group to help selected candidates attempt the examination using the leaked questions.SSP Joginder Singh stated that the alleged arrangement was intended to assist candidates appearing at a particular examination centre.JK Students Association seeks CBI investigationMeanwhile, the Jammu and Kashmir Students Association (JKSA) has written to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, seeking intervention into the alleged examination malpractice.The association has demanded an independent investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), postponement of upcoming examinations and a comprehensive institutional review of the JKSSB.The investigation into the alleged cheating network is continuing, with the arrests bringing the involvement of government employees and other individuals under scrutiny.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. headline: Street plays to promote co-existence between humans and wildlife organised in Kotagiri
content: UDHAGAMANDALAM Street plays to promote peaceful co-existence between humans and wildlife were organised in Kotagiri and Kattabettu forest ranges in the Nilgiris forest divisions recently. The street plays were organised by Keystone Foundation in collaboration with the Forest Department. The two-day human-wildlife interaction awareness programme included street plays performed by Aayudham Foundation, Coimbatore, which ‘presented a series of engaging street plays to raise awareness among local communities about reducing negative interactions between humans and wildlife,’ a press release stated. The performances focused on the importance of peaceful coexistence with wildlife, particularly species such as sloth bears, leopards, tigers and elephants and practices that can be adopted by human communities to minimise negative interactions with wildlife. Key themes of the plays included understanding wildlife behaviour, avoiding encounters with wild animals, responsible waste disposal and the role of improper waste management in attracting wildlife towards human settlements. Through interactive and culturally engaging performances, the street plays highlighted how everyday human activities can influence wildlife movement and contribute to human–wildlife conflict. The programme also encouraged villagers to adopt responsible practices, remain alert and work collectively towards creating safer environments for both people and wildlife, the release added. A total of six street plays were conducted across the two forest ranges. Through the medium of street theatre, the initiative aimed to strengthen community awareness, encourage responsible behaviour and promote harmonious coexistence between local communities and wildlife, it added.

headline: Uttar Pradesh farm exports at ₹25,000 cr; industry seeks commodity boards
content: The agro industry has called for crop-specific commodity boards to boost agricultural exports from Uttar Pradesh, India’s leading producer of agricultural and horticultural crops. The state’s agricultural and allied exports are currently estimated at ₹25,000 crore, with meat accounting for a bulk of the shipments. Despite producing more than 73 million tonnes (mt) of agricultural output and 60 mt of horticultural produce, Uttar Pradesh's farm exports remain concentrated in rice, sugar, spices and buffalo meat. “Uttar Pradesh has a massive farm sector profile and a high export potential. Sadly, it lags in agro exports and instead needs institutional support,” said M J Khan, advisor to the Indian Chamber of Food and Agriculture (ICFA) and its former chairman. He called for commodity boards to promote horticultural exports from the state, a leading producer of potatoes, paddy, sugarcane, wheat and dairy products. Gujarat, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh are currently among the country’s leading agricultural exporting states. Uttar Pradesh Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Horticulture, Agriculture Exports, Marketing and Foreign Trade Dinesh Pratap Singh had earlier said the government was considering setting up state-level horticultural commodity boards on the lines of the Spices Board of India. At a recent roadshow in New Delhi, Additional Chief Secretary (Food Processing) B L Meena said closer collaboration between farmers and industry could help processors source produce locally while giving farmers reliable access to buyers. Invest UP Chief Executive Officer Vijay Kiran Anand said the state was emerging as a major hub for food processing and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) investments, supported by infrastructure, sector-specific investor facilitation and an expanding manufacturing ecosystem. “With its vast agricultural resources, skilled workforce and growing industrial clusters, Uttar Pradesh offers immense potential for investment, value addition and employment generation,” he added. Meanwhile, ICFA will host its flagship AgroTech 2026 in Lucknow from December 3 to 5. Delegates from 25 countries, including the US, Australia, Canada, Brazil, the Netherlands, the UK, the UAE, Malaysia, Morocco, Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, New Zealand, Ghana, Singapore and Thailand, are expected to attend. Diplomats from more than 15 embassies will also participate to explore opportunities for international agricultural cooperation, trade and investment. The fourth Uttar Pradesh State Agriculture Summit, being held as part of AgroTech 2026, will be inaugurated by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari on December 4. It will focus on agricultural policy, investment, infrastructure, agribusiness development, exports and strengthening farmer-industry partnerships.

headline: Karnataka Ministers, MLAs should stay in farmers’ homes during Belagavi legislature session to cut costs: Farmers’ outfit
content: MYSURU The Federation of Karnataka Farmers’ Organisations has offered to arrange accommodation in farmers’ homes for Ministers, legislators and officials during the upcoming Legislature session in Belagavi as part of an effort to reduce government expenditure. Federation president Kurubur Shanthakumar has made the offer in an appeal addressed to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the presiding officers of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council, and the leaders of the Congress, BJP and JD(S) legislature parties. Mr. Shanthakumar has suggested that Ministers, MLAs and officials stay in farmers’ homes instead of hotels during the session, citing the financial constraints faced by the State Government in implementing its welfare schemes. He said farmers were concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought. Moral support “Although we are not in a position to provide financial assistance for the implementation of government schemes during these difficult times, we are capable of extending moral support. With this in mind, we, the farmers, have decided to extend our support to the MLAs and officials during this year’s Belagavi session,” he said. Pointing out that the government spends substantial amounts on hotel accommodation and other facilities for legislators and officials during every session, Mr. Shanthakumar appealed for a reduction in such expenditure. “We invite Ministers, MLAs, officials and government employees to stay in the homes of farming families instead of hotels,” he said. Hundreds of farming families were ready to host the elected representatives and officials, and the farmers themselves would bear the expenses of their hospitality, including food and other arrangements, he said. “This would help the government save the substantial amounts otherwise spent on hotel accommodation and preserve those funds in the State exchequer. Staying in farmers’ homes would also enable legislators to understand their problems first-hand and facilitate meaningful discussions during the Assembly session, paving the way for appropriate solutions,” he said. Over weekend Mr. Shanthakumar also suggested that the Legislature conduct proceedings over the weekends instead of allowing legislators to return to their respective hometowns. He proposed extending the daily sitting by two hours to make the session more productive and reduce additional expenditure. He said farmers, as providers of food, were prepared to stand by the government during difficult financial circumstances. Mysuru growers question sugarcane pricing announced in Belagavi district Mysuru growers question sugarcane pricing announced in Belagavi district Mysuru growers question sugarcane pricing announced in Belagavi district storyline 1 Recalling the recent protests by farmers demanding a State Advised Price (SAP) for sugarcane, enhanced compensation for drought-related crop losses and a waiver of agricultural loans, Mr. Shanthakumar said the government had declined to concede to their demands, citing the additional financial burden. Farmers were, however, conscious of the Chief Minister’s predicament and were making the appeal in that spirit, he added.

headline: T.N. BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran condemns alleged caste discrimination at Ariyalur government school
content: CHENNAI BJP State president Nainar Nagenthran on Monday (November 23, 2026) condemned an alleged incident of human excreta being placed on the table of a laboratory assistant belonging to a Scheduled Caste at a government school near Jayankondam in Ariyalur district. In a social media post, Mr. Nagenthran said the incident, which reportedly took place on November 10, and the alleged caste discrimination were was shocking. The BJP leader alleged that attempts had been made to destroy evidence before the arrival of education department officials and that efforts had been made to close the issue by merely transferring the staff concerned. Recalling the Vengaivayal incident [in 2022], he alleged that caste atrocities continued under the TVK government, just as they had under the erstwhile DMK regime. Mr. Nagenthran further demanded an explanation from the School Education Minister over the alleged delay in the police investigation and urged the police to arrest those responsible and take stringent action against them.

headline: Telangana govt seeks 12-month gap in crop loan repayment for farmers in drought-hit mandals
content: HYDERABAD The Telangana Government has asked the banks to consider a 12-month moratorium and extension of total repayment period to 60 months including moratorium, for borrowers in the 111 mandals severely affected by drought across the State. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/banks-in-telangana-achieved-74-of-kharif-loan-targets-in-h1/article71686919.ece Moratorium of 12 months and extension of total repayment period by 36 months should be considered for 254 moderately affected mandals. Banks were asked to identify eligible accounts on suo-motu basis to initiate available relief process without waiting for borrowers to approach them, through a suitable communication to the borrowers wherever deemed fit. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/telangana-declares-365-mandals-drought-affected-of-which-111-severely-drought-affected/article71632836.ece The banks should also make available option for borrowers to opt out of the resolution plan at any point till the end of 135 days from the date of declaration of calamity on October 24. The State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC), which met under the chairmanship of Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, recently had resolved to sanction additional need-based finance to eligible affected farmers to address financial stress and restoration and continuation of productive activities. This will be subject to borrower wise viability assessment, projected cash flows and respective approved policies of the respective banks’ boards. It has also resolved to ensure that insurance proceeds, if any, should be adjusted towards the restructured accounts in cases where fresh loans have been granted to the borrowers. Banks could, however, consider restructuring and sanctioning fresh loans without waiting for the actual receipt of the claim. The SLBC has requested the State Government to take up with the Central Government the issue of extending interest subvention benefit in rescheduled crop loans affected by drought till the repayment term ends as it will benefit farmers. headline: India-Nepal weekly train: Check stations, timings and more about Ayodhya-Janakpur Saryu-Kamala Express

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh to Janakpur in Nepal, from Delhi on Monday (November 23, 2026). The weekly cross-border train service is scheduled for joint inauguration during Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India on November 22-23. headline: One held for sexually assaulting minor girl on train in Keralam
content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The Railway Police took a 22-year-old man into custody for allegedly sexually assaulting a minor girl aboard the Rajya Rani Express near the Thiruvananthapuram North Railway Station in the early hours of Monday (November 23, 2026). The accused, identified as Aravind, who hails from Edava near Varkala, allegedly misbehaved with the 16-year-old girl as she was coming out of the train’s washroom. Five held for alleged abduction and gang rape of woman in Keralam Five held for alleged abduction and gang rape of woman in Keralam A special investigation team under the direction of Thrissur City Police Commissioner arrest the gang, which includes a woman, in connection with the incident that happened on September 22 Five held for alleged abduction and gang rape of woman in Keralam storyline 1 According to official sources, the girl raised an alarm after the purported crime, following which her family and fellow passengers rushed to her assistance, caught hold of the accused and handed him over to the Railway Police after the train reached the station. headline: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre warns of possible misuse of WhatsApp Web sessions
content: CHENNAI The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, has warned WhatsApp users about the possible misuse of authenticated web sessions to gain unauthorised access to their accounts. In an advisory, the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) of the I4C said a malicious person could exploit an active WhatsApp Web session to read private messages, send messages by impersonating the account holder, access contacts and group conversations, and misuse the user’s trusted identity for fraud, phishing and other cybercrimes. Over 3,000 cases of WhatsApp hacking scam reported in T.N. Over 3,000 cases of WhatsApp hacking scam reported in T.N. The scammers trick a target into revealing the 6-digit SMS or in-app code that WhatsApp sends during login; it is typically done by phone calls or chat messages in the guise of tech support Over 3,000 cases of WhatsApp hacking scam reported in T.N. storyline 1 The unit has asked users to exercise caution while accessing WhatsApp Web, particularly on office computers, shared systems, public computers and devices that may be accessible to others. It recommended users to avoid exchanging government-related, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web mode on computers. Users have also been advised against keeping their accounts permanently logged in and to manually log out after every session. Closing window not enough Simply closing the browser window or tab should not be considered sufficient to terminate an authenticated session, the advisory said. Where using WhatsApp Web was unavoidable, the users were advised to opt for ‘Incognito’ or ‘Private Browsing’ mode on trusted computers and log out manually before closing the browser. Logging in from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres and borrowed or otherwise untrusted systems should be avoided. Also read: WhatsApp to simplify communication on app, add financial services https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/technology/whatsapp-to-simplify-communication-on-app-add-financial-services/article71688497.ece The unit also urged WhatsApp users to remain alert to unusual account activity. Unexpected messages sent from user accounts or unexplained replies from contacts should be viewed seriously. The advisory called for keeping operating systems, browsers and security software updated. Users were advised to avoid suspicious downloads, unknown files and untrusted software. Institutions or organisations were advised to avoid using WhatsApp Web in official and sensitive work environments.

headline: FSSAI Suspends Licences Of Five Nutraceutical Makers
content: Food regulator FSSAI on Monday said it has suspended the licences of five nutraceutical and health product makers for serious violations. In a social media post, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) informed that it has suspended the licences of Vedant Remedies, Lucid Healthcare Pvt Ltd, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare, Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals and Adorreal Healthcare for various violations, including poor hygiene and damaged infrastructure. "FSSAI has suspended the license of several nutraceutical and health product manufacturers for serious food safety and regulatory violations," the regulator said. FSSAI said it remains committed to safeguarding public health through strict vigilance and enforcement of food safety standards.Earlier this month, FSSAI took action against six nutraceutical manufacturers for various violations. "Regulatory action initiated, including suspension of FSSAI licenses for serious food safety violations," it has said. The six companies against whom the action was initiated are -- Airen Herbals, Aquabliss Lifesciences, Raskam Healthcare, Supercure Biotech, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare and Vedant Remedies.During the current calendar year, FSSAI has increased enforcement action against food business operators (FBOs) as well as e-commerce companies as part of its efforts to provide safe food to people. It has cracked down against alcoholic beverage and energy drink makers.
