headline: Messi Keralam Visit Controversy: Sports Minister Says SIT Probe Progressing, Calls For Strict Action Over
content: Thiruvananthapuram (Keralam) [India], November 23: Keralam Sports Minister OJ Janeesh has said the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe into alleged financial irregularities surrounding the proposed visit of football icon Lionel Messi to the state is progressing effectively, calling for a strict investigation into everyone involved in the transactions.Sports Minister Highlights Serious Allegations"The Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigation into the scam involving the promise of bringing Messi to Keralam is progressing effectively. The investigation conducted by the Sports Department has brought out only limited details. The allegations raised against the Sports Council President are serious. The agreement was signed before receiving government approval. Even before the government's permission was obtained, a person representing the government signed as a witness. The then Sports Council President signed the agreement as if it were part of their official responsibility. Meanwhile, it is alleged that money was transferred to their account. Let a detailed investigation take place into this matter," Janeesh told the reporters."The government has not interfered in the investigation in any way. An effective and transparent investigation is underway. The RBC should provide whatever evidence it can as part of the investigation. The investigation was announced after it came to the government's notice that several irregularities had taken place in connection with this issue. There was political ownership behind it. Political directions led to such an agreement. It was the then Chief Minister who repeatedly and firmly announced that Messi would come to Keralam," he added.Minister Rejects Claims Of Investigation DelayJaneesh also rejected suggestions that the investigation had been delayed, stressing that the alleged financial transactions and the involvement of those who facilitated them needed to be examined."I do not agree with the opinion that there was a delay in the investigation. There was a political and policy-level decision behind the transfer of money. The main question is whether anyone used the government to carry out private financial transactions. If so, a strict investigation is necessary. Everyone who supported or facilitated such transactions must come under the purview of the investigation," he said.Chief Minister Addresses Financial IrregularitiesThe controversy surrounding Messi's visit has seen fresh developments, with Keralam Chief Minister VD Satheesan earlier stating that the Sports Department had completed its examination of the matter and that the government would take action based on its recommendations.Satheesan had said the alleged irregularities had caused a loss of more than Rs 22 crore to the state exchequer. He also confirmed that the GST Department had constituted a Special Investigation Team to probe the alleged GST fraud linked to the proposed visit.Lionel Messi Throws Ball At Gonzalo Tapia's Face, Gets Yellow Card As Inter Miami Suffer Humiliating 3-0 Defeat | Video"The examination related to the issue has been completed, and a decision will be taken soon based on the complaint submitted by the Sports Department Secretary. The inquiry has been completed, and recommendations on the action to be taken will be sent to the concerned department," Satheesan had said.Messi's Proposed Keralam Visit PostponedThe controversy relates to a proposed visit by Messi and the Argentina men's football team to Keralam for a friendly match. The fixture, which was expected to be held at the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium in Kochi, was postponed after sponsors cited delays in obtaining FIFA permission.Also Watch:The proposed visit did not materialise, with Messi subsequently travelling to India as part of the 'GOAT India Tour', visiting Kolkata, Hyderabad, Mumbai and New Delhi, but not Keralam.Questions Raised Over Private AgreementSatheesan had also questioned the process through which a private company was allowed to enter into an agreement with the Argentine Football Association (AFA) for the proposed tour, raising concerns over whether the company's financial capacity, source of funds and market value had been properly examined.The government has maintained that it would take appropriate action following the completion of the inquiry into the alleged financial and procedural irregularities.Level up your brain the fun way. headline: IIT Madras expands campus health services with new autism, sleep research facilities
content: The Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT) Madras has announced three new healthcare initiatives on its campus: an autism lab to study an integrated therapy for children with autism, a dedicated facility for sleep assessment and research, and an electric ambulance service for emergency medical assistance. The facilities were inaugurated by Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava, with the initiatives being part of the institute's broader wellness programme and are intended to expand access to healthcare for students, faculty and staff, while also supporting research into medical conditions and healthcare technologies, the IIT said in a statement. The new sleep study facility, located at the institute's campus health centre, will provide specialised assessment, consultation and treatment through experts associated with a private hospital in Chennai. It follows concerns around sleep deprivation identified through the institute's existing mental health support services. IIT Madras said its mental health services, established with assistance the private chain of hospitals will provide access to counsellors, clinical psychologists and psychiatrists. A separate 24-hour counselling service is also being operated. Also Read | India to set up offshore IIT campus, startup hub in Nepal Beyond consultations and treatment, the sleep facility will support research into sleep patterns and different categories of sleep disorders. Such studies will be conducted subject to approval from the Institutional Ethics Committee and informed consent from participants. The Department of Medical Science and Technology will also explore the development of indigenous and affordable sensors and technologies for sleep monitoring and analysis. The autism lab is part of the proposed activities of the Centre for Indian Medical Knowledge (CIMK), which aims to scientifically study traditional Indian medical practices. IIT Madras plans to work with the Paediatric Neurology team at AIIMS Jodhpur to evaluate Integrated Varmam Therapy for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Also Read | Curious about AI, aerospace or cybersecurity? IIT Madras has 20 courses for school students According to the institute, AIIMS Jodhpur has shared its clinical experience of administering the integrated therapy to more than 800 children. The proposed collaboration will involve exchanging clinical expertise and research findings to develop evidence-based practices. The institute said the research will be subject to the required ethical approvals. IIT Madras researchers will also develop indigenous pressure-sensing gloves to measure contact pressure and provide real-time feedback to practitioners, helping them follow prescribed treatment parameters. The research plan also includes genetic, molecular and epigenetic studies to investigate possible mechanisms underlying the therapy and examine their correlation with clinical outcomes. The third initiative, an e-ambulance service, is intended to improve emergency response and patient transport within the campus, particularly for elderly people and those requiring immediate assistance. It will supplement the institute's existing fleet of two small ambulances and one fully equipped ambulance.

headline: Revised GDP, CPI Data To Help RBI Make Better Policy Decisions: Poonam Gupta
content: Mumbai: The revised GDP, Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) series will help the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) assess economic conditions more accurately and make better-informed monetary policy decisions, RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said.Speaking at a conference organised by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Gupta said the revised statistical series capture the structural changes in the Indian economy, including evolving consumption patterns, changing sectoral contributions and new sources of growth.She highlighted that the revised GDP series, with 2022-23 as the base year, incorporates wider surveys, administrative data and double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture. The changes are expected to improve the reliability of growth estimates and reduce revisions in successive data releases.Gupta said more stable GDP estimates would support better-calibrated monetary policy, as the RBI relies on early economic indicators and provisional data while assessing growth and inflation trends.'Look At India': Trump Cites 7% GDP Growth, Says US Could Achieve 20% GDP With Lower Interest Rates, Calls Fed Policy 'A Sad Thing' | Video On inflation measurement, she pointed to the updated CPI series, which uses the 2023-24 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey to determine consumption weights instead of the older 2011-12 data. The revised basket reflects changing household spending patterns, with a shift in the relative importance of food and non-food items.The new CPI series also incorporates prices from 12 online markets for the first time, reflecting the growing role of digital consumption. It excludes free public distribution system items and employer-provided and government accommodation from the relevant calculations, while expanding house rent coverage to rural areas. Gupta said these changes would help narrow the gap between measured and perceived inflation and provide more detailed information on price movements across regions.The revised IIP series has also increased the weight of technology- and consumption-oriented sectors, including motor vehicles, pharmaceuticals and electronics, while reducing the weight of sectors such as petroleum products and mining.She said better-quality economic data was crucial for understanding the changing economy and strengthening policy decisions.

headline: Central, Delhi government offices to remain closed on September 11 amid BRICS Summit
content: Offices of the Central and Delhi governments will remain closed on September 11 in view of the security and logistical arrangements for the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, officials said on Thursday. The decision has been taken to minimise inconvenience to the public amid restrictions related to the movement of motorcades and other Summit-related arrangements in the national capital. The Delhi government had earlier declared September 11 a holiday for its offices. The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions has now issued a circular declaring a holiday for Central government offices in Delhi on the same day. Ahead of the international event, the Delhi Traffic Police has been conducting rehearsals to prepare for traffic movement during the Summit. As part of traffic management arrangements for events scheduled from September 11 to 13, traffic diversions have been planned at 22 points, while traffic movement will be regulated on more than 35 roads. On Wednesday, the Traffic Police imposed restrictions and diversions between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. as part of a motorcade rehearsal for the BRICS Business Forum and the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.

headline: FM holds 10th pre-Budget meeting with health, social sector stakeholders ahead of Budget
content: New Delhi [India], November 23 (ANI): Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday chaired the tenth pre-Budget consultation with experts and stakeholders from the health and social sectors in New Delhi as part of preparations for the Union Budget 2027-28.The meeting was also attended by Secretaries from the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, senior officials from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the Chief Economic Adviser to the Government of India.In the Union Budget 2026-27, the government allocated Rs 1,06,530.42 crore to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, marking an increase of 10 per cent over the previous revised estimates.Among the major healthcare allocations, the National Health Mission (NHM) received Rs 39,390 crore, while the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), which supports AIIMS and medical college upgrades, was allocated Rs 11,307 crore.The Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) received Rs 9,500 crore, while the allocation for the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) increased 67.66 per cent to Rs 4,770 crore.Alongside healthcare, the government had also provided significant funding for rural employment, housing and welfare programmes in the social sector in the previous Budget.With the latest meeting, the Finance Minister has so far completed ten rounds of pre-Budget consultations with experts and stakeholders across various sectors of the economy ahead of the forthcoming Budget.The consultation process began with leading economists, followed by representatives from agriculture, manufacturing, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and startups.Subsequent meetings covered capital markets, banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), the information technology sector, infrastructure, energy and sustainability.The ninth round was held with stakeholders from housing, urbanisation and culture, followed by the tenth consultation with representatives from the health and social sectors.The latest consultation forms part of the government's exercise to gather inputs from different stakeholders and sectors before finalising priorities for the Union Budget 2027-28.
