headline: Odisha government to launch household travel survey today to prepare BKPPER’s regional mobility plan
content: BHUBANESWAR: The state government will launch a household travel survey from Monday to prepare a Comprehensive Regional Mobility Plan (CRMP) for the ambitious Bhubaneswar-Kataka-Puri-Paradip Economic Region (BKPPER) plan, which aims to merge four major urban centres of Odisha into a single economic powerhouse by 2047.Housing and Urban Development department officials said the survey will assess everyday travel needs, commuting patterns and mobility challenges of people across the region. The findings will serve as an important foundation for developing an integrated, efficient, affordable and citizen-centric regional transport network to ensure seamless connectivity between key urban centres and emerging economic hubs.H&UD minister Krushna Chandra Mahapatra said the survey will capture information on people’s preferred modes of transport, journey duration, commuting expenditure, travel frequency, connectivity gaps and difficulties encountered during daily journeys. It will also provide an opportunity for citizens to share their views and suggestions on improving public transport services, road connectivity and other essential transport infrastructure.“Through our initiative #OdishaOnTheMove, we are working towards a transport system that is integrated, accessible, affordable and responsive to the needs of our citizens. The survey will help us understand people’s actual travel experiences and expectations,” he said, urging the households across the region to share their inputs.Additional chief secretary Usha Padhee said the data gathered through this exercise will provide valuable insights for evidence-based planning, better integration of different modes of transport and prioritisation of future investments. The exercise will be conducted through authorised enumerators visiting households as well as a digital survey facility, enabling citizens to participate conveniently by scanning the official QR code shared by the department..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Odisha government to place 3 Bills in Assembly today, Opposition likely to take part
content: BHUBANESWAR: The state government is likely to place three Bills in the Assembly on Monday even as steps are being taken to persuade the Opposition BJD and Congress to stop disruptions and participate in the proceedings.Sources said two Bills, the Odisha Repealing Bill 2026 and the Odisha Development Authorities (Amendment) Bill, 2026, pending since the last session, are likely to be placed and passed. The Industrial Service Validation of Appointment of Assistant Managers and Assistant Directors (Amendment) Bill, 2026 will also be introduced in the House. However, all depends on the BJD and Congress members who have stalled the proceedings during the last three days over the issues of mishandling of Ganjam floods and Kotia border dispute. CLP leader Rama Chandra Kadam alleged that the state government was not allowing discussion on Kotia issue despite Congress submitting a motion in this regard. He said that in the current situation, there is no other option before the Opposition members but to protest inside the House. “If government has nothing to hide, it should allow discussion by suspending all other business,” he added..Though BJD is yet to state its stance officially, several members believe that normalcy will return to the House. A senior party MLA told this paper that members want the House to run. On the issue of Ganjam floods, the BJD can corner the government through discussion more effectively than by disrupting the House, he said.Sources said the government is likely to reach out to the Opposition to bring normalcy to the House so that Bills can be passed. Parliamentary Affairs minister Mukesh Mahaling had announced that the state government will place five Bills during the session.Besides, the Assembly will also discuss and pass the budget of three important departments before the First Supplementary Bill for 2026-27 is passed on November 30..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: State Transformation Commission meeting: Yogi says policy benefits for private sector should reach youth | Hindustan Times
content: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday said the direct benefits of investor-friendly policies, concessions and subsidies for the private sector should reach the state’s youth and the general public to the maximum extent. He also directed officials to ensure that all infrastructure, industrial development and public welfare projects are completed by adhering to quality within stipulated timelines.He was reviewing ongoing and proposed development projects and public welfare schemes at a State Transformation Commission meeting.“Along with various facilities including tax concessions and subsidies to industries, the private sector and investors, the government has ensured that the interests of people of the state remain at the centre of every government policy, decision and provision,” he said.Reviewing the honorarium payments of 3,10,437 outsourced personnel deployed in 88 departments of the state, he said, “It must be ensured under all circumstances that every employee receives the enhanced honorarium in full and on time.”During a review of expressway projects, officials informed the CM that the tendering process for the Chitrakoot Link Expressway would be finalised by November 30. Acquisition of 91.46% land required for the Farrukhabad Link Expressway has been completed and the Letter of Award (LOA) has been issued to the selected firm, the officials added.Similarly, 82.98% of land for the Agra-Lucknow-Purvanchal Link Expressway, 86.04% of the Jhansi Link Expressway, and 83.45% for the Jewar Link Expressway have been acquired and LOAs have also been issued to the firms selected for construction of all three projects.Verification work for the Meerut-Haridwar, Vindhya Expressway and Vindhya-Purvanchal Spur has been completed, and land rates have also been approved in most districts, officials said. Instructions were issued to initiate land acquisition at the earliest.Reviewing industrial development projects, the chief minister directed that financial bids for tenders received for the Multi-Modal Logistics Hub in Greater Noida be opened within the next two weeks and that further action on the Multi-Modal Logistics Park be expedited.Taking stock of public welfare schemes, the chief minister laid special emphasis on connecting 12.50 lakh families identified under the ‘Zero Poverty Scheme’ with basic facilities. Officials informed the chief minister that 59,447 PM/CM houses had been sanctioned for eligible families.The chief minister directed officers that workers should be provided with labour cards, Ayushman cards, subsidised meals and free medicines on the spot.Instructions were issued to complete 279 public works department projects costing more than ₹50 crore each, with a total cost of ₹47,248 crore, within the stipulated timelines.Expressing satisfaction with the completion of repairs on 50,189 kilometers (91%) of roads against the target of 54,878 kilometers under the pothole-free roads campaign, the chief minister directed that the remaining roads be made pothole-free immediately.

headline: Government takes note of JKSSB ‘exam cheating’, action to follow, says advisor to Omar | Hindustan Times
content: The Jammu and Kashmir government has taken cognisance of the cheating controversy in recruitment examinations by the J&K Services Selection Board (JKSSB), and strict action will follow, advisor to the chief minister Nasir Aslam Wani said.Wani said the government will soon come out with details of what actions will follow. He assured transparent exams and said students’ futures will not be compromised. “We are monitoring this issue and wherever action is needed, it will be taken. There will be no compromise with the career of the students,” he said.He said that the government can’t be held responsible for exam fraud cases before 2024 but in the latest case they are very much aware. “We won’t allow any such actions and every exam will be held with complete honesty and the confidence of the students will be restored,” he said.The controversy emerged when J&K Police busted a sophisticated cheating module during the finance assistant examination of JKSSB on November 15, raising doubts about the fairness of the whole examination. Four modules were allegedly caught with eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles were seized. JKSSB said that it was a standalone incident and the rest of the exam was not compromised.On Saturday, many aspirants sat in protest in Srinagar against the alleged rigging. Former Srinagar MP, Ruhullah Mehdi, also joined them who were later removed by police from the protest site.Peoples Democratic Party leader Iltija Mufti on Friday accused the JKSSB of colluding with the cheating mafia and indulging in examination frauds. Iltija alleged that since 2019, there have been constant instances of frauds in recruitment examinations particularly conducted by JKSSB.However, the JKSSB has issued a clarification saying that the accounts assistant examination was successfully held across all 20 districts of the Union territory and that the “isolated incident” involving an attempt to use unfair means did not compromise the examination process.

headline: Tamil Nadu: Teachers want senior principal to head collegiate education directorate
content: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu Government Collegiate Teachers’ Association has urged the state government to appoint a senior-most principal serving in a government arts and science college as the director of Collegiate Education, instead of an IAS officer.In a representation submitted to the chief minister, chief secretary, higher education minister and higher education department secretary, the association said the practice of appointing senior-most government college principals to head the directorate of collegiate education had been followed for nearly 30 years. Such appointments ensured the director has practical experience in the functioning and administration of colleges, it said.The practice was discontinued after a senior-most principal, who was serving as the DCE, was placed under suspension on administrative grounds on January 30, 2024. Thereafter, IAS officers were appointed to the post.Raising concerns over the present arrangement, the association said the current DCE, P Ponniah, has been on leave for the last three months, and the additional charge was assigned to another IAS officer, P Rathinasamy, currently the director of Technical Education.The association said earlier, when a principal headed the directorate, the additional charge during the incumbent’s leave was given to the joint director (Planning and Development) ensuring continuity in administration..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: It's time for monetary policy in India to act and contain inflationary expectations
content: With oil prices easing, bond yields softening, foreign inflows rising, and the rupee recovering sharply over the past few weeks, India’s macroeconomic outlook looks brighter than it did a few weeks ago. However, rising prices point to emerging stress points in the economy. The latest retail and wholesale inflation figures suggest that price pressures are piling up rapidly across economic sectors.

headline: After Malappuram teen’s ordeal, Kerlalam government targets unregulated beauty industry
content: KOZHIKODE: Behind the promise of glowing skin, flawless complexion and healthy hair, a largely unregulated beauty-products market thrives on social media, with thousands of homemade and little-known brands finding customers through Instagram and WhatsApp. Marketed as traditional ‘Muthassi’ (grandma’s) remedies or organic formulations, these products are now under the state government’s scanner after a teenager developed kidney damage allegedly following prolonged use of a fairness cream laced with mercury levels far exceeding the permissible limit. The government is now preparing to intensify its crackdown on the unregulated industry. Health Minister K Muraleedharan promised action against cosmetic products if complaints are received and stressed the need to regulate the creams sold online.“Government-approved creams are available in the market. Several other products, however, are being sold online. Consumers should check where these are manufactured and check their details before applying them to their skin. Applying creams does not necessarily make someone beautiful,” he said, adding that the government would consider measures to regulate the online sale of such products. An 18-year-old girl from Areekode, Malappuram, developed a serious kidney disorder allegedly after using the fairness cream, which she purchased through Instagram, for nearly a year. The FIR taken up by Areekode police on her complaint identified the product as ‘F tune face cream’. The police have recorded her statement and collected samples of the cream for tests.Interacting with reporters after giving her statement on Sunday, the girl said she would move against the manufacturer and seller legally. .“Several students in my class have also been using this cream. I have already suffered, and I do not want others to go through the same experience. Those currently using it should stop immediately,” she said, adding that although early detection helped her recover to some extent, her skin has already suffered damage and would require further treatment.The girl also said that the Instagram page through which the cream was marketed was no longer visible.‘Unlabelled fairness creams also a problem’Dermatologists warned that the problem was not restricted to mercury contamination. Dr Alisha Naha, consultant dermatologist at Aluer Skin Clinic, Kozhikode, said they frequently meet patients who developed adverse reactions after using unlabelled fairness creams. “These creams may show immediate results for the first one or two months. However, users subsequently begin developing side-effects and approach doctors. Side-effects can include skin thinning, telangiectasia (visible small blood vessels), uncontrollable acne, increased sensitivity to sunlight and itching,” she said.Dr Naha said absence of adequate regulatory oversight over products entering the Indian cosmetics market was a major concern. “Products can enter the market under descriptions such as homemade, handmade, natural or organic, without necessarily establishing safety. Consumers are particularly vulnerable when products do not carry proper ingredient lists,” she said. She also pointed to counterfeits of international cosmetic brands sold online, often packaged to resemble original products and offered at discounted prices.Dr Irfan Ahmed, a nephrologist from Malappuram, recalled a case in which a 47-year-old woman developed persistent swelling in both legs and feet. Tests revealed proteinuria and a kidney biopsy revealed membranous nephropathy, in which damage to the kidney’s filtering membranes causes protein to leak into the urine. .The woman later disclosed that she had been using a beauty cream, recommended by a local chemist, for two years, as she was unhappy with her complexion. She noticed dark patches on her forearms and discontinued its use following advice from a dermatologist. “This is not a lone case. Hundreds of victims have already sought treatment for these instant cosmetic solutions,” Dr Ahmed said.Fairness cream use leaves Mappila song singer with kidney diseaseKozhikode: Popular Mappila song singer Saleem Kodathur has revealed that he developed a serious kidney disease after using a fairness cream allegedly containing excessive levels of mercury. In a startling disclosure, the singer said he was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, the same kidney condition that recently affected a teen girl, allegedly following the use of a mercury-laden fairness cream. Saleem said he started using the fairness cream on a friend’s recommendation. The product appeared to deliver quick results, with a noticeable change in his complexion within a few days. However, the initial improvement was short-lived, and his facial skin subsequently became darker than it had been before he started using the cream. What appeared to be a cosmetic concern soon developed into a serious health crisis as he began experiencing complications and underwent numerous medical examinations to identify the cause of his deteriorating condition. He said he had undergone almost every possible medical test for several months before doctors could establish the cause of his illness. Recounting the severity of his condition, the singer said his immune system had become severely compromised as the disease progressed. The prolonged illness also affected his professional commitments, forcing him to postpone musical programmes for several months. Although his health has improved following treatment, Saleem said he was yet to regain his normal sleeping pattern. He also revealed that he had to completely avoid several food items because of the illness and its impact on his health.Lab confirms high Mercury contentA test by a private lab in Chennai confirmed mercury content in the cream used by the teen at 1.25%, equivalent to 12,500 parts per million (ppm). India’s Cosmetics Rules, 2020, fix the permissible limit for unintentional mercury in finished cosmetic products, other than those intended for the eye area, at 1 pm. The mercury concentration in the tested cream is 12,500 times the permissible limit..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: ‘Warnings ignored, policy apathy fuels landslides in Nilgiris’
content: Landslides are not new to the Nilgiris. They have, during the annual monsoon, become recurring phenomena, finding new vulnerable avenues each time to devastate the hills. The Burliyar tragedy that detached the district from the rest of the country during the first spell of this year’s northeast monsoon was not unprecedented.The subsequent mudslips were foreseeable too. These were perhaps disasters deferred for a few years. As the climate crisis intensifies, measures to prevent such incidents remain transient. Sadly, accountability in disaster management remains arbitrarily restricted to only rescue, rehabilitation and indemnity.In the Nilgiris, considering the history of landslides dating back to being recorded for the first time in 1824, the causes, intensity and impact have changed with ‘development’ outgrowing ‘conservation’. The ghats opening up from the eastern and south eastern slopes have been particularly susceptible. The 1881 landslides wreaked havoc at multiple points from Mettupalayam to Coonoor, prior to smothering the section of Kotagiri ghat. A decade later, the ghats were brought to a standstill for three weeks upon receiving a copious rainfall of 740mm. From the early 20th century to the recent past, the hills have braved several mudslips with varied intensity. The Marapallam landslide of November 1993 and the Ralliah ravage of 2009, part of a catastrophic wave of over 1,150 simultaneous landslides, remain green in the memory of Nilgiriologists. .Nevertheless, renewed demand for more interventions against further damage remains skeptical hitherto, thanks to rapacious anthropogenic influence, intergovernmental non-compliance, weak enforcement of conservation policies and apathy towards safeguarding the fragile mountains.There is no single universal minimum rainfall amount that triggers a landslide. However, the Nilgiris’ weakened geology makes slopes susceptible when rainfall approaches 150mm. The geological formation of this high-altitude landmass dates back to the Precambrian era, consisting of high grade metamorphic rocks. Though ancient, their foliated structures, joints and fractures can create weakness, potentially destabilising the slopes, especially during long rain spells in the monsoon.The onset of monsoon in the Nilgiris means shifting people from vulnerable locations, getting the rescue force on its toes, curbing tourism, and closing schools. With obligatory scientific interventions becoming sporadic, the hills have become an environmental basket case. Unfortunately, post-hoc crisis management has outstripped prevention.Recently, the result of the Nationwide Landslide Susceptibility Mapping – 2025 released by the Geological Survey of India (GSI), was contested by environmental observers, as it reduced the number of vulnerable locations in the Nilgiris from 283 to 156, against the state’s assessment. Even as the district administration endorsed the GSI figure as “scientific”, the dispute has triggered ambiguity among residents, who are first-hand victims. At a time when identifying vulnerable locations is increasingly difficult, can a reduction in their number be justified?.The tenets of crisis management involve sharing of information amongst all line departments for effective and coordinated action. However, collaboration remains deficient in the Nilgiris. A recent TNIE report substantiates this claim. Although GSI’s bulletin issued on October 23 served as a caveat, identifying Burliyar among other vulnerable locations where isolated landslides could occur, the state reportedly dismissed the signal as too general and difficult to act upon.For long, GSI’s recommendations have been neglected. Having studied the district extensively, GSI ex-director DN Seshagiri noted in his 1982 report, “Indiscriminate extension of roads has contributed to the geological instability of the district … engineers have a tendency to restrict stabilisation, drainage and protective measures”.The 2013 report also identified four pernicious human causes: vertical cutting of slopes, loading of slopes with heavy construction, bench-cutting and terracing for construction and encroachment on stream banks. Beyond the GSI, the Save Nilgiris Campaign’s counsel also went unheard for years. Had these recommendations been considered, many catastrophes could have been mitigated, if not prevented.The mountains are in urgent need of more scientific implementation of conservation policies. The effectiveness of the Hydroseeding and soil nailing techniques against concretisation of slopes needs more scrutiny, besides bolstering nature based solutions. Better public access to disaster risk data and action plans needs enhancement – as such information may prove invaluable during trying times. And to ensure more accountability, interdepartmental non-compliance cannot be trivialised when it can contribute to a disaster. When enough damage has already been done to a fragile ecosystem, the stage of prevention is in a race against time. Time to act!Lack of collaborationTenets of crisis management involve sharing of information amongst all line departments for effective and coordinated action. However, collaboration remains deficient in the Nilgiris districtYukesh Saravanan(The author is a researcher At the Madras Institute of Development Studies).Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: After missing salary, employees at Indian-origin CEO's robotic soldier startup backed by Eric Trump lose health benefits
content: Employees at Foundation Future Industries, a San Francisco-based robotics startup developing humanoid robots for heavy industrial and defense applications, have been told that their health benefits through administrator Rippling have been terminated amid a growing cash crunch and concerns about the company's future. According to CNBC, the startup, founded by CEO Sankaet Pathak, Mike LeBlanc, and Arjun Sethi, with Eric Trump involved as an investor and chief strategy advisor, told employees that they would be offered coverage through COBRA, a federal law that lets them temporarily keep health insurance after losing benefits by paying the full premium out of pocket.“Because our last pay run through Rippling was in October, they have ended our benefits with them retroactive to October,” a Foundation human resources manager said in the memo, according to CNBC. “COBRA will be offered to all employees to cover November.”Missed salaries in August, OctoberThe development comes nearly a week after it was reported that the startup, founded in 2024 and developed humanoid robots for logistics, manufacturing, mining, construction and military use, failed to pay October salaries to its employees. This is not the first time; the company, which has several high-profile clients, including a $24 million Pentagon contract, has failed to pay its employees on time. In August, too, the company failed to pay employees on time.Many have blamed CEO Pathak for the crisis and pointed fingers at his 2025 purchase of a $4.6 million home in Sausalito, California, with money allegedly borrowed from the company.Who is Sankaet Pathak?Foundation is the second startup founded by Rajasthan-born Pathak, who has a master's degree in electrical engineering from the University of Memphis. His first venture, Synapse Financial Services, a banking-as-a-service (BaaS) platform, was launched in 2014. In 2023, amid reports about his conduct and discrepancies in the company's ledgers of customer funds, the board of Synapse considered replacing Pathak. The company filed for bankruptcy in April 2024. Pathak co-founded Foundation in the same month.Trump Family linksAccording to Reuters, Foundation, which makes gun-carrying “Terminator”-style robot soldiers, has emerged as one of the Trump family’s highest-profile bets on defense technology. In April, Eric Trump appeared on Fox News with Pathak and said he got involved in the company to help the US beat China in humanoids. “That’s exactly what Sankaet is doing, and he’s doing a phenomenal job,” Eric Trump said.Foundation bets on South Korean investmentReuters also reported that South Korean conglomerate Base Group was preparing to invest $150 million in Foundation. Pathak, in emails to employees, had expressed confidence that the company would pay salaries once the Base funding came in.“My read, given where Base is, this is a timing issue, not an existential one for the company,” Pathak wrote in an 8 November email seen by Reuters, referring to the payroll issues.Pathak also told employees in another email that the loan for his house was agreed in August 2025 and “had no relationship to the current cash situation”.(With inputs from Reuters)

headline: 4,758 urban infrastructure works worth Rs 1019 crore sanctioned across Tamil Nadu in 5 months
content: CHENNAI: The Directorate of Municipal Administration (DMA) has sanctioned 4,758 infrastructure and developmental works at Rs 1,019.61 crore over the past five months, since June, towards improving basic infrastructure and living conditions in urban areas across the state.Of the total, Rs 366.23 crore has been sanctioned for 3,765 road works covering 599.79 km under the Chief Minister’s Integrated Urban Development Mission (CMIUDM) and the Urban Road Development Fund of the sixth State Finance Commission. The works include laying new roads and repairing damaged ones.Five drinking water supply projects worth Rs 119 crore have been sanctioned in the Madurai and Cuddalore municipal corporations and the Cumbum and Chidambaram municipalities under CMIUDM and the Operation and Maintenance Deficit Grant Fund. Additionally, `97.36 crore has been allocated for 457 works under SDRF to urban local bodies that faced drinking water scarcity due to rain deficit during the southwest monsoon.The government has also approved the development of 87 parks at Rs 14.87 crore, Rs 71.40 crore has been sanctioned for constructing 106 additional classrooms and Rs 13.83 crore for repairing and maintaining 78 existing classrooms. Another Rs 30.06 crore has been allocated for anganwadi infrastructure, including 123 new buildings at Rs 29.68 crore and repairs to nine existing centres at Rs 38 lakh.Further, 78 works worth Rs 13.14 crore and two sports stadiums worth Rs 14.35 crore have also been approved. Nearly 48 solid waste and wastewater management projects worth Rs 279.37 crore have been sanctioned under the Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0 and general funds. .Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Is a third-front opening up in Rajasthan? What the revival of Hanuman Beniwal’s RLP signals
content: Apart from the Congress, the results of Rajasthan rural elections have come as a shot in the arm for the beleaguered Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP), which has achieved its best-ever performance in any election in the state. The RLP won 497 Panchayat Samiti (PS) and 51 Zila Parishad (ZP) seats, emerging as the third-largest party behind the Congress and the BJP in the results declared on November 20. Just two years ago in 2024, the RLP lost in its home turf of Khinwsar in Nagaur district for the first time since the Assembly constituency went to polls in 2008, two years after it was created in a delimitation exercise. While party supremo Hanuman Beniwal was elected as the Nagaur MP in 2024 as an INDIA bloc candidate, he vacated the Assembly seat — his party’s lone win in the Assembly polls months earlier in late 2023 — and fielded his wife Kanika in the bypoll. Kanika, however, lost to the BJP’s Rewant Ram Danga by close to 14,000 votes, leaving the party without any representation in the Assembly. Cut to 2026, and the party has now cornered 6.78% of the votes in the Panchayat Samiti polls and a 6.64% vote share in the Zila Parishad elections (including NOTA in both), after hovering around 2.5% in all the previous polls. The RLP’s resurgence in Nagaur is also good news for Beniwal ahead of the 2028 Assembly polls: its comfortable position in Nagaur and wins elsewhere may give the party the much-needed boost to once again look at expanding its footprint. Following the high of three MLAs in 2018, the party had dropped to just one MLA in 2023. Best-ever performance Beniwal founded the RLP on October 29, 2018, with the objective of “providing a political platform for the voices of farmers, youth, labourers, and ordinary citizens”. However, it was largely seen as a party of Jats. At present, they are estimated at 8.56% as per the state OBC Commission, while Jat outfits claim the figure to be in excess of 10%. In the 2018 Assembly polls, the RLP fielded 58 candidates, out of whom three won and the party bagged 2.4% of total vote share. This was the fourth-highest in the state behind the Congress, the BJP, and the BSP (4.03%). Then, in panchayat and Zila Parishad polls in 2020-21, the party cornered 2.25% vote share in the Panchayat Samiti, behind the Congress and the BJP, and 2.92% in the Zila Parishad. However, it could not manage to get a Zila Pramukh elected. In the 2023 Assembly polls, the party fielded 78 candidates, but only one, Beniwal himself, managed to win, with the party’s candidates forfeiting deposits in as many as 70 constituencies. The party stood third behind the BJP and the Congress in vote share (2.39%), but above the Bharat Adivasi Party that got a 2.35% vote share. This time, its vote share has crossed 6% for the first time ever in both the panchayat and Zila Parishad, with the party looking at electing its first-ever Zila Pramukh in Nagaur, where it crossed the halfway mark, winning 19 of the 37 seats. Panchayat Samiti poll results In Panchayat Samitis this year, RLP has won a majority in 14 of them. For comparison, the BJP managed to cross the halfway mark in 51 of the 419 Panchayat Samitis across the state, and the Congress in 229. Overall, the RLP emerged as the largest party, either independently or jointly, in 27 Panchayat Samitis. Its top-performing districts are Nagaur (31.29% vote share, 92 Panchayat Samiti seats); Deedwana-Kuchaman (26.71% and 66 seats); Barmer (22.09% and 75 seats); Jodhpur (17.42% and 62 seats), and Jaipur (14.1% and 60 seats). Together, these account for 355 of its 497 seats — or 71.4% of its statewide tally — and 56.3% of its statewide vote-share. Adding Balotra and Bikaner takes the party's tally to 414 seats, or 83.3% of its statewide total seats. Jaipur also stood out as a significant outlier for the RLP, as it secured 1,86,772 votes in the state capital, the third-highest district vote tally; Jaipur is not traditionally considered the centre of RLP's organisational strength. Beniwal speaks of Third Front Beniwal told The Indian Express that the chief reason behind the party’s impressive performance is that “the people want change”. “Since 2013, 2018, and in 2023, we have been trying; but whoever talked of the third front with us, they eventually left, leaving us alone,” he said. Beniwal said people were tired of corruption and paper leaks under the Congress government (2018-23) and the BJP government of Bhajan Lal Sharma only “hushed up” that corruption. Under the incumbent BJP government, the bureaucracy has had a “free run”, hampering the administration’s “ability to govern, and so the people have, since long, been looking at alternatives beyond the two parties”. Beniwal also said the RLP could have performed much better, but that it currently lacks resources, organisation, and people. Repeated defections had also affected it, he added. While both RLP and Congress haven’t seen eye to eye lately, state Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said after the results were declared that the RLP was “part of INDIA bloc” and that they would “form Boards together”. Beniwal told Express that he remains in the INDIA bloc, but alleged that during the Khinwsar Assembly bypoll, “Dotasra and CM Sharma had a secret meeting at a senior BJP leader’s home in New Delhi” where they conspired to defeat his party. RLP turncoat Rewant Ram Danga won the seat on a BJP ticket. Beniwal also accused the Congress of breaking up the RLP in Barmer during the 2024 Lok Sabha polls by inducting its leader Ummeda Ram Beniwal, who won from the Barmer constituency. The RLP supremo said he would work on strengthening the RLP’s organisation in the coming months and expel some workers who had been working against the party.

headline: AAP to launch Punjab election campaign with Moga rally on November 26
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) is set to use its 14th foundation day on November 26 to begin a statewide mobilisation ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, with a rally in Moga bringing together national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann and all 71 candidates announced so far. The party expects supporters from all 117 constituencies to attend, turning the event into a platform to present its government’s record and signal its election priorities. The gathering will also include constituency in-charges, giving the party an opportunity to place its declared candidates and local organisation alongside its senior leadership. AAP won 92 of Punjab’s 117 seats in the 2022 Assembly elections and formed the government under Mann. The November 26 event is expected to set out how the party plans to seek another mandate. A statewide political pitch Moga’s location in the Malwa region is central to the choice of venue. The district is connected to Ludhiana, Ferozepur, Faridkot and Barnala, while routes through Jalandhar provide access to Doaba. The party is seeking to use the rally to send a message beyond Malwa, reaching voters and workers across Majha and Doaba as well. Punjab’s 117 constituencies are distributed across three regions: 69 in Malwa, 23 in Doaba and 25 in Majha. AAP has announced candidates for 71 seats, or about 61% of the total, and has finalised nominees for all four constituencies in Moga district. The rally will bring those candidates together as the party advances candidate selection and organisational preparations. Governance and next steps The party is expected to highlight initiatives of the Mann government, including free electricity, Aam Aadmi Clinics, free treatment of up to ₹10 lakh, government schools and employment-related measures. Its leadership is also expected to outline a development roadmap for Punjab for the next five years. Kejriwal and Mann sharing the stage will bring the party’s national leadership and its state government into a joint campaign setting. Their speeches are expected to address the government’s work as well as issues concerning farmers, young people, women, education and healthcare. Operational details and schedules were not provided yet. The statewide rally will therefore combine a review of the government’s nearly five-year tenure with an outline of the party’s priorities for another term. Its scale, the presence of all 71 announced candidates and participation from across Punjab will offer a public indication of AAP’s organisational readiness as the state moves towards the 2027 contest.

headline: 7 serving & retired Punjab govt officers summoned as ED probes ‘middleman’ hockey player in bribery case
content: New Delhi: Alleging that a hockey player arrested on charges of aiding suspended Punjab Police Deputy Inspector General Harcharan Singh Bhullar in collecting a bribe was working as a liaison for several state government officers, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned five serving and two retired officers for questioning this week.The list of officers summoned includes the state’s health secretary, Kumar Rahul, and senior police officers such as Ludhiana Police Commissioner Swapan Sharma and Punjab Police Service officer Gagan Ajit Singh, now Senior Superintendent of Police in Fazilka district. Singh and Sharma have been summoned to appear before the investigating officer on Thursday and Friday, respectively.The agency arrested Kirshanu Sharda, a national-level hockey player, in September this year on charges of generating proceeds of crime, citing alleged repeated WhatsApp communications between him and Bhullar, who was also arrested later in October. The agency’s money-laundering probe stems from a case by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), which had arrested Sharda for assisting Bhullar in collecting a bribe from a Fatehgarh Sahib-based scrap dealer in exchange for not framing him in a case.Kumar Rahul, posted as administrative secretary in the state’s Health & Family Welfare and Medical Education & Research department, has been summoned to appear Monday. Apart from the trio, the agency has also summoned Punjab Civil Service officer Anand Sagar Sharma, who is posted as staff officer to the Commissioner, Faridkot Division, and promotee Indian Administrative Service officer Neeru Katyal Gupta, who has been posted as special secretary in the General Administration and Coordination department. They have been asked to appear on Wednesday and Thursday.Two recently retired officers—Gurpreet Sapra and Arun Sekhri—have also been summoned to appear before the investigating officer on Wednesday and Thursday.Contacted by ThePrint, Sapra said she had not received any summons as of Sunday evening. “If I may receive it, I will go,” she added.Meanwhile, the Fazilka SSP attributed his acquaintance with Sharda to his sports background, and said he would appear before the agency. “I am a hockey player and an Olympian, and I have a family history of Olympians, and that guy is a hockey player. I know a lot of hockey players, and he is one of them,” Gagan Ajit Singh told ThePrint, adding that he would appear before the agency on the designated day.Anand Sagar Sharma also confirmed that he had received summons and said he would appear before the agency. “Yes, I have received the summons, and I will appear on the date of the summons unless there is some contingency," Sharma told ThePrint.Attempts to reach Neeru Katyal Gupta for comment over phone were unsuccessful. ThePrint has sent her queries via WhatsApp. Similarly, Sekhri’s phone was also switched off, and a response to queries sent over WhatsApp is awaited.WhatsApp calls to Kumar Rahul and Swapan Sharma went unanswered. This report will be updated if and when responses are received.Also Read: ‘Shortage of vehicles, manpower’: Chandigarh admin fails to produce arrested Punjab DIG Bhullar in courtCase against ShardaED sources said the officers were summoned after a forensic analysis of Sharda’s phone records. The agency has also cited funds credited to Sharda's bank account in a short span of time, leading to a cumulative balance of Rs 1.41 crore, and that the CBI had recovered Rs 21 lakh from his residence during searches in October last year.According to the ED’s prosecution complaint filed last week, Sharda allegedly told the agency that the Rs 21 lakh recovered from his premises by the CBI was given to him by a clerk at the Ropar Deputy Commissioner's office to facilitate a land compensation matter involving an Amritsar resident through an IAS officer. Additionally, the agency cited his own statement allegedly admitting that he had received Rs 15 lakh to facilitate the transfers and postings of government officials and to secure various favours from Punjab government officials. This included payments of Rs 50,000 on various occasions when he had allegedly passed on advance information regarding proposed transfer lists of government officials. In one such instance, the agency stated that he allegedly admitted to pocketing a Rs 2 lakh commission from the Rs 5 lakh he received for facilitating the transfer of a government official. The remaining Rs 3 lakh was passed on to another intermediary, he allegedly told the ED. “That investigation under the PMLA further revealed that the activities of Kirshanu Sharda were not confined to Harcharan Singh Bhullar alone. He was acting as an intermediary for several other civil servants and government functionaries in Punjab by facilitating transfers/postings, numberdari, land-related matters, building plan approvals and other official work in consideration of monetary gratification,” the agency alleged in the prosecution complaint. “He utilised his connections with officials of various government departments to secure official favours for individuals in exchange for money, received either in cash or directly in his bank accounts,” it further said. “In his statements recorded under Section 50 of the PMLA, he admitted having received approximately Rs 15 lakh for facilitating such official work and disclosed specific instances of monetary transactions, including payments made to intermediaries and commissions retained by him.”Additionally, agency sources said that forensic examination of the hockey player's phone has revealed several high-value transactions totalling up to Rs 2 crore for settlement in a harassment case, as well as transactions of Rs 10 lakh for clearance of project files from the forest department and for information on upcoming projects of the housing and urban development department.Sources refused to divulge specific details of the transactions or the roles of the officers summoned so far, citing the investigation’s nascent and critical stage.Sharda’s counsel, Vipul Sharma, refused to comment on the specific allegations against him. However, at the time of the agency’s arrest, he argued before the court that Sharda had been a hockey player for the last 16 years, that his grandfather too had played hockey internationally, and that the ED can’t assume that his assets of Rs 1.4 crore were “stealthily” accumulated.This report has been updated to incorporate details from the ED's prosecution complaint.(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)Also Read: CBI sought day-to-day hearings against suspended Punjab Police DIG. Why Chandigarh court junked plea

headline: Virtual hearings permitted, but 45 district consumer commissions in Punjab, Haryana lack VC infrastructur
content: Chandigarh: Virtual hearings may be permitted in consumer commissions under e-Jagriti (Electronics, Justice And Grievance Redressal through Information Technology and Innovation), but litigants in Punjab and Haryana are yet to benefit at the district level. Replies to Right to Information (RTI) applications have revealed that 45 district consumer commissions across the two states lack operational video-conferencing (VC) facilities, raising questions about access to justice for consumers across the two states.The RTI applications were filed by advocate Raja Vikrant Sharma. According to the reply from Haryana’s State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, the state has 22 district commissions, but “no such hardware or displays have been provided for video conferencing”. The commission also stated that no grant had been given for setting up VC infrastructure in the district commissions.The Haryana reply assumes significance in light of a letter issued by the state commission to assistant registrars of district commissions. It directed that requests from parties or advocates to pursue cases through video-conferencing should be accepted. However, the RTI response indicates that the equipment needed to facilitate such hearings has not been provided.In Punjab, the RTI reply confirms that none of the state’s 23 district consumer commissions has operational VC facilities. The principal bench of the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has operational VC facilities, but its additional bench does not.Asked for official VC links, meeting IDs or web portal details for district commissions, Punjab’s State Commission replied, “No information is available.” The same response was given to questions about funds or grants received during the last three financial years for VC infrastructure, and guidelines governing virtual hearings. It says the information was not available.Advocate Raja Vikrant Sharma said the absence of facilities could undermine a provision intended to make hearings accessible. “Virtual hearings are not just a convenience; they are a means of access to justice. Section 38(6) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, recognises video conferencing for hearings. Yet, without VC infrastructure and internet connectivity in Punjab and Haryana consumer commissions, how can this be implemented? Many consumer commissions are not adequately accessible to persons with disabilities. Virtual hearings can open a door for them, but without the necessary infrastructure, that opportunity remains only on paper,” he said.The gap is particularly relevant for senior citizens, persons with disabilities and litigants living far from commission headquarters. The RTI replies do not say when the infrastructure will be installed.The states lack infrastructure and until it is installed the aim for easy access to legal remedies and an accessible justice system through remote hearings risks remaining a direction on paper.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: ED summons Ludhiana top cop, 6 other serving & retd Pb officers in Bhullar case
content: Chandigarh: Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned seven serving and retired bureaucrats and police officers in Punjab for questioning in connection with a corruption and money-laundering investigation originally based on suspended Punjab Police DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar.ED is examining whether Krishanu Sharda, a middleman, acted as an intermediary for a wider network of officials across the state administration, allegedly facilitating official work and influencing decisions in exchange for money.Those summoned include Ludhiana police commissioner Swapan Sharma, a 2009-batch IPS officer, who is scheduled to appear on Nov 27.This is his second ED summons in barely a month. He was questioned for over four hours on Oct 19 in a separate case involving alleged fabrication of forensic and cyber analysis reports to support claims that a controversial video linked to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann was AI-generated. Sharma had maintained that his visit to Gurugram was related to a cybercrime investigation.The other officers summoned are Kumar Rahul, a 2000-batch IAS officer and administrative secretary, health and family welfare and medical education and research, on Nov 23; Anand Sagar Sharma, a 2012-batch PCS officer and staff officer to the Faridkot divisional commissioner, and retired officer Arun Sekhri, former divisional commissioner of Faridkot, Ferozepur and Jalandhar, on Nov 25. Neeru Katyal Gupta, a 2016-batch IAS officer and special secretary, general administration and coordination; Gagan Ajit Singh, PPS and Fazilka SSP; and retired officer Gurpreet Sapra, former Jalandhar commissioner, have been summoned on Nov 26.The case originated from an Oct 2025 complaint by scrap dealer Akash Batta, who alleged that suspended DIG Bhullar demanded Rs 8 lakh through Sharda to settle a police case in Sirhind.The CBI arrested Sharda on Oct 16, 2025, after allegedly catching him accepting Rs 4 lakh. Bhullar was arrested the same day. Subsequent CBI searches of premises linked to Bhullar yielded around 73.7 crore in cash and jewellery worth Rs 2.32 crore, prompting a separate disproportionate assets case.The ED later filed a money-laundering case, arresting Sharda on Sept 18 and Bhullar on Oct 9. The ED has alleged that Sharda operated as a conduit for several govt officials, flagging suspicious financial transactions involving several officers and attributed around Rs 1 crore in alleged proceeds of crime to Sharda.PROBE WIDENSNov 23 | Kumar Rahul, administrative secretary, health and family welfare, and medical education and researchNov 25 | Anand Sagar Sharma, staff officer to Faridkot divisional commissioner; Arun Sekhri, retired officerNov 26 | Neeru Katyal Gupta, special secretary, general administration and coordination; Gagan Ajit Singh, Fazilka SSP; Gurpreet Sapra, retired officerNov 27 | Swapan Sharma, Ludhiana police commissioner(The seven serving and retired officers summoned by ED)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Ludhiana sees sharp increase in child malnutrition cases
content: Key child nutrition indicators in Ludhiana have deteriorated over the past four years, raising concerns about the effectiveness of nutrition interventions despite improvements in healthcare access and immunisation coverage.Data from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) reveal a significant rise in the proportion of undernourished children.The most alarming increase has been recorded in the prevalence of wasting, an indicator of acute malnutrition.The percentage of children under five years of age who are wasted surged from 5.9 per cent in the 2019-21 survey to 18.9 per cent in 2023-24, more than a threefold increase. Similarly, the proportion of underweight children more than doubled from 12.4 per cent to 25.7 per cent during the period.Stunting cases, which reflect chronic malnutrition and impaired growth, also increased from 22.1 per cent to 25.3 per cent.The survey findings suggest that although children are increasingly accessing healthcare services and vaccination coverage remains high, nutritional outcomes have failed to keep pace.Wasting and underweight prevalence are considered critical indicators of inadequate nutrition, recurrent illness and poor feeding practices during early childhood.The data also highlight concerns over infant and young child feeding practices. The proportion of children aged 6-23 months receiving an adequate diet declined from 14.1 per cent to 11.4 per cent.Among breastfed children in the same age group, the proportion receiving an adequate diet dropped from 14.3 per cent to 8.3 per cent, suggesting that a large majority of young children are not receiving nutritionally adequate complementary foods.Public health experts note that malnutrition is influenced not only by food availability but also by dietary diversity, household income, maternal awareness, sanitation and childcare practices.The latest survey findings are likely to prompt closer scrutiny of nutrition programmes being implemented through Anganwadis and other government initiatives aimed at improving child health.Health officials and nutrition experts say a detailed analysis of district-level data will be required to identify the reasons behind the worsening indicators and develop targeted interventions.“With one in four children now underweight and nearly one in five suffering from wasting, the latest figures underscore the need for a renewed focus on child nutrition in Ludhiana,” said Dr Tarundeep, a city-based paediatrician.

headline: ED: Bhullar aide admits receiving Rs 21 lakh for facilitating land compensation through IAS officer
content: The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has claimed that Krishanu Sharda, an alleged aide of suspended Punjab DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar, admitted before the agency that the cash amount of Rs 21 lakh recovered from his residential premises by the CBI on October 16, 2025, had been given to him by a clerk in the DC Office, Ropar, for facilitating a land compensation matter pertaining to Harjeet Singh, a resident of Amritsar, through an IAS officer.The ED recorded Krishanu Sharda's statement under Section 50 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, between September 18, 2026, and September 25, 2026, during his remand period.The statement forms part of the prosecution complaint filed by the ED against Krishanu Sharda before the PMLA Court, Chandigarh, under Section 44(1)(b), read with Section 45 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.As per the prosecution complaint, Sharda told the ED that he had worked as a contractual fireman with the Municipal Council, Mandi Gobindgarh, from 2018 to 2022. Thereafter, he provided hockey coaching to children from 2021 to 2025. He claimed to have earned approximately Rs 50,000 per month from coaching and also received cash prizes at hockey tournaments.In his statement dated September 23, 2026, he admitted to having received approximately Rs 15 lakh in consideration for facilitating the transfers and postings of government officials and securing various official favours from Punjab Government officials.He further disclosed several instances in which he had facilitated transfers and postings and arranged for official work to be carried out through government officials in exchange for illegal gratification.Among the several instances disclosed by Krishanu Sharda in his statement recorded under Section 50 of the PMLA, 2002, regarding favours facilitated through various government officials in lieu of monetary consideration, a few notable instances included his admission that he had received Rs 5 lakh for facilitating the transfer of a government official. Of this amount, Rs 3 lakh was allegedly passed on to an intermediary, while he retained Rs 2 lakh as commission.He further admitted to having received approximately Rs 50,000 on various occasions for providing advance information about proposed transfer lists of government officials.Regarding the cash amount of Rs 21 lakh recovered from his residential premises by the CBI on October 16, 2025, he stated that the amount had been given to him by a clerk in the DC Office, Ropar, for facilitating a land compensation matter pertaining to Harjeet Singh, a resident of Amritsar, through an IAS officer. Thus, he disclosed that the cash recovered from his residence had been received in connection with facilitating official work.The ED has filed the prosecution complaint against Krishanu Sharda before the PMLA Court, Chandigarh, under Section 44(1)(b), read with Section 45 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.Krishanu Sharda was arrested by the CBI along with Harcharan Singh Bhullar on October 16, 2025, while they were allegedly accepting Rs 5,00,000 as part of the bribe demanded from the complainant.The FIR in the case was initially registered by the CBI on the complaint of Akash Batta, who alleged that Bhullar, then posted as DIG, Ropar Range, Punjab Police, had demanded illegal gratification through a private intermediary, Krishanu Sharda. The alleged bribe was sought in exchange for securing favourable treatment in an FIR registered at Police Station Sirhind and ensuring that no coercive action was taken against the complainant's business.The ED initiated its investigation following the registration of the CBI case.

headline: Himachals IIT-Mandi hosts annual meet of IIT librarians
content: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Mandi, hosted the 12th Annual Pan-IIT Librarians Meet on November 22 and 23, bringing together librarians and library professionals from IITs across the country to discuss emerging technologies, institutional collaboration and the future of academic libraries.The two-day meeting provided a common platform for participants to exchange experiences, share best practices and explore strategies to strengthen library services across the IIT system. The inaugural session was attended by the Director of IIT-Mandi.A key focus of the discussions was the implementation of the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) initiative, Open Access and Article Processing Charges (APCs). Participants reviewed the progress, coverage and usage of ONOS while discussing the challenges faced by IIT libraries. The deliberations covered APC support mechanisms, publisher agreements and possible solutions for accessing journals not covered under existing arrangements.The meeting also addressed the structure of the library cadre, recruitment rules and career progression of library professionals. Participants explored the possibility of developing a common framework across IITs by harmonising designations, recruitment practices and promotion opportunities.An expert lecture on “Reimagining the Modern Academic Library: Technology, Innovation, Well-being and Professional Excellence” was delivered by Dr Jadhav, former Librarian at IIT-Madras. The lecture highlighted the evolving role of academic libraries and the need to balance technological advancements with professional excellence and staff well-being.Capacity building and professional development of library staff also featured prominently in the discussions. Participants emphasised the importance of training in Artificial Intelligence (AI), programming and scripting, data analytics, research support tools, mentoring and reskilling to prepare library professionals for emerging technological challenges.Strengthening collaboration among IIT libraries through Inter-Library Loan (ILL), Document Delivery Services (DDS) and resource sharing was another major agenda item. Discussions focused on developing a common discovery and request portal and introducing standardised protocols to improve access to academic resources.The programme also featured interactions with publishers and representatives of scholarly information services, focusing on emerging APC models, AI-based databases and research tools. Participants discussed the proposal to establish an IIT Libraries Consortium to facilitate collective negotiations, resource sharing and improved access to scholarly information.On the second day, participants joined a tree plantation drive on the IIT-Mandi campus, reaffirming the institute’s commitment to environmental sustainability. An open discussion and panel session on the future roadmap for IIT libraries explored proposals for launching an open-access journal and introducing regular newsletters to improve communication and information exchange.Participants also visited various units of the IIT-Mandi Library to familiarise themselves with its facilities and services.The annual meeting concluded with a shared emphasis on professional networking, institutional cooperation and the development of technologically advanced, inclusive and future-ready academic libraries across the IIT system.

headline: Dry cold intensifies in Himachal; Tabo shivers at -4.6°C | Hindustan Times
content: Dry cold has intensified in Himachal Pradesh, with night temperatures dropping below the freezing point in tribal areas and dense morning fog in the plains and river-valley regions, while Tabo, in the Lahaul-Spiti district, was the coldest place in the state with a minimum temperature of -4.6°C.On Sunday, visibility in Sundernagar (Mandi district) plummeted to just 70 metres due to fog, causing difficulties for motorists. There is no likelihood of rain or snowfall in the state until November 28, the MeT said.So far in November, the state received 3.1mm of rain against normal rainfall of 12.2mm, a deficit of 74% from November 1 to 22. The lack of precipitation is exacerbating the dry cold conditions.The state’s average minimum temperature recorded a decline of 0.2°C over the last 24 hours. In Palampur, the temperature was 2°C below normal. In Nahan, it was 1.5°C and in Bilaspur and Chamba, it was 0.5 and 0.3°C below normal, respectively.

headline: HPPCL generates 3,459 MU of electricity in 4 yrs, realises revenue of Rs 1,387cr
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (HPPCL) recorded power generation of 3,459.99 million units, resulting in revenue accumulation of Rs 1,387.49 crore in the four years since Dec 2022.According to a govt statement, the 100 MW Sainj Hydroelectric Project in Kullu district contributed 1,252.56 MUs of electricity, earning revenue of Rs 462.55 crore.Similarly, the 65 MW Kashang Stage-I Hydroelectric Project in Kinnaur generated 776.328 MUs, earning revenue of Rs 252 crore. The 5 MW Berra Dol solar power project in Bilaspur district contributed 62.78 MUs and a revenue of Rs 27.05 crore.The 111 MW Sawra Kuddu Hydroelectric Project in Shimla district contributed 1,190.383 MUs of electricity, earning a revenue of Rs 589.6 crore. The 32 MW Pekhubela solar power project in Una district, inaugurated on June 20, 2024, by chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, recorded net power generation of 113.27 MUs, realising revenue of Rs 32.89 crore, the statement added.Apart from these commissioned projects, various hydro power projects are under execution. These include the 450 MW Shongtong Karcham Hydroelectric Project in Kinnaur district, work for which has been expedited and completion is expected by April 2027, the statement read.The work on the 130 MW Integrated Kashang Stage-II & III Hydroelectric Project in Kinnaur district and the 48 MW Chanju-III HEP in Chamba district will be completed in the coming years. The construction of the diversion tunnel for the 40 MW Renukaji Dam Project in Sirmaur district is currently underway, and main dam works are expected to be awarded in the next fiscal year.The 191 MW Thana Plaun HEP in Mandi district; the 48 MW Surgani Sundla Hydroelectric Project, designed to utilise the tail water of Baira Suil Hydroelectric Project; the 1,630 MW Renukaji Pump Storage Project in Sirmaur district; the 270 MW Thana Plaun Pump Storage Project in Mandi district; the 780 MW Jangi Thopan Hydro Electric Project in Kinnaur district; and the 422 MW Kishau Multipurpose Project on River Tons are at the pre-construction stage, the statement added.The state govt has set a target of installing 500 MW of solar power projects. The implementation of the projects was taken up expeditiously during the last four years, which has resulted in the commissioning of three solar projects of 47 MW and execution of three solar projects of 29.6 MW capacity. Also, bidding for four solar projects of 34 MW capacity is at the tendering stage; read the statement.

headline: India Inc outlines measures to attract foreign capital
content: Days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticised Indian industry for falling short on job creation and other fronts, senior officials of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) on Monday outlined steps the government could take to boost private investment, including strengthening market integrity, improving regulatory transparency and easing the flow of cross-border capital. “The key strategy of the government must be to create a business environment characterised by robust investor protection and regulatory ease coupled by market integrity. Towards this objective, regulatory authorities would play a key role by ensuring that their compliances do not stand as an obstacle for the free flow of cross border capital,” said CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee, in a post on X. He said Modi’s call for industry to invest more, foster innovation and improve competitiveness was a strong reminder of the need to raise productivity and secure long-term economic growth. “India’s ability to attract long-term capital will be determined by the strength of its markets and the competitiveness of our industries. Increased transparency, along with ease of doing business, will strengthen India’s standing as a global investment destination,” he added. Addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry’s (Ficci’s) annual general meeting last week, Modi criticised Indian companies for their continued reliance on imports in critical sectors and for treating the country’s vast domestic market as a “comfort zone”, rather than improving product quality and building capabilities to compete globally. Rajiv Memani, CII’s immediate past president, said global investors sought clear, predictable and proportionate rules. “India’s regulatory framework must deliver on all three. India will need both domestic savings and foreign capital to finance its investment requirements. Long-term global investors weigh regulatory clarity, predictability and compliance costs alongside returns,” he said. He further said openness to global capital and market integrity are complementary objectives. “A transparent, predictable and proportionate regulatory framework is essential to achieving both and sustaining India's attractiveness to long-term investors,” he added. Memani said SEBI's use of public consultation allows market participants to provide feedback and enables regulatory requirements to be reviewed in the light of changing market conditions, emerging risks, and benchmarked with international standards and practices. “SEBI has taken several steps to make India's capital markets more accessible to foreign investors, including risk-based regulatory requirements, simplified operating processes and initiatives such as SWAGAT-FI. These efforts are important, alongside effective safeguards for investor protection and market integrity,” he added. Sanjiv Puri, former CII president and chairman and managing director of ITC, said for Indian enterprises seeking to attract long-term domestic and global capital, strong governance and predictable regulation are essential. “Transparency, investor confidence and ease of investment reinforce one another. Vibrant markets can give a significant impetus to robust economic growth and competitiveness,” he added. Puri said capital markets have played a vital role in channelising savings into productive investments contributing to nation-building and enabling growth with inclusiveness. “Undoubtedly, market integrity is built on transparency and good governance. India has made considerable progress on both,” he said. Puri said over the years, Sebi has steadily strengthened corporate governance and disclosure standards for listed companies apart from a sharp focus on enabling ease of doing business. “Laudable steps include the strengthening of board oversight, related-party transaction norms and comprehensive Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRR). These measures have helped improve corporate accountability and the quality of information available to investors. Good regulation must also evolve with changing market conditions. SEBI's consultative approach to reviewing and refining its regulations provides an important opportunity to balance compliance requirements with emerging opportunities risks, while keeping transparency and investor protection central,” he added. R Dinesh, another former CII president and executive chairman of TVS Supply Chain Solutions, said access to long-term capital and confidence in market regulation were crucial for an economy investing heavily in infrastructure and logistics. “Clear rules, strong governance and proportionate regulation can help deliver both,” he suggested. Dinesh said India’s infrastructure needs patient, long-term capital, and the right market frameworks help bring it in transparently. “SEBI's frameworks for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) have created regulated avenues for domestic and global investors to participate in infrastructure and real estate assets, including roads, power transmission, warehousing and commercial properties. Strong disclosure and governance requirements have been central to these frameworks. Equally important is the willingness to review and refine regulations as markets develop. SEBI's consultative approach provides an opportunity to calibrate requirements to evolving risks and investor needs, without compromising transparency or investor protection,” he added. CII President R Mukundan, who is also managing director and chief executive officer of Tata Chemicals, said the next priority was to move beyond ease of doing business to the “speed of doing business”. CII’s Private Investment Barometer showed that private project announcements reached a record ₹26.6 trillion in the first half of FY27, 4.4 times the long-run average, he said. As the prime minster Modi has said, “the task now is for industry to make ‘India First’ the basis of every long-term decision. CIl and its members are committed to this agenda,” he added.

headline: MCD navigating legal hurdles to clear Ghazipur landfill, meet 2027 deadline
content: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is currently navigating a Supreme Court order on stay on a tender owing to which work on the third phase of biomining operations at the Ghazipur landfill site is on hold. According to government data released in October, at Ghazipur, 69 lakh Metric Tonnes (MT) of legacy waste was still left to be cleared. According to a report published by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Sunday, the progress in legacy waste processing at Ghazipur is the slowest among all major landfill sites in Delhi, with the commission rating it ‘unsatisfactory’. Reason: stay on tender The Supreme Court had last month stayed the tender for the work at the site, awarded to Greentech Environ Management. The Rs 249-crore project for the third phase of biomining and reclamation of the land was awarded to the agency, which was the lowest bidder. The Standing Committee of the MCD had also approved awarding of the tender at a meeting held last week. The tender was issued last year. Greentech appeared before the Delhi High Court to be included in the financial bids as the agency was earlier disqualified after being blacklisted by the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) and fined over Rs 5 crore for failing to meet processing targets last year. The agency had challenged the decision before the HC and highlighted that the MCG’s decision related to the blacklisting had already been withdrawn on August 25 this year and that the tender terms/addendum did not explicitly specify that work orders had to be for active ongoing projects. The high court eventually allowed Greentech to bid for the tender. However, Guru Ramdas Constructions, the second lowest bidder for the tender, moved the Supreme Court in October challenging the HC’s decision, after which the apex court issued a stay on all orders until a judgement was passed. This meant that Greentech could not start their operations at the site. The Delhi government then moved the court to vacate the stay order. The Supreme Court was supposed to hear the matter on Monday, but it did not take it up and postponed it by a week. According to MCD sources, however, the December 2027 deadline will not be missed even after the court stay as Alwazo Solutions JV, another agency which was awarded the tender for the second phase of the biomining work at Ghazipur, is currently carrying out work at the site on an interim basis — despite its contract having been terminated in December 2024 for failing to meet the processing targets. According to the recent CAQM report, against an annual target of 39.12 lakh MT as of October 31, only 16.53 lakh MT legacy waste was processed at the Ghazipur landfill — an achievement of 42%, fetching a rating of ‘unsatisfactory’. This does not, however, take into account the nearly 3,000 MT of fresh waste being deposited at the site daily. Landfill sites at Okhla and Bhalswa, meanwhile, have met 67% and 57% of their targets, respectively. The three sites in Delhi had a combined target of 114.99 lakh MT of legacy waste liquidation for 2026. Collectively, the three sites have processed 62.28 lakh MT, leaving a gap of 52.71 lakh MT.

headline: Former Tripura CM accuses BJP govt of 'jungle raj'
content: Former Tripura Chief Minister and veteran CPM leader Manik Sarkar on Monday launched a scathing attack on the BJP-led state government, alleging that ‘jungle raj’ prevails in Tripura and calling for the restoration of the rule of law. Sarkar was addressing a public meeting organised in front of the CPM party office at Uttar Bazar in Amarpur in support of Left Front candidates contesting the upcoming Nagar Panchayat elections. From the afternoon, a large number of Left Front workers and supporters began gathering at the venue from different wards and nearby villages. The meeting witnessed a notable turnout of party supporters. In his address, Sarkar alleged that people had been deprived of basic necessities and economic opportunities under the present government. He pointed to rising prices of essential commodities, alleged food shortages and the lack of employment opportunities, claiming that unemployment was increasing while ordinary people continued to face financial hardships. He further alleged that while common people were struggling to make ends meet, leaders and ministers of the ruling party were enjoying themselves without showing any concern for public suffering. The former Chief Minister claimed that people were now seeking a change and urged voters to support Left Front candidates in the upcoming Nagar Panchayat elections. He said electing Left candidates would help restore people's rights, put an end to alleged corruption in the name of development and ensure access to employment, food and rightful entitlements. Calling for an end to what he described as the prevailing “jungle raj”, Sarkar stressed the need to establish the rule of law in the state.

headline: Koraga community seeks direct government jobs for educated youth in Udupi
content: Udupi: Members of the Koraga community have urged the government to provide direct recruitment opportunities for educated unemployed youth in government departments, stating that vocational training alone would not address their employment needs. At a meeting held to discuss the grievances of the Koraga community in Udupi and Brahmavara taluks at the Udupi Taluk Panchayat meeting hall, Ganesh Kundapura said that the community was seeking direct recruitment to government jobs rather than training programmes.'Youngsters who had undergone vocational training were not inclined to take up self-employment,' he said. The government should therefore create opportunities for direct recruitment of eligible candidates from the community. .Koraga community urges govt to address long-pending demands at Mangaluru cabinet meet.Declining Koraga population in Dakshina Kannada raises concern.Responding to the demand, MLA Yashpal Suvarna, who chaired the meeting, said the authorities should collect data on educated youth from the Koraga community and organise a job fair by inviting various companies. This would help some of them secure employment in reputed companies. He also asked officials to explore employment opportunities for community members in cooperative institutions. The meeting also discussed the long-pending renovation of Adivasi Bhavan at Puthur in Udupi, constructed at a cost of around Rs 3 crore under the Integrated Tribal Development Project (ITDP) for the use of the Koraga community. Narayanaswamy, Project Officer of the District Integrated Tribal Development Project, said a proposal seeking Rs 76 lakh for the renovation of the building had been sent to the central office. Community leaders said the building had remained unsuitable for use despite being constructed several years ago due to several problems, including sound reverberation. They urged the authorities to take immediate steps to make it functional. Municipal Commissioner Mahantesh Hangaragi said the Udupi City Municipal Council had levelled the premises around the building and was considering renting it out on the lines of a town hall. The MLA said efforts would be made to undertake the renovation using funds from the SC/ST grant of the City Municipal Council, Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat, besides Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds.The community also raised concerns over the exclusion of Koraga families living within Udupi city limits from the Chief Minister's Health Card scheme provided by the City Municipal Council. Ganesh Kundapura, Gowri and Putran Hebri urged the authorities to ensure that urban Koraga families received healthcare benefits similar to those extended to their counterparts in rural areas through the ITDP. Raising land-related grievances, Putran Hebri said the community had not received any relief despite an earlier meeting held in Brahmavar. Brahmavar Tahsildar AN Bhat assured the members that the issue would be examined and a solution found soon. The MLA said a meeting of gram panchayat officials would be convened to address revenue related problems in Brahmavar taluk. Bogra Kokkarnе alleged that meetings convened to discuss the community's grievances had become a mere formality, as decisions taken at such meetings were rarely implemented. Putran also alleged that Koraga land had been encroached upon in some places and sought the removal of encroachments. The issue of contaminated well water at Nittoor was also raised. Residents of a nearby Koraga colony were reportedly forced to use unfit water for drinking after the well became polluted. Responding to the complaint, Suvarna directed the municipal commissioner to immediately test the well water and shift the septic pit of a nearby residential complex, suspected to be the source of contamination, to another location.
