headline: Bisleri-FSSAI row: How can prolonged exposure to bromate and PAHs in drinking water affect your health?
content: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International after one of its water samples was declared "unsafe" in laboratory testing. The company, however, has disputed the findings, triggering a row over the presence of bromate and polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the sample.According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), prolonged exposure to certain chemical contaminants in drinking water, including bromate and some PAHs, may pose health risks, including potential kidney damage and an increased risk of cancer.The two substances have different sources and potential health effects.What is bromate and what happens if you consume it in excess?Bromate is a chemical compound that can form during drinking-water disinfection, particularly when ozone reacts with naturally occurring bromide ions in water, according to the WHO.The WHO has set a provisional guideline value of 10 micrograms per litre (µg/l) for bromate in drinking water, primarily because of concerns about its potential carcinogenic effects.The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) has classified bromate as a Group 2B substance, meaning it is "possibly carcinogenic to humans". According to the WHO, while evidence of carcinogenicity in humans is inadequate, animal studies have shown sufficient evidence of cancer-causing potential.Bromate has also demonstrated mutagenic properties in laboratory studies, meaning it can cause changes in genetic material, or DNA. The WHO's assessment discusses oxidative DNA damage as one possible mechanism behind its carcinogenic effects.Animal studies have linked prolonged exposure to bromate with tumours in the kidneys and thyroid, among other tissues. These findings raise concerns about long-term exposure, although they do not mean that consuming water with a slightly elevated bromate concentration will immediately cause cancer.The potential health risk depends on the concentration consumed, the frequency of exposure and its duration. The WHO's guideline is intended to limit long-term exposure and reduce associated health risks.What are PAHs and how can they affect your health?Polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons, commonly called PAHs, are a group of organic chemical compounds containing two or more fused aromatic rings.According to the WHO, PAHs are formed primarily through the incomplete combustion of organic materials. They can enter the environment through industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust and other sources of atmospheric pollution. They may also contaminate drinking water through coal-tar coatings used in water distribution pipes.PAHs can enter the human body through food, air and drinking water. The WHO notes that these compounds may be present in food following exposure to airborne pollution and in fish from contaminated waters. They can also form during cooking methods such as grilling, roasting, frying and baking.Some PAHs are particularly concerning because of their carcinogenic potential. The WHO identifies benzo[a]pyrene as an important indicator of PAH contamination and has prescribed a guideline value of 0.7 micrograms per litre in drinking water.The WHO's assessment says evidence linking PAH mixtures to cancer in humans comes primarily from occupational studies involving inhalation and skin exposure. It also notes that human data on cancer risks from oral exposure are unavailable.The health effects vary depending on the specific PAH, the amount of exposure and its duration. Prolonged exposure to certain compounds, particularly benzo[a]pyrene, is a concern because of their cancer-causing potential.What is the Bisleri-FSSAI controversy?The dispute relates to a sample collected by FSSAI from Bisleri's Goa manufacturing facility on September 30, 2025.According to the company, the regulator collected six samples, of which five initially met the applicable standards. The sixth recorded bromate at 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre, it mentioned, as per PTI.Following Bisleri's appeal dated November 22, 2025, FSSAI sent the sample to a referral laboratory for retesting. The company said the laboratory found bromate within the prescribed limit but separately flagged the presence of PAHs.Bisleri subsequently arranged an independent test at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which also found bromate within the prescribed limit, it said. The company submitted the results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office through a formal letter dated February 2 this year.Bisleri said it received no further communication from FSSAI and understood the matter to be closed. It also maintained that it had not received any formal notice by email or in hard copy.However, FSSAI announced on Sunday, November 22, that it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd after finding its packaged drinking water sample "unsafe".In its statement on Monday, Bisleri said it would cooperate with the regulator to address the issue and reiterated that its packaged drinking water was safe for consumption."Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls of over 90 tests across our 10-step manufacturing process," the company said.

headline: Rahul Gandhi keeps painting Bharat in a bad light. He must study Nehru’s foreign policy
content: A Sanskrit subashita dictates that some things must be kept secret and shouldn’t be spoken about in public. They include age, wealth, mantra, problems in one’s home, sex, medicine, insults, austerity, and charity: आयुर्वित्तं गृहच्छिद्रं मन्त्रमैथुनभेषजम्। अपमानं तपो दानं नव गोप्यानि यत्नतः॥ Our erstwhile “youth icon” Rahul Gandhi, despite his newfound love for his “Hindu roots”, would do well to spend some time reading the ancient texts that form the basis of this philosophical way of life. Perhaps he would then not indulge in what those in the West call “airing dirty laundry”. I am not referring to his infamously embarrassing gaffe at the book launch of his mother’s memoir, which is now a meme on Instagram and X. Nor am I referring to his immaturity. Rather, I am referring to Gandhi’s constant need to paint Bharat in a bad light, seeking validation from I don’t know who, especially in spaces that are supposedly “intellectual”. In my column last week, I countered his missive from Columbia University that India is facing an economic disaster. On 19 November, during an interaction with students at the University of Chicago, Gandhi yet again made a factually incorrect statement describing India as a “side player” in global affairs. He based the argument on the immediate example of Pakistan’s involvement in discussions between the US and Iran, with India “watching” on the sidelines.

headline: Australia to treat AI as key foreign policy challenge
content: SYDNEY, Nov 23 (Reuters) – Australia will treat artificial intelligence as a key challenge in its foreign policy, warning the technology was reshaping society’s foundations and giving overseas actors new ways to interfere in its democracy. In a major address to parliament on Tuesday setting out Australia’s changing foreign policy approach, Foreign Minister Penny Wong is expected to name AI alongside forces such as the growing influence of middle powers and strategic competition between the US and China. “Technology is transforming the foundations and dimensions of economic and strategic power,” Wong will say. “Artificial intelligence and emerging technologies are spreading and disrupting faster than any previous revolutionary technologies — reordering our lives, economies and militaries in ways we cannot fully foresee.” It comes after the Australian government earlier this month announced it would toughen its AI regulation, mandating companies report breaches and establishing a dedicated regulator for the technology, following revelations an OpenAI agent breached the database of the country’s health system. Citing recent foreign disinformation operations, Wong will also warn in her speech, entitled “Securing Australia’s future in a changing world: Australian foreign policy for a new era”, that AI tools make interference in Australia’s democracy by foreign actors faster, cheaper, and harder to recognise.

headline: SC relief for PACL plot holders in Mohali, Bathinda; cash buyers face uncertainty
content: The Supreme Court has laid down a time-bound mechanism to settle long-pending claims of plot holders in PACL (Pearl Agrotech Corporation Limited) residential projects in Sectors 100 and 104 of Mohali and Bathinda. The order brings relief to hundreds of allottees who paid through banking channels. However, those who purchased plots through cash transactions face uncertainty, with the court directing that such plots be treated as unsold and auctioned. The order could also affect people who subsequently purchased properties in these projects through resale, particularly where the original allotments involved cash payments or did not meet the court’s prescribed payment conditions. A Bench of Justices Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Atul S Chandurkar accepted the categorisation framework prepared by the Justice (Retd) R M Lodha Committee based on audits conducted by chartered accountants. It also prescribed deadlines for issuing sale certificates, recovering outstanding payments, and refunding eligible buyers. The directions cover 2,032 units in Mohali’s Sectors 100 and 104, and 1,078 units in Bathinda. The allotments were divided into five categories, depending on the mode and timing of payments, particularly in relation to the Supreme Court’s February 2, 2016, order freezing PACL assets. Under Category I, buyers who paid the entire consideration through banking channels, including RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement) and cheques, will be treated as having purchased the plots. The Recovery Officer under Section 28A of the SEBI Act has been directed to issue sale certificates and no-objection certificates (NOCs) within eight weeks. Possession certificates will also be issued within the same period to eligible allottees who have not received them. This category covers 92 allottees in Sector 100, 241 in Sector 104 and 203 in Bathinda. Category II covers buyers who paid more than 50 per cent of the consideration through banking channels before February 2, 2016. Their allotments will also be treated as sold, subject to payment of the outstanding amount. The Lodha Committee will issue statements detailing the balance consideration and applicable contributions towards internal development works within eight weeks. Buyers will then have 30 days to deposit the amount through banking channels. A one-time extension of up to 30 days may be granted for valid reasons. Failure to clear the dues will result in the plot being treated as unsold, making the buyer eligible only for a refund under Category III. The category covers 227 allottees in Sector 100, 138 in Sector 104, and 126 in Bathinda. However, buyers who paid less than 50 per cent through banking channels will not get ownership of their plots. Rejecting pleas by residents' welfare associations and builders, including Pearl City Mohali Residents Welfare Association, Pinnacle Self Supporting Co-operative Welfare House Building Society, and KLV Builders & Developers, to allow payment of the balance at prevailing market or collector rates, the court ruled that fresh title transfers after nearly a decade would further prolong the proceedings. The mentioned plots will be auctioned, and eligible buyers will receive refunds of audited payments along with 8 per cent interest within three months of the successful auction. This category includes 117 allottees in Sector 100, 66 in Sector 104 and 16 in Bathinda. The court has also refused relief to buyers who made payments in cash, either fully or partially. Such plots will be treated as unsold inventory and put up for auction. Buyers who made payments through banking channels after February 2, 2016, will also not get ownership but will be entitled to refunds of their audited payments with 8 per cent interest within three months of the successful auction. Importantly, the court clarified that cash buyers can approach competent civil courts by filing suits for recovery or declaration against PACL Ltd. The existing restriction on litigation protects SEBI and the Lodha Committee from being impleaded as defendants, but does not prevent proceedings against PACL. The court also addressed resale cases. Buyers who acquired allotments from original allottees during the pendency of the SC proceedings will be governed by the category applicable to the original allotment. Meanwhile, applications by Navdeep Kumar and Dr Surinder Kumar Bansal, seeking inclusion in Category I, were referred to the Lodha Committee for verification, subject to SEBI’s approval. The order does not automatically cancel every resale transaction. The legal position depends on the original allotment’s payment category. Cash buyers have been left to pursue their claims against PACL through civil courts.

headline: As Guru Nanak Prakash Purab is celebrated tomorrow, a curious question about dates
content: Ahead of Guru Nanak Prakash Purab on Tuesday, November 24, a debate has emerged on social media over why the first Sikh Guru’s birth anniversary is being observed in Maghar, the ninth month of the traditional calendar, instead of Kattak (Kartik), the month traditionally associated with his birth. US-based Sikh scholar and writer Gurcharanjit Singh Lamba explains the calendar calculation behind this year’s observance of Guru Nanak Prakash Purab and why, in his view, questions about the timing are misplaced and could confuse the general public. Why is Prakash Purab being celebrated in Maghar this year? According to the lunar calendar, it is not Maghar. November 24 falls on Kattak Purnima (the full-moon day), which marks the end of the lunar month of Kattak. The same date corresponds to 9 Maghar in the solar calendar. The Gurpurab is being observed on Kattak Purnima, in accordance with the lunar calendar. How do the two calendars differ this year? According to the solar calendar, Kattak began on October 17 and ended on November 15, with Maghar beginning on November 16. But according to the lunar calendar, Kattak began on October 27, with Kattak Vadi 1, and ends on November 24, which is Kattak Purnima. Thus, the same day is Kattak Purnima in the lunar calendar and 9 Maghar in the solar calendar. There is no contradiction; the two calendars simply calculate months differently. Which calendar is followed for celebrating the Gurpurabs? According to Lamba, most religious observances and Gurpurabs commemorating the Sikh Gurus follow the lunar calendar, with their dates determined by lunar dates such as Purnima, Sudi, and Vadi. “The SGPC and the Akal Takht also follow this system for observing the Gurpurabs. An SGPC communication issued in November 2022 refers to the observance in the context of the traditional lunar date. Therefore, the solar-calendar month should not be used to question a Gurpurab whose date is determined by the lunar calendar,” he says. Has Kattak Purnima fallen in the solar month of Maghar in the past? Yes. Lamba points out that Guru Nanak Dev’s 500th Prakash Purab was celebrated on November 23, 1969, which too was Kattak Purnima and corresponded to 9 Maghar in the solar calendar. Such differences occur because the two calendars follow separate calculations. The lunar date remains Kattak Purnima, irrespective of the solar month in which it falls. Why does this confusion keep surfacing? Such confusion began to arise, particularly following the introduction of the new Sikh calendar. Lamba says the two systems should not be mixed up. The solar calendar marks the beginning of months through Sangrands, while the lunar calendar follows the phases of the moon. Gurpurabs are linked to their prescribed lunar dates and, therefore, do not fall on a fixed English-calendar date every year. He says questions raised by comparing a lunar date with a solar month create avoidable confusion among devotees. Even introducing a new calendar, he argues, should not blur the distinction between the two systems or the traditional lunar dates on which Gurpurabs are observed. The clarification is simple: November 24 is Kattak Purnima in the lunar calendar and 9 Maghar in the solar calendar. Guru Nanak Dev’s Prakash Purab is being celebrated on Kattak Purnima, he concluded.

headline: Walking 10,000 Steps A Day? Your Health Insurance Policy Could Reward You
content: Morning walks, gym sessions, and regular workouts do more than keep you fit; they might also help lower your health insurance costs. Many health plans now reward policyholders with points for staying active, completing health assessments, or going for routine check-ups. However, staying active alone does not guarantee automatic perks. Knowing how your insurer’s wellness programme works, which activities qualify, and how to redeem your earned points can help you turn everyday healthy habits into real savings. Not every health insurance wellness programme cuts your renewal bill directly. While some policies turn earned activity points into renewal premium discounts once you hit a certain target, others follow completely different reward structures worth checking beforehand. (Image: Canva) Several insurers provide a wellness wallet where your accumulated points carry actual rupee value. Depending on your policy terms, you can put this balance toward lowering your next renewal premium or paying for eligible medical expenses. (Image: Canva) Some policies skip premium discounts altogether and instead let you redeem points for everyday medical needs. You may be able to use those rewards toward doctor consultations, prescribed medicines, or routine preventive health check-ups. (Image: Canva) Certain health plans extend perks like fitness sessions, diet consultations, or discounts on medical services. However, check the fine print carefully; some insurers merely help arrange these wellness services while leaving you to pay out of pocket. (Image: Canva) Before tracking workouts, confirm whether your plan actually includes a wellness programme or requires an add-on fee. Next, register on the insurer’s app, link your policy, and sync your phone’s step tracker or smartwatch properly. (Image: Canva) Walking 10,000 steps daily will not earn anything unless tracked through the approved app. Some insurers also ask you to complete an initial health assessment before unlocking points for workouts, check-ups, fitness challenges, or marathons. (Image: Canva) Make it a habit to verify that earned points are regularly credited to your account. Certain activities, such as diagnostic check-ups or fitness events, may require uploading medical reports or proof within a strict deadline. (Image: Canva)

headline: Non-bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case
content: A Delhi court on Monday issued a non-bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case filed by Vikas Pandey over allegations made in a video that the BJP’s Information and Technology cell had attempted to bribe him. Judicial Magistrate First Class Anam Rais Khan of Saket courts issued the warrant and listed the matter for December 3. The case relates to a video Rathee created in May 2018 alleging that the BJP IT cell had attempted to bribe Pandey. Rathee tweeted the video, which was later retweeted by Arvind Kejriwal, who was then Delhi chief minister. Pandey subsequently initiated defamation proceedings, alleging that the circulation of the video had harmed his reputation. In his complaint, he alleged that Rathee, who ordinarily resides in Germany, had published and circulated a video titled “BJP IT Cell Part II” containing false allegations against him. Rathee was first summoned in the case in July 2019. In October, the court issued fresh summons to him at the Gurugram address he had submitted after being informed that he was at his residence there. The court had earlier directed that the fresh summons be issued at the Gurugram address. Later in October, Judicial Magistrate First Class Rahul Jain, who is hearing the defamation case, issued bailable warrants against Rathee after the court was informed that his premises in Gurugram were locked. The bailable warrants followed the fresh summons issued to him. Pandey had earlier sought preponement of the matter, saying Rathee, who ordinarily resides abroad, was in India at the time in connection with the CJP protests. The latest non-bailable warrant was issued as the court continued proceedings in the defamation case, with the matter now listed for December 3.

headline: Pilot targets Mann govt, says Punjab needs ‘serious and responsible’ government
content: Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Monday launched a sharp attack on the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government, accusing it of failing to address Punjab’s key concerns and losing public confidence. He said Punjab, being a sensitive border state, needed a “serious and responsible” government.Taking a dig at Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Pilot alleged that the state government had focused more on rhetoric and humour than on governance and resolving people's problems. He said people were looking for a change and the Congress was well placed to offer a credible alternative.“Punjab is a border and sensitive state. It needs a serious and responsible government,” he said, questioning the Mann government's handling of the state's affairs.Pilot also questioned the BJP's pitch of a ‘double-engine government’, saying its electoral performance had exposed the limitations of the claim. He said the BJP needed to introspect on why its promise of better governance through the double-engine model had failed to win public confidence.On the Congress's candidate selection for the Punjab Assembly elections, Pilot said the party's state election committee would meet soon, while the screening committee had already been constituted to begin the process.He said candidates would be selected on the basis of merit, public feedback and winnability, indicating that the party would prioritise electoral prospects while finalising its nominees.On the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Pilot said the Congress and the Samajwadi Party would contest together. He said seat-sharing discussions would be completed soon and expressed confidence that the alliance would form the government in the state.

headline: Nagaland partners with Starscapes to develop astro-tourism across the state
content: The Government of Nagaland has signed an MoU with Starscapes to develop astro-tourism, promote dark-sky conservation and create astronomy-led visitor experiences across the state. As the first initiative under the partnership, Starscapes will serve as the exclusive astro-tourism partner for Hornbill Festival 2026, offering guided stargazing activities at Kisama in December. The Government of Nagaland has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Starscapes to develop and promote astro-tourism across the state, with guided stargazing experiences at the Hornbill Festival 2026 marking the first initiative under the partnership. Announced by Temjen Imna Along, Minister of Tourism and Higher Education, Government of Nagaland, the partnership aims to leverage the state's natural landscapes and night skies to develop astronomy-led tourism experiences. Starscapes will serve as the exclusive astro-tourism partner for the Hornbill Festival 2026, where it will organise a series of stargazing and astronomy activities for visitors at Kisama in December. The collaboration extends beyond the festival, with plans to develop astro-tourism and astronomy education across Nagaland. According to the state government, the partnership will focus on training local youth, developing observatories across districts and positioning Nagaland as an emerging dark-sky destination. "Nagaland has always looked to the sky in our stories, our seasons, our sense of place. This Hornbill Festival, we are proud to announce a formal and exclusive partnership with Starscapes Experiences, India's leading astro-tourism company, bringing guided stargazing and astronomy experiences to our festival grounds this December at Kisama," said Along.
