headline: BJP to dispel top-down image, senior leaders to fan out, meet workers in UP
content: Marking a shift from the top-down process that has characterised much of the BJP’s approach over the last decade in Uttar Pradesh, the party has started its preparations for the coming Assembly elections by sending senior leaders to hear out workers on the ground. Steered by the BJP’s UP in-charge Vinod Tawde and joint in-charges Medha Kulkarni, Jagdish Patel, Pradeep Verma and Anant Ojha, along with state BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary, several teams of senior leaders will be visiting every district and meet local leaders to discuss their concerns besides organisational gaps and ground realities. The process got underway with the recent two-day chintan baithak of the party held in Mathura, attended by about 50 BJP leaders, including party president Nitin Nabin and national general secretary (organisation) B L Santhosh, where each participant was allocated time to put forward their views. Sources said that the idea that senior leaders tour the districts was discussed at a meeting in Gorakhpur earlier this month, which was also attended by Nabin. At the meeting, Jagdish Patel said that during a recent visit to Bundelkhand, he had been approached by villagers with complaints regarding implementation of the Har Ghar Jal Yojana. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said an inquiry had been ordered in that matter. Sources said a senior minister then urged all the leaders present to listen to Patel’s views, holding that they should all speak freely or else such internal meetings would be futile. The minister also remarked that a major grievance of the workers has been that their voices were not heard, sources said. With the message going out, “an atmosphere of patient listening” marked the Mathura meeting, as per sources present. Leaders said that B L Santhosh went on to ask a pointed question as to who among the participants had not met CM Adityanath personally since 2017 (when he first became CM). Pushkar Mishra, Ranjana Upadhyay and Tryambak Tripathi – all leaders from the Brahmin community, which believes the Adityanath regime is “Thakur-focused” – raised their hands. They were asked to meet the CM after the session. Gonda, Mishra and Tripathi, who have been former office-bearers in the UP BJP, later shared photographs of their meeting with Adityanath on social media. When contacted, one of the three leaders confirmed they met the CM, without sharing any more details. Incidentally, while former state BJP presidents and current general secretaries were invited for the Mathura session, ex-state chiefs Kalraj Mishra, Vinay Katiyar and Om Prakash Singh, who have not been very active in the party, did not attend. Katiyar said he was not informed about the meeting. BJP’s challenges Immediately after the Mathura meeting, Adityanath travelled to Delhi to hold discussions with Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Nabin and Santhosh, which was seen as an effort to also realign leaders at the highest levels in the BJP. Shah was expected to be present at the Mathura meeting but did not attend. Incidentally, the party meeting was originally to be held in Vrindavan in October, but was postponed, with one reason cited by sources being the unavailability of Shah. As per sources, the state BJP is also feeling the absence of national general secretary Sunil Bansal. As the UP general secretary (organisation) for several years, Bansal played a significant role in the party’s successive wins, but later distanced himself due to differences with the state leadership. Bansal shifted to the Centre in August 2022 as national general secretary of the BJP and is now the party’s in-charge of West Bengal and Telangana. One of the reasons for the setback to the BJP in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, particularly in Uttar Pradesh, was seen to be the lack of involvement of the RSS in the campaign. With the Samajwadi Party getting a new lease of life from the 2024 results, and its chief Akhilesh Yadav on the offensive, the BJP does not want to take any chances. Hindutva as the message The choice of Mathura as the venue of the meeting was also deliberate, coinciding with a renewed focus by the BJP on the Krishna Janmabhoomi dispute. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said during the meeting that a grand Krishna temple at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Eidgah mosque site in Mathura was very much a part of the BJP’s poll agenda. Over a dozen petitions in the Mathura case are pending before the Allahabad High Court. Sources said the BJP feels that Akhilesh’s ‘PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak)’ narrative cannot be effectively countered by the BJP’s social justice slogans alone, and that a stronger Hindutva message is required. Along with the call for a Krishna Janmabhoomi temple, the slogan Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De emerged from the Mathura conclave. This push may also help the BJP make inroads in the Yadav vote bank, which claims kinship to Lord Krishna – though, as an insider pointed out, no delegate from the Yadav community found representation at the meeting. The BJP is aware that whenever a party has been able to cash in on the social justice theme in UP – as Akhilesh is trying to do – it has found the going tough. The late Sushma Swaraj once observed that a cheque can be encashed only once, in response to questions about whether the campaign for a Ram temple in Ayodhya alone would sustain political advantage for the BJP. In another change from 2024, the BJP is likely to avoid slogans such as “Abki Baar, Chaar Sau Paar”, setting for itself a 400-plus seat target in the general elections. The Opposition projected it as a sign of the BJP’s arrogance, and played on fears that a dominant party like it would “alter” the Constitution and remove provisions such as reservations once in power.

headline: Two Army soldiers accidentally run over by tank during military exercise in Hisar
content: Two Army soldiers died after they were accidentally run over by a tank during a routine military training exercise near Bhojraj village in Haryana's Hisar district on Saturday, police said on Sunday. According to preliminary information, dust kicked up by the movement of tanks during the training obscured the tank driver's vision and led to the accident, police said. The deceased were identified as Naik Manish Kumar, a resident of Uttar Pradesh's Shamli, and Naik Ankush Kumar of Uttar Pradesh's Budaun, both of whom were positioned at the front of the tank, police said. ' A Hisar police spokesperson said, “Both soldiers sustained critical injuries and were immediately rushed to the Military Hospital in Hisar, where doctors declared them dead. Post-mortem examinations of both personnel have been conducted, and senior Army officials were informed about the incident.” “As many as 32 tanks were participating in the routine military exercise on Saturday. Army personnel were deployed at designated positions on the ground as part of the exercise. However, as the tanks moved in formation, they raised a thick cloud of dust, considerably reducing visibility,” the spokesperson said. “It seems the driver of one of the tanks failed to notice the two soldiers positioned ahead and ran them over.” Police sources said Ankush Kumar was scheduled to proceed on leave from Sunday. He had spoken to his family members a few hours before the accident on Saturday. Manish Kumar's father, Ramveer, had also served in the Army, police said. Hisar Superintendent of Police Siddhant Jain told The Indian Express that inquest proceedings under Section 194 (accidental deaths) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, were initiated.

headline: Punjab news: EC orders FIR against Akali Dal Patiala in-charge over threats to minister
content: Following the directions of the Punjab State Election Commission, the Patiala police have registered an FIR against the Shiromani Akali Dal’s (SAD) Patiala Rural halqa in-charge, Jaspal Singh Bittu Chatha, for allegedly issuing threats to a Cabinet minister and serving officers involved with the polling process. Notably, the model code of conduct is in place ahead of repolling in Patiala municipal wards.According to the information, an FIR has been registered at civil lines police station under section 192 (malignantly giving illegal provocation that is likely to cause rioting), 353(1)(b) (statements conducing to public mischief), 352 (intentional insult) and 351(3) (criminal intimidation) of the BNS.Senior police officers confirmed that though the offences were bailable, if proven, the accused could face a jail term ranging from two to seven years.As per the FIR, a copy of which is with The Tribune, the state election commission brought a video clip to the notice of the district electoral officer. “Please find enclosed a video clip received at the Commission today, wherein a person is seen interacting with the press and allegedly issuing threats to a Minister and government officers who are directly involved in current election process”, says the complaint mentioned in the FIR.The complaint further read, “The Commission desires you to look into and take action as per following: 1. To ascertain genuineness of the video clip; 2. To ascertain identity of the gentlemen in video; 3. To take necessary action, including preventive measures as necessary, and lodging of FIR under the relevant sections of BNS and election laws as may be applicable”.Speaking to The Tribune, Bittu Chatha said the SAD was not afraid of such FIRs and he would continue to raise his voice against the government. “Anyone who highlights the government’s failures is booked in cases on flimsy grounds,” he said.A senior police officer closely monitoring the case said the Deputy Commissioner can order that the accused be kept away from the electoral process till voting is complete.Polling will take place on November 28 from 8 am to 4 pm. The re-elections follow a Supreme Court decision ordering fresh polls in wards where alleged irregularities were reported during the previous municipal elections.

headline: Changing tastes : Processed food basket raises health concerns
content: THE rapid change in rural India's food consumption patterns should ring alarm bells. An IIM Ahmedabad report, based on household expenditure data, reveals that the share of rural household spending on processed food has risen 2.35 times in 24 years — from 4.19% in 1999-2000 to 9.84% in 2023-24. The corresponding increase in urban areas has been considerably lower. Packaged food, beverages and refreshments have overtaken cereals, milk and vegetables as the largest food expenditure category in both rural and urban households. This is not merely a lifestyle shift; it has significant public health implications.

headline: PM’s critique exposes a deeper policy failure
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has asked some pertinent questions to Corporate India, though some of them he must answer himself. The questions that he posed to the top leaders of industry and business have a clear accusatory and reprimanding tone, unusual for a prime minister long regarded as business-friendly. Yet, the questions are relevant. He asked whether companies had increased employment and raised wages after the government lowered corporate tax rates, raised the income-tax concession threshold, and made other concessions. The concessions should have incentivised investment, expanded consumption, and created jobs. Instead, companies strengthened their balance sheets and increased profits without sharing them with society. As Modi put it, industry had an “insatiable hunger for concessions”, but a portion of the resulting profits did not flow back to society. Since these concessions came from public resources, corporate beneficiaries were expected to honour a broader social and economic contract. .'Tax cuts given, but where are the jobs and hikes?' PM Modi asks industry leaders.The Modi government reduced the headline corporate tax rate from 30% to 22% to encourage investment, production, and employment. GST replaced multiple indirect taxes, and further formalised the economy. But many analyses, including government surveys, have shown that corporate profits have grown many times more than wage expenditure. In all these years, the government made little effort to effectively deal with this mismatch. It has not created a suitable environment or adopted policies that would prompt industry to create jobs and increase wages. It has taken credit for the high GDP numbers even as the claimed growth was largely jobless growth. Real incomes stagnated or declined even as inflation went up. Labour-intensive industries needed greater support, skill development programmes required strengthening, and MSMEs should have received better assistance. Instead, demonetisation severely damaged the MSME sector, which provides livelihood and employment to millions of people. It has yet to fully recover. While the wealth got increasingly concentrated, the government did not adopt policies to reduce inequality. .Opposition parties and other critics have long criticised the government for favouring big business, promoting crony capitalism, and failing to create jobs or expand social and economic good. The government has consistently rejected these charges. But the prime minister has now had to accept some of them, though he is blaming the corporate sector for them. He seems eager to shed his ‘pro-corporate’ image and adopt a new image, perhaps in response to Gen Z’s demand for jobs and a shifting political mood.

headline: Eight months on, Noida International Airport at Jewar awaits 1st international flight
content: Nearly eight months after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Noida International Airport at Jewar, not a single scheduled international passenger flight has taken off from the much-publicised project.Instead, the airport, developed as a second aviation gateway for the National Capital Region (NCR), is struggling with declining passenger traffic, limited airline operations and poor connectivity.Recently, the Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved the proposal to rename Noida International Airport at Jewar as Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar, on October 9.According to the latest Airports Authority of India (AAI) data, Jewar handled just 55,890 passengers in September, a decline of 27 per cent from 76,593 in July. Passenger traffic had fallen to 58,520 in August. Aircraft movements, including take-offs and landings, declined from 1,049 in July to 893 in September, a fall of nearly 15 per cent. The airport handled only 2,11,525 passengers between June 15 and September 30, with not a single international passenger recorded.Commercial flight operations at the airport began on June 15 after its inauguration in March.Despite being designated an international airport, Jewar currently has only two passenger airlines, IndiGo and Akasa Air. According to airport officials, the airport had expanded its network from five to 16 domestic destinations, with around 35 daily flights. However, no scheduled international passenger service has begun, even five months after commercial operations commenced.The figures raise questions about the pace at which the airport can establish itself as an alternative to Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA), particularly when its first phase has been designed to handle 1.2 crore passengers annually.The airport’s troubles began barely a month after commercial operations commenced on June 15. Akasa Air, among the first airlines to launch services from Jewar, temporarily suspended flights in July, announcing that operations would resume from October 1. The airline attributed the decision to network optimisation driven by passenger demand, seasonality and aircraft deployment requirements.The suspension highlighted the difficulties airlines face in establishing new routes from greenfield airports, where passenger demand takes time to develop and the absence of established connecting networks can affect commercial viability.Aviation industry sources had earlier pointed out that airlines operating from newly opened airports were struggling to attract adequate passenger traffic, forcing them to review schedules and aircraft deployment.According to sources, inadequate last-mile connectivity and supporting infrastructure were also influencing passengers’ choice of airports. With Delhi’s IGI Airport offering a wider network of domestic and international flights, passengers have fewer reasons to shift to Jewar unless airlines offer competitive fares, convenient timings and reliable connectivity.The airport operator, Zurich Airport International AG, had itself warned in August that operations would grow more slowly than anticipated because of the challenging geopolitical environment and uncertainty surrounding near-term performance. The absence of international passenger flights remains another concern. Although the airport was developed to serve overseas destinations, airlines have yet to announce confirmed international passenger schedules.Airport officials have said discussions are underway with carriers serving West Asia and Southeast Asia, but the launch of international services depends on regulatory approvals, commercial considerations and airline network plans.Another challenge is connectivity. Unlike Delhi’s IGI Airport, Jewar does not have a direct Metro or railway connection. Passengers currently depend on private vehicles, taxis and bus services, making travel time and accessibility important factors in choosing an airport.

headline: Too Cold To Exercise? Why You Should Start Your Winter Mornings With Surya Namaskar
content: Waking up for exercise on chilly mornings can feel tough, yet starting your day with Surya Namaskar delivers real rewards. Rishikesh yoga teacher Dinesh explains that this sequence connects 12 distinct postures in a deliberate order. Practiced regularly, it builds natural body warmth, strengthens muscles, and improves flexibility across nearly the entire body. For anyone fighting winter sluggishness, this full-body routine offers an approachable way to wake up muscles, boost energy, and begin the morning feeling grounded, active, and ready for the day ahead. Cold mornings often tempt people to stay under blankets, yet practicing Surya Namaskar warms the body naturally and shakes off chilly sluggishness. According to Rishikesh yoga teacher Dinesh, moving through these 12 postures helps keep you active and energized through winter. (Image: Canva) Each round exercises almost every major body area, including your arms, legs, waist, back, abdomen, and shoulders. Smoothly shifting between standing tall, bending forward, lowering near the floor, and arching backward engages multiple muscle groups together. (Image: Canva) Dinesh recommends practicing Surya Namaskar early in the morning around sunrise on an empty stomach. Following a consistent daily routine makes the sequence feel smoother while helping you stay alert and refreshed after waking up. (Image: Canva) Begin standing upright with palms joined in Pranamasana, then reach upward in Hastauttanasana and fold forward into Padahastasana. Continue into Ashwa Sanchalanasana, Dandasana, Ashtanga Namaskar, Bhujangasana, and Parvatasana to complete the first eight postures. (Image: Canva) Finish the full twelve-pose round by repeating Ashwa Sanchalanasana, Padahastasana, and Hastauttanasana before returning to Pranamasana. Performing each posture in its set order gives the sequence rhythm, balance, and steady physical flow. (Image: Canva) Regular practice strengthens muscles and gradually increases body flexibility without needing heavy equipment. Because the sequence works the arms, legs, waist, and core together, steady daily effort builds noticeable stamina and ease of movement. (Image: Canva) Practicing Surya Namaskar daily during winter generates warmth that counters cold-weather heaviness and fatigue. Consistent rounds also support calorie burn, making this traditional twelve-pose routine a helpful addition to weight management efforts. (Image: Canva)

headline: India maps landslide susceptibility as part of shift from post-disaster relief to landslide management
content: NEW DELHI India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026). He noted that India is progressively shifting its approach to landslide management, from post-disaster relief to prevention, preparedness, and risk reduction, marking a “major transformation” in the country’s disaster management strategy. He was speaking at the 7th World Landslide Forum being held at the Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Faridabad. This is the first time the periodic International Consortium on Landslides and the International Programme on Landslides is being held in India. The 4-day programme brought together international experts, scientists, and policymakers from more than 75 countries. Interdisciplinary research and monitoring Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters. The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

headline: Himachal Pradesh: Ex-BJP candidate claims colleague forged details to get SC certificate
content: NEW DELHI: Former BJP candidate from Himachal Pradesh's Rampur assembly constituency Prem Singh Daraik on Monday accused party leader Kaul Singh Negi of giving false information to obtain a Scheduled Caste certificate.Talking to reporters, Daraik alleged that Negi had hidden details from old official records and provided incorrect information while applying for the certificate. He demanded an investigation into the role of officials involved in issuing it.Daraik said the SDM court in Rampur had, on October 12, 2026, cancelled an order issued by the Rampur Tehsildar on October 29, 2022, and directed the cancellation of the SC certificate issued to Negi on August 16, 2022.He said Negi originally belongs to Nanspo village in Kinnaur district and questioned the verification of documents by the Rampur revenue authorities before issuing the certificate.Daraik said a certificate issued in 2002 mentioned Negi's caste as 'Kinnaura', while another certificate issued in 2004 recorded it as 'Kinnaura Koli'. However, the SC certificate issued by the Rampur Tehsildar in 2022 mentioned his caste as 'Koli'.He alleged that Negi had mentioned his caste as 'Koli' in the online application submitted in 2022 despite older documents recording it as 'Kinnaura Koli'.Daraik also accused the BJP of fielding Negi in the 2022 Assembly elections despite questions over the validity of his certificate, calling it a "betrayal" of the people of Rampur.The political situation in Rampur has heated up following the death of four-time MLA Nand Lal on November 3.Daraik had unsuccessfully contested from the Rampur seat in 2012 and 2017. He was replaced by Negi in the 2022 Assembly elections, which Negi also lost. Congress candidate Nand Lal won all three elections.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Amid poor public response to Census self-enumeration, enumerators fan out in Uttar Pradesh
content: New Delhi Amid poor public response to self-enumeration on the Census portal, enumerators, mostly government school teachers, said they were being “forcibly” deployed to persuade people to complete the process on their personal phones, several enumerators in Uttar Pradesh told The Hindu. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/ In Uttar Pradesh, where the self-enumeration of the Population Enumeration phase is currently underway, Census enumerators are facing several challenges, including the refusal to share One-Time Passwords (OTPs), suspicion on being asked about the number of bank accounts, and difficulty in recalling the date of birth and place of birth of both parents. They faced the least resistance when they asked questions on caste, religion or identity documents (Aadhaar number, Voter ID number, driving license number, passport number), enumerators said. Census 2027: ‘Other’ religions list made predictive text, over 200 entries from earlier list dropped Census 2027: ‘Other’ religions list made predictive text, over 200 entries from earlier list dropped This comes days after The Hindu reported that at least 287 entries such as ISKCON, Gorak Nath, Sanatan, Vedic Dharm, Ramdev etc. had been listed in a drop-down menu for “Other” religions on the portal and then removed Census 2027: ‘Other’ religions list made predictive text, over 200 entries from earlier list dropped storyline 1 Despite examinations and assessments underway in schools, almost all primary school teachers have been deployed on Census duty, although door-to-door enumeration begins on December 1. Each enumerator has been given the task of completing as many self-enumerations as possible through the Census portal, failing which they would be marked absent at their place of work, an enumerator said. Census 2027 is the first digital Census and the first to enumerate castes other than Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and the first to allow self-enumeration. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/census-2027/ Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained As Uttar Pradesh and three other poll-bound States — Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab — prepare to launch the second phase of Census 2027 on December 1, field trainers are briefing about 34 lakh enumerators on 40 questions that will require longer, more sensitive interviews and digital data entry, including caste, religion, Aadhaar access and parents’ details Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained storyline 1 “Unlike door-to-door enumeration, which is done through an app, the self enumeration is to be done on a website (se.census.gov.in). Internet speed is mostly abysmal in rural areas, the page does not upload, and we have to spend over 30 minutes in each household. Although self-enumeration means that people have to fill the details on their own, here, we are being forced to visit households, nudge them for OTPs, and fill the questionnaire on their behalf,” another enumerator said. They were consciously choosing households with few members to meet the target, the enumerator added. “For large households, the process becomes particularly time-consuming as details for each member has to be entered separately. The toughest part is obtaining the OTP needed to log into the portal. Residents often tell us that the government has advised them to not share OTPs with anyone. Their suspicion deepens when we ask about the number of bank accounts they hold, and a considerable amount of time is spent convincing them,” the second enumerator said. ‘ISKCON’, ‘Tantric’, ‘Gorak Nath’: 287 ‘other’ religions briefly listed on Census portal ‘ISKCON’, ‘Tantric’, ‘Gorak Nath’: 287 ‘other’ religions briefly listed on Census portal The drop-down menu under the ‘Others’ category in the question pertaining to the respondent’s religion had 287 options for those not choosing from among the six major religions in India. After The Hindu raised a query about the classification, the drop-down menu was removed from the portal. ‘ISKCON’, ‘Tantric’, ‘Gorak Nath’: 287 ‘other’ religions briefly listed on Census portal storyline 1 The exercise should be renamed as it was hardly “self-enumeration”, the enumerators said. There were no such instructions from the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) to States to deploy enumerators for the self-enumeration phase, an official of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs in Delhi said. “State government officials (who also hold the charge of Principal Census Officers) have only been asked to create awareness about the self-enumeration portal,” the official said. “Regarding Question 10 (C) on caste, we observed that General Category people are prompt with their response. Since it is an open column, we typed whatever response they gave. It is the people from the reserved categories who were little hesitant in sharing the sub-caste identity from the drop-down box,” the first enumerator said. Census 2027 turning out to be farce: Congress Census 2027 turning out to be farce: Congress Census 2027 is turning out to be a farce in many respects. This will have grave implications, Jairam Ramesh said Census 2027 turning out to be farce: Congress storyline 1 Though the RG&CCI did not issue a cumulative figure, according to a May 17 statement and State government’s records, around 1.56 crore households had self-enumerated during the first phase of the Census, the House Listing Operations (HLO), which started on April 1 and concluded on September 30. India’s population was 121.09 crore according to the 2011 Census. During the first phase, 24.25 lakh enumeration blocks (EBs) were marked across the country, except in Manipur, where the exercise has been indefinitely deferred. Each EB comprises around 700-850 people or 150 households. In Uttar Pradesh, around 3.9 lakh EBs were mapped. As this is also the first digital Census, around 34 lakh enumerators, including private individuals, are required capture the data on an app on their personal phones. Census 2027: Statistics and Statecraft Census 2027: Statistics and Statecraft The history of the Indian census questionnaire is, in many ways, the history of the Indian state itself. Its changing questions have mirrored not only the country’s developmental trajectory but also the political priorities and anxieties of the governments that framed them.” Census 2027: Statistics and Statecraft storyline 1 The door-to-door enumeration of the Population Enumeration (PE) or the second phase of Census is all set to begin on December 1 in the poll-bound States of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa, ahead of the rest of the country, where the exercise will commence January 24, 2027. The PE phase concluded on September 30 in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of J&K, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. The PE phase will ask a set of 40 questions, including 13 new questions that will be asked for the first time —caste (other than Scheduled Tribe/Scheduled Caste); religion, place, and date of birth of both parents; number of bank accounts; spouse’s name; nationality; digital literacy; permanent residential address; place of COVID-19 vaccination; passport number; driving licence availability; and mobile, Aadhaar and voter ID numbers, if available.

headline: Silent Valleys, Empty Orchards: How Manali’s Locals Survive the Lean Months !
content: Manali — When the bustling tourist crowds thin out along the Mall Road and the final crates of apples and off-season vegetables leave the orchards for the plains, a quiet resilience settles over the Manali valley. For the residents of this Himalayan hub, life during the off-season—when hotel rooms sit vacant and agricultural harvests have ended—is a master class in adaptation, community reliance, and careful financial planning. In a region where the economy rests heavily on two seasonal pillars—hospitality and horticulture—the transition into the lean months requires families to shift gears dramatically. For most local households, survival during the off-season begins months earlier. Because income from tourism and cash crops like apples, plums, peas, and cauliflower arrives in concentrated bursts, families treat peak-season earnings as a year-round reserve rather than immediate disposable income. During the off-season, spending tightens across the valley. Discretionary expenses are paused, and households rely on savings accumulated during the summer and autumn rushes to cover winter essentials, children’s education, and medical needs. With hotels operating at bare-minimum staff and orchards dormant, many locals pivot to alternative, smaller-scale income streams. As temperatures drop, traditional Kullvi weaving takes center stage. Women across villages like Vashisht, Old Manali, and Naggar spend their afternoons weaving shawls, caps (topis), and woolen socks, selling them to local cooperatives or stockpiling them for the next tourist wave.

headline: CM Sukhu Inaugurates Kangra Software Tech Park
content: Dharamshala: Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu today inaugurated the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) Centre at Chetru, near Gaggal Airport in Kangra district, constructed at a cost of Rs. 18.29 crore. The centre is expected to support 15–20 budding entrepreneurs and generate employment for 350–400 people over the next five years. Equipped with modern plug-and-play incubation facilities, the centre offers 106 workstations, four managers’ cabins and 5,031 sq. ft. of incubation space, besides an auditorium, conference rooms, Network Operations Centre and other essential facilities. The Chief Minister said the initiative would strengthen Himachal Pradesh’s IT ecosystem, attract investments and promote start-ups and entrepreneurship. He added that the government was committed to creating a technology-driven economy and providing skilled youth with employment opportunities within the state, thereby checking migration in search of jobs. Sukhu expressed confidence that the STPI Centre would emerge as a major hub for IT activities, innovation and entrepreneurship in the region. Member of Parliament Anurag Sharma, MLA Suresh Kumar, Principal Advisor to the Chief Minister (Innovation, Digital Technologies and Governance) Gokul Butail, Wool Federation Chairman Manoj Thakur, Congress leader Devender Jaggi, Secretary Health Ashish Singhmar, Director Digital Technologies and Governance Abhishek Verma, Deputy Commissioner Hemraj Bairwa, SP Kulbhushan Verma and other dignitaries were present on the occasion. Arvind Sharma is an award winning bi-lingual journalist with more than 20 years of experience.

headline: Paid Rs 90,000 for wedding memories but got no photos or video, man wins Rs 1.4 lakh
content: A man who paid Rs 90,000 for his wedding arrangements, including a 350-photo album and a 3.5-hour video, was allegedly left without either despite clearing the entire bill. More than four years later, a Himachal Pradesh consumer commission has directed the tent house owner to deliver the wedding photographs and video or pay Rs 1.4 lakh to the complainant, including the compensation. The Una District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president D R Thakur and member Neelam Gupta were hearing a complaint filed by Balbir Singh against Heera Lal, who operates a tent house in Shimla, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice for failing to deliver his wedding album and videography despite receiving Rs 90,000, and seeking appropriate relief. “The complainant through evidence has proved this fact that he has paid Rupees 90,000 to opposite party and opposite party had promised to hand over the album of photos and vediography of marriage to complainant. But despite that opposite party has not provided the same to complainant,” the commission said on November 5. Tent house owners provide equipment and services for weddings and other functions. Singh had allegedly hired Lal for his July 2022 wedding, agreeing to pay Rs 90,000 for tents, a 350-photo album and 3.5 hours of videography. Despite paying the full amount in three instalments, the last on July 25, 2022, Singh never received the album or video despite repeated requests, prompting him to approach the consumer commission on August 6, 2024. Man pays Rs 90,000 in three instalments According to the complaint, Singh got married in Shimla on July 18, 2022, and the celebrations continued for three days. The marriage invitation card produced before the commission recorded the wedding dates as July 17 and 18. The total consideration for the tent house services was fixed at Rs 90,000. Singh paid Rs 25,000 through an online payment app via his father's account on July 2, 2022. He later paid Rs 55,000 in cash on July 19. Heera Lal contacted Singh later and asked him to clear the remaining Rs 10,000, assuring him that he would hand over the album and videography after payment. Singh transferred the amount through an online payment app on July 25, 2022. However, the promised photographs and video were never delivered. Singh later approached the commission alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The commission examined Singh's affidavit, marriage invitation card and payment receipts. The records established the digital payments of Rs 25,000 and Rs 10,000, while Singh stated on oath that he had paid the remaining Rs 55,000 in cash. The commission noted that Lal had been served but did not appear before it and was proceeded against ex parte (without hearing his side). It held that Singh had established payment of the entire Rs 90,000 and the service provider's promise to deliver the wedding album and videography. However, neither had been supplied. Finding a deficiency in service, the commission allowed the complaint. 30 days to deliver album The commission directed Heera Lal to hand over the wedding photograph album and videography within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order. If he fails to comply, he must refund Rs 90,000 with interest at 9 per cent per annum, calculated from the date of filing of the complaint until realisation. The commission also awarded Singh Rs 30,000 for mental tension and harassment, and Rs 20,000 towards litigation expenses. Thus, if the promised material is not delivered, the monetary liability will amount to Rs 1.4 lakh, comprising the conditional refund, compensation, and litigation expenses. Interest on the refund will be additional. Singh presented the complaint on August 6, 2024. Takeaway Consumers who pay for wedding photography and videography but do not receive the promised deliverables can approach consumer forums for compensation. Payment receipts, digital transaction records, and evidence of the agreed services can help establish deficiency in service. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states (Himachal Pradesh: 1800-180-8087) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. headline: Himachal BJP protests Cong minister Jagat Singh’s comments on Rafale, Indian Army
content: Hamirpur (HP), Nov 23 (PTI) BJP’s ex-servicemen cell on Monday staged a protest in Himachal Pradesh’s Hamirpur against Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi’s controversial remarks on Rafale fighter jets and the Indian Army. The minister made the comments on November 18, during a Himachal Pradesh Assembly debate on an adjournment motion, which were later expunged. During the demonstration, ex-servicemen and BJP workers raised slogans, carried out a symbolic funeral procession, burnt his effigy, and demanded an apology. Addressing the protesters, Purushottam Guleria, state convener of BJP Himachal Pradesh cells, described Negi’s remarks as “unfortunate” and called the Indian Army the “pride and honour of the nation”. “Our brave soldiers guard the borders under arduous conditions and, when necessary, make the supreme sacrifice for the motherland. His irresponsible remarks regarding the Army and the nation’s defense capabilities are highly unfortunate,” he said. “There is deep resentment among ex-servicemen regarding the comments made by minister Jagat Singh Negi. The Congress government must clarify whether it endorses the minister’s statement,” he added.

Restraint and moderation, rather than agitational language, are the hallmarks of the paper.The Tribune has two sister publications, Punjabi Tribune (in Punjabi) and Dainik Tribune (in Hindi).

headline: Aditya Birla Group set to run Himachal’s new health insurance scheme
content: The Aditya Birla Group is set to operate a health insurance scheme for the general public in Himachal Pradesh after emerging as the lowest bidder in the tenders floated by the state government for the purpose.According to sources, the government and the group are holding final discussions to fine-tune the scheme, which is likely to be launched next year.The proposed scheme will replace the government’s Himcare health assurance scheme, under which beneficiary families are entitled to cashless health coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh annually. Under the new scheme, eligible families will be entitled to annual health coverage of up to Rs 10 lakh.Sources said there would be different categories of beneficiaries, with the premium varying according to the financial condition of each family. “Extremely poor families may not have to pay any premium or may be charged a nominal amount to avail themselves of the scheme,” an official said. It is learnt that the Aditya Birla Group has quoted a premium of around Rs 4,300 per family per annum.Government employees and pensioners will not be eligible for the scheme. However, efforts are being made to bring contractual and outsourced employees under its ambit.

headline: Himachal Plans Heli-Taxi Services to Hamirpur, Chamba and Palampur; Seeks Expansion of Flight Routes
content: The Himachal Pradesh government is stepping up efforts to strengthen air connectivity in the state, with plans to introduce heli-taxi services connecting Shimla with Hamirpur, Chamba and Palampur, besides expanding existing flight operations from the state capital. As part of the proposed expansion, the government is exploring new air routes from Jubbarhatti Airport and the Sanjauli Heliport in Shimla. The proposed heli-taxi services are expected to provide faster connectivity to several districts, particularly those located in remote and geographically challenging areas. The Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation has also initiated the process to expand flight services on the Delhi–Shimla and Shimla–Dharamshala routes. In this regard, the state government has submitted proposals to the Union Ministry of Civil Aviation and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), seeking approval for the proposed operations. The services are expected to be introduced under the revised Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (UDAN) scheme, aimed at improving regional air connectivity and making air travel more accessible. The proposed heli-taxi connectivity to Hamirpur, Chamba and Palampur is expected to benefit local residents by reducing travel time, particularly for emergency requirements, official work and other essential journeys. It is also likely to provide a boost to tourism by making destinations more accessible to visitors. Similarly, the expansion of flight operations between Delhi and Shimla, as well as Shimla and Dharamshala, would offer additional travel options to tourists and residents while reducing dependence on lengthy road journeys.

headline: Rise above politics, join BJP’s Samrasta Sankalp Yatra: RS MP to Himachal CM, Cong
content: Shimla, Nov 23 (PTI) Hitting back at Congress for its criticism of the BJP’s Samrasta Sankalp Yatra, Rajya Sabha MP Sikander Kumar on Monday invited Himachal Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and other party leaders to participate, asking them to rise above party politics and join the initiative “dedicated to social harmony”. The Himachal MP’s response came after Congress questioned the BJP’s objective in holding the yatra, claiming it was being conducted to drive political mileage ahead of the Assembly elections across many states. Seven Indian states are scheduled to hold Assembly elections in 2027. They are Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, and Himachal Pradesh Dedicated to the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas, the 16-day Samrasta Sankalp Yatra was flagged off on November 18 from Jalandhar, Punjab, by BJP National President Nitin Nabin to promote social harmony, equality, and brotherhood. It will cover five states and two Union Territories across northern India. “If the Congress genuinely believes in social equality and brotherhood, it should participate constructively instead of questioning the purpose of the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra,” Kumar said while welcoming the yatra in Parwanoo in Solan district. Issuing an open invitation to Congress leaders, Kumar said, “We openly invite every Congress leader to participate in the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra.”

headline: Natural farming push fails to bring profits for growers
content: Growers are struggling to get remunerative prices for their produce due to inadequate promotion of natural farming products and 15 per cent commission being charged by the marketing platform of Dr YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni in Solan district.The university’s ‘UHF Naturals Store’, which became operational on July 18, lacks key facilities such as refrigeration, essential for enhancing the shelf life of perishable products like fruits.Jiwan Singh Rana, a progressive farmer of Gharjarot village in Kangra district, who sold his dragon fruit through the store, rues that he had supplied 150 kg of A-grade dragon fruit to the university store on August 1 and another 150 kg on August 31.He says that the produce was sold only weeks later, resulting in a considerable quantity of the fruit getting spoiled. “After investing thousands of rupees on transporting my produce from Kangra district and paying 15 per cent commission to the university store, I did not make profit,” he adds.Growers lament that in the absence of adequate promotion of natural farming products by both state government and university, consumers remain largely unaware of the nutritional benefits of such produce. Consequently, farmers struggle to find sufficient buyers, defeating the very purpose of promoting natural farming as a remunerative livelihood activity in the state.“Natural farming products have a high nutritional value as their production does not involve chemical pesticides or synthetic fertilisers. This farming practice relies on naturally available local resources and also helps rejuvenate soil health while promoting digestive health,” opine health experts.The absence of accredited laboratories to certify their produce as naturally farmed is adding to the woes of the growers. This makes it difficult for farmers to establish the authenticity of their products, further limiting their ability to secure remunerative prices in the market.An official of the university, however, justifies the 15 per cent commission, stating that it is necessary to meet the recurring operational expenses of the store, including the salaries of two employees, rent and electricity charges.He adds, “The UHF Naturals is an outcome of the Himachal Pradesh Government’s Prakritik Kheti Khushhal Kisan Yojana (PK3Y), aimed at promoting natural farming and developing sustainable agricultural systems. The UHF Naturals provides marketing and retail space to Natural Farming Farmer Producer Companies from across Himachal Pradesh, enabling them to showcase and sell their produce. It also offers university departments an opportunity to market their raw and value-added products while extending support to university-based start-ups.”

headline: New Industrial Act Approved: Mandatory 80% local employment in HP industries
content: The 'Public Safety and Convenience (Third Amendment) Bill, 2026', aimed at ensuring the safety and convenience of road users and pedestrians in Shimla, was introduced by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu in the HouseShimla/Dharamshala (HP), Industries operating in Himachal Pradesh will now have to allocate 80 per cent of their jobs to the state's residents under the newly approved industrial legislation.On Saturday, the government introduced the 'Himachal Pradesh Investment Promotion and Simplification Bill, 2026', to establish a formal legal framework and ensure the right to employment for local people.Industries Minister Harshwardhan Chauhan presented the bill in the Legislative Assembly, where it was subsequently passed.Furthermore, investors looking to set up industries in the state will receive necessary clearances through a 'Single Window System.'The Industries Minister said industrialists will now be legally bound to comply with the government's terms and conditions. Under the provisions of this Act, it will be ensured that 80 per cent of the workforce in these industries consists of 'Himachalis'.During the discussion on the Bill, BJP MLA Bikram Singh Thakur questioned the necessity of a new Act, pointing out that an industrial policy was already formulated in 2019 and that a Single Window System for industrial clearances was already in place. He also raised questions regarding the government's underlying intentions.In response, Harshwardhan Chauhan said that every state has its own industrial legislation. This Act has been introduced in Himachal Pradesh to bring industries within a legal framework and ensure adherence to government conditions.He said that a similar Act was drafted in 2018, but the previous administration failed to implement it. The current government has introduced this Bill with the state's interests in mind, providing legal protection for the employment of local residents.The 'Public Safety and Convenience (Third Amendment) Bill, 2026', aimed at ensuring the safety and convenience of road users and pedestrians in Shimla, was introduced by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu in the House.Under its provisions, residents living near 'sealed' roads will be eligible to obtain three-year permits for their vehicles. The House passed the Bill without any discussion.The Industries Minister introduced the 'Himachal Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Bill, 2026' and the 'Himachal Pradesh 'Jan Vishwas' (Trust-based Governance) Provisions (Amendment) Bill, 2026' in the House. Both Bills were approved without any discussion.In the absence of Public Works Minister Vikramaditya Singh, Ayush Minister Yadvinder Goma introduced the 'Himachal Pradesh Municipalities (Amendment) Bill, 2026' and the 'Himachal Pradesh Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026'. These two Bills were also passed by the House without any discussion or opposition.

headline: Himachal: Unrest brews among Baddi villagers over govts plan to acquire land for township
content: SHIMLA, Nov 22: Farmers of about 14 panchayats in Solan district's Baddi area on Sunday threatened to stage protests and pursue a legal battle against Himachal government's plan to acquire land in the region for a township, demanding cancellation of HIMUDA's notification issued in this regard."We do not want a 'mini-Chandigarh' in Baddi," said villagers, whose land is reportedly under the scope of the project.They said the region needs roads, hospitals, schools, healthcare facilities, and employment opportunities, not a form of development that forces people to be displaced from their ancestral lands and homes.The proposed township, Him-Chandigarh, will be located at Shitalpur in the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh industrial belt of Solan district, about 30 km from Chandigarh. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, in January, had claimed that three panchayats were willing to give land for the project.On October 23, Himachal Pradesh Urban Development Authority (HIMUDA) issued a notification last month, stating that the government proposes to acquire over 8,000 bighas of land including private land.Against the proposed township, farmers from the affected villages held a meeting and declared that they would not surrender their ancestral and private land for the project under any circumstances and would submit memorandums to the Governor and the Chief Minister on November 28 and 30.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu had on November 17 informed the house that the government has not sold any land in Chandigarh. Instead, 8,000 bighas of land have been transferred to the Housing Department.During the meeting, the farmers also raised concerns regarding the conduct of administrative officials. They allege that officials failed to accurately present the ground reality and the objections raised by the local population to the government.Those present at the meeting included former MLA Paramjit Singh, Hansraj Chandel, Bhag Singh Kundlas, Krishan Kaushal, Chintram, Sanjeev Thakur, Charandas, Vidhi Chand Rana, Zila Parishad member Raj Kumar, and BDC Vice-Chairman Ashok Kumar, along with other local residents.Instead of clarifying the position regarding the acquisition of private land, the notification included private plots which fuelled fears among villagers that their land is being forcibly seized, Struggle Committee president Bhag Singh said. The Struggle Committee has been formed to raise affected villagers' concerns in the matter.The farmers expressed concern that the government is being misled by inaccurate or incomplete reports, preventing the genuine grievances of the local people from reaching the administration.The farmers said that during an earlier meeting held at the religious gaushala (cow shelter) in Shitalpur, local MLA Ram Kumar Chaudhary, speaking on behalf of the government, had given assurances that private land would not be acquired and that only government-owned land would be utilised for the project.The inclusion of private land in the notification has left people feeling cheated. If there was no intention to acquire thousands of bighas of private land, then why was it included in the notification, a local, Chintan Chaudhary, said.The farmers warned that if their demands are ignored, women will also join the agitation, and they are prepared to take action ranging from staging protests and sit-ins to pursuing a legal battle.It was decided during the meeting that a memorandum would be submitted to the Governor on November 28 and to Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on November 30, demanding the cancellation of the notification and the exclusion of private land from the project.It was also resolved to keep the movement apolitical, bringing farmers from all political affiliations onto a single platform. The farmers stated unequivocally that any attempt to compromise the rights of local people or tamper with their land in the name of development would not be tolerated. (PTI)

headline: Conference at Palampur in Himachal stresses sustainable use of bio-resources
content: A two-day national conference on “Himalayan Bio-resources: Use, Conservation and Livelihood” concluded at the CSIR-Institute of Himalayan Bio-resource Technology (IHBT), Palampur, on Saturday, with scientists and experts calling for the sustainable use of natural resources, conservation of biodiversity and creation of livelihood opportunities for Himalayan communities.The conference, held on November 20 and 21, brought together scientists, researchers, academicians and students to deliberate on climate change, environmental degradation and the potential of Himalayan bio-resources to promote sustainable development. Chief Guest Dr Rajeev Bhardwaj, Member of Parliament from Kangra, appreciated CSIR-IHBT’s contribution to environmental conservation and livelihood generation.Welcoming the delegates, CSIR-IHBT Director Dr Sudesh Kumar Yadav highlighted the institute’s efforts to link scientific research with societal needs. He referred to initiatives such as the Aroma Mission, the Golden Revolution associated with wild marigold and nutrition-related programmes, which have helped create livelihood opportunities through the sustainable use of bio-resources.Dr Narmada Prasad Shukla emphasised the role of science and technology in addressing climate challenges and encouraged young people to participate in environmental protection. Delivering the presidential address and keynote lecture, Dr Shiv Kumar Sharma explained the geological formation of the Himalayas and highlighted their ecological sensitivity. The conference featured technical sessions on biodiversity conservation, biodiversity-based livelihoods, natural disasters, nature-based solutions and ecosystem responses to environmental changes. Researchers presented studies on medicinal plants, aromatic crops, wild edible mushrooms, biotechnology, food innovation, beneficial microorganisms and climate-resilient agriculture.The inaugural session also witnessed the release of the conference abstract book, technology transfer activities and the signing of memoranda of understanding (MoUs). An exhibition showcased Himalayan bio-resources and scientific technologies developed for societal applications.Awards were presented to winners of outstanding oral and poster presentations during the concluding session. Dr Yadav called for stronger research collaboration to address societal needs, while Dr Shukla urged young researchers to combine scientific excellence with environmental responsibility.The conference reaffirmed CSIR-IHBT’s commitment to conserving Himalayan biodiversity and promoting sustainable livelihood opportunities for communities in the region.

headline: Ex-minister Kaul Singh Thakur hints at contesting 2027 Himachal Assembly polls
content: Senior Congress leader and former minister Kaul Singh Thakur (81) has indicated his willingness to contest the 2027 Himachal Pradesh Assembly elections from the Darang constituency in Mandi district, saying that he would abide by the decision of the Congress high command.The issue gained political significance during his birthday celebrations at Bijani Rest House in Mandi on Monday, where Congress workers and supporters from Darang assembled in large numbers and expressed their support for his continued leadership.On the occasion, Congress workers from the Darang Assembly constituency passed a resolution urging Kaul Singh Thakur to contest the 2027 Assembly elections from the constituency. The resolution reflected the workers' demand that the veteran leader should once again represent Darang in the state Assembly.Addressing the gathering, Thakur said that he had not personally wished to contest another election and believed that capable young leaders were also available in the constituency. However, he made it clear that he had always respected the party's decisions and would abide by whatever the Congress high command decided regarding his candidature."I have never disobeyed the party high command. Whatever decision the Congress leadership takes, I will accept it," he said, adding that people from his constituency had been urging him not to retire from active politics.Recalling his political journey, Thakur said that the people of his constituency had elected him to the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly eight times, giving him opportunities to serve in various capacities, including as a minister, Speaker of the Assembly and state Congress president.He also thanked party workers for organising the birthday celebrations and honouring him with warmth and affection. He assured the gathering that he would continue serving the people as long as he had the strength and remained alive.Thakur criticised the Central Government for discontinuing the Revenue Deficit Grant to Himachal Pradesh. He also praised the functioning of the state government under the leadership of Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.The gathering was attended by District Congress president Champa Thakur, former Chief Parliamentary Secretary Sohan Lal Thakur, district- and block-level Congress office-bearers, elected representatives and party workers.The resolution passed by Darang Congress workers has added a new political dimension to the constituency's preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections, making Thakur's political future an important subject of discussion within the party.
